body._comment: body (since build 314): parts of her body kept as running numbers, beat by beat, instead of decided by one roll (the dice still decide how hard each blow and each struggle is). Each part is its own switch; enabled false here turns them all off. Shown on her card (hover for what they mean) and told to the story. AIR (0 to 100, her breath): each beat she loses per_energy for every point of energy she spent, choke (x how tight the grip is, more the more worn she is: health_drain) while a grip is on her throat, coils x how far coils have squeezed her chest in, and winded while she is breathless, coughing water, throat-struck or panicking; breathing freely she gets regen back (x spent_regen after a hard beat; less inside coils, and x0.4 winded). Below low she hits softer (down to power_min at none), dodges slower (dodge_min) and gets her energy back slower (regen_min); under short she is SHORT OF AIR, under starved STARVED OF AIR. chokes: a choke puts her out by the air really left in her (from out_from down she can go under, up to out_max a beat), in place of its fixed count of beats: she starts the choke with whatever breath the fight has left her. (since build 316) BLOOD CHOKES: a grip closing on the sides of her neck (legs, arms or coils round it, hands or jaws round it) cuts off the blood to her head: that gauge drops blood_choke a beat (x how tight, more the more worn she is) while she can still breathe a little, and comes back blood_back a beat once it is off; she goes under by whichever of the two runs out first. pin_choke (since build 317): a grip on her neck that is part of a pin drains her at this share of a choke's rate (a pin holds her down more than it chokes her; held long, it still can put her out). A blood choke is the usual kind now: a grip whose words don't say it presses across the front of her throat counts as one (blood_default; false = such a grip is an air choke, as before). LIMBS (0 to 100, how tired each one is: arms, legs, jaws, head, tail, wings): every blow thrown with a limb adds strike (more for a heavier move), every beat she holds a grip with it adds grip (coils go by holds.coil.energy instead), and a limb she doesn't use recovers rest a beat (less when her energy is low). From `from` it tells: her blows with it weaker (down to power_min), a grip held with it easier to break (up to x1 + grip_break), tired legs make her dodge worse (up to dodge_legs); from tired the story is told (her ARMS HEAVY...). Both are fighter.learned.body, saved and undone with her.
body._blood_comment: blood (since build 318, on by default): the blood she has lost, 0-100 (100 = none lost). A bite or a claw opens the part it hurts to bleed (per_damage x the damage it did, at most part_max a beat per part); each wound clots x clot a beat (x held_clot while a grip is on it); bleeding little, she makes back regen a beat. Never below floor: it is never a death. Under low her blows and dodges weaken (down to power_min / dodge_min at the floor), her heart quickens (heart) and her blood pressure falls; under pale she is PALE, under faint LIGHT-HEADED; bleeding fast (bleeding a beat or more) she is BLEEDING, and the story may show the blood. The card draws blood running from a bleeding wound.
body._adrenaline_comment: adrenaline (since build 318, on by default): how much is running in her, 0-100. It rises with the health a beat costs her (per_loss for every % of her full health), with being held or pinned (held), and with her health low (under low_health %, low_rate for every % under it), and ebbs x decay a beat. It dulls the pain (her resistance to a tap x 1 + pain x its share), adds a little to her blows (power) and quickens her heart (heart); from high she is KEYED UP. When it falls from crash_from or more to under crash_below, the CRASH: crash_beats beats of her strength coming back slower (crash_regen) and her blows a little weaker. The one-time adrenaline surge at her last strength (adrenaline) is still its own thing, and sets it to 100 while it lasts.
body._tissue_comment: tissue (since build 318, on by default): swelling in her hurt parts. A blow sets how far a part will swell (per_damage x the damage x by kind: blunt most, a grip, a bite, a claw, a burn, a shock, cold less); it swells toward that over the next beats (rise of the way a beat) and goes down slowly (x fade a beat). A swollen limb (from `from`) is stiff: its blows weaker (down to power_min), swollen legs dodge worse (dodge_legs); from swollen she is SWELLING and the story is told. On her card the bruises spread with the swelling and age: angry red-purple when fresh, purple, then dark with a yellowing edge.
body._bones_comment: bones (since build 318, on by default): bones that really break. In a fight, very rarely: a blow or a grip that takes a bone part past during_from damage breaks it during_chance of the time (blunt or crushing x blunt_mult, cuts x cut_mult), once a fight at most. At the end of her match she may be found with bones broken: each bone part past end_from damage, end_chance x how far past it over end_span (at most end_max), x coil_mult for her ribs or chest inside coils (a constrictor's match breaks ribs), x trapped_mult for a limb held in a grip; at most max_end. A broken limb hits at power_mult, a broken leg dodges x dodge_legs; the story is told, plainly and without gore. Never her spine, back, neck or skull, and nothing is permanent: it heals. enabled false = bones never break (the story may still say so on a part past narration.bone_break).
body._heart_comment: heart (since build 316, on by default): her heart rate as a running number, carried from beat to beat. Each beat it moves toward what her body asks of it: her resting rate (fighters.json heart_rest) x (1 + exert x how much energy she has spent + pain x how hurt she is + her statuses' share (fear, panic, a surge, short of air: cards.STATUS_SIGNS) + air x how much air she has lost), at most max x her resting rate; quickly when it has to rise (rise of the way a beat), slowly as it settles (settle), with a little natural unevenness (wobble). So a hard exchange leaves it racing for beats after, and a rest brings it down gradually. Under coils round her body it is the constriction's own heart. The heart monitor on her card shows it. false = worked out fresh each beat, as before.
body._mind_comment: mind (since build 321, on by default): her state of mind as two running numbers, which drive the mind reactions (moves.reactions: shaken, panicking, emboldened) rather than adding rival ones. COMPOSURE (0-100, 100 calm): each beat the health it cost her takes per_loss for every % of her full health, being held or pinned held, a grip on her throat or coils round her with her air going air_fear x the share of air gone, being knocked down down; landing her own blows gives back per_dealt for every % of her opponent's health. All of it over her toughness, and damped as the fight goes on (x 1 / (1 + beat / damp_at)), so a long fight never grinds her nerve to nothing. Every beat it settles back toward calm (settle of the way) and it never goes under floor: always temporary. EDGE (-100 to 100): who the fight is going for, from the beat's health dealt and taken (edge_gain a %), fading x edge_decay a beat. What they do, all small: under unnerved she is UNNERVED (blows x power_min, dodging x dodge_min); low composure makes shaken and panicking likelier (up to x1 + react) and a smaller blow enough to shake her, and she gives in to a hold a little sooner (her resistance down to x1 - tap); a good edge makes emboldened likelier (up to x1 + bold). It colours the fight, it never decides it.
body._heat_comment: heat (since build 320, on by default): her core temperature, as degrees from her normal (normal, shown on her card). Each beat fighting hard heats her (per_energy for every point of energy she spent); fire that hits her heats her (burn x the damage) and ice cools her (cold x the damage), at most hit_max a beat; her own type takes x own_type of it (a Fire type shrugs off heat, an Ice type cold). The sun heats her (sun), rain and hail cool her, standing in water cools her (water; a Water type x0.3), and bodies pressed together in a hold warm a little (held). She sheds it back toward normal by cool of the way a beat (x cool_spent after a hard beat). Past warm she is FLUSHED, past hot HEAT-EXHAUSTED: her energy comes back slower (down to regen_min at hot), her breath too (air_min), her blows and dodges a touch weaker (power_min, dodge_min), her heart quicker (heart a degree). Under chill she is SHIVERING, under cold_at NUMBED: her blows and dodges weaker. Kept within min..max: never a danger to her life. In an ordinary fight she only rarely gets flushed; a fight full of fire does it. (since build 322) tap_min: past warm she gives in to a hold a little sooner, down to this at hot; the arena's weather heats or cools her too (arena_weather).
body._footing_comment: footing (since build 319, on by default): how steady she is on her feet, 0-100. A blow knocks it down by the damage it does x per_damage, x by where it landed (regions: her legs and head most; region_other for the rest), x by what it was (kinds: blunt and blasts most), x by her build (plans: four legs or a serpent's coils hold steadier), over her toughness; being knocked staggering costs stagger more, a blow turned aside off_balance. It comes back regen a beat (slower with her energy low and her legs tired, swollen or broken), but no higher than faint_top while she is light-headed or starved of air, dazed_top while dazed, concussed or confused, slick_top on slick ground; getting up she starts at getup at most. Under low her blows lose some weight (down to power_min at none) and her dodging slows (dodge_min); with footing gone a blow staggers her up to x1 + stumble more often, a knockdown blow keeps her up x1 - keep_feet as often, and she slips on slick ground up to x1 + slip more. Under unsteady she is UNSTEADY and the story is told. Only on her feet: down, pinned or in the air it doesn't count.

arena_weather._comment: arena_weather (since build 322, on by default): the weather over the whole fight (a move's weather, Rain Dance, Sunny Day or Hail, still takes over while it lasts). kind: scene (the default: the arena's own weather from scenes.json, none for most arenas), random (one picked for the fight from random), clear, or a kind by name; an indoor arena (scenes.json indoors) never has any. Each kind: word and say (how the story is told it), type_mult (moves of that type stronger or weaker), heat (degrees a beat on her body heat: body.heat), cool_mult (how fast she sheds heat in it), slick (the ground slick: more slips, less footing), soaks (everyone soaked: Electric hits harder), fighters (how it sits with her own type: power on her blows, regen on her energy coming back, heat on what it does to her temperature; wet_ok = not while she stands in water or is soaked: a Water type wilts in the heat, unless she is in the water). storm: lightning (a bolt strikes a fighter strike a beat, x air_mult up in the air, at power; stunned stun of the time, knocked down down (always out of the air); a Ground type is untouched, an Electric type takes x absorb; near: a bolt close by, both flinch, fear off their composure) and gusts (chance a beat: footing knocked off those standing, buffet = the chance a flyer is BUFFETED for a beat, dodging slower). wind: gusts as above, more often. COILS (in any weather): the coils round her heat her, coil_heat a coil round her body (x coil_limb round a limb), x the kind's coil_mult (summer heat: x3), so a long constriction in the heat can overheat her. enabled false = no arena weather.

Water.say: in her element in the rain

Water.say: in her element in the rain

Fire.say: doused and steaming in the rain

Water.say: wilting in the heat, out of the water

window._comment: The fighter pictures in the window (python window.py) and in exported fights. back_view: a second picture of her from behind, with her back, lower back and tails on it (back_regions; click a label, then either picture, to move a part); back_size its size. The back picture: images/<name>_back.png or <species>_back.png if you have one, else the PokeAPI back sprite (back_download), else her outline. weak_look: she looks as worn as she is: your own images/<name>_worn.png (under worn_below % health), _hurt (under hurt_below), _down (on the ground or pinned), _out (and _back_worn and so on for the back), else her picture faded, slumped or tipped over. damage_marks (the Damage marks switch in the window): each hurt part from marks_from % damage on shows the marks of what hurt it, worse as the damage climbs: claw slashes, bite punctures, bruises, scorch, lightning burns, frost, grip marks; glow: the damage colour round each hurt part (half as strong while the marks are on); status_look: frozen, chilled, soaked, paralyzed, poisoned and burned tint her and show on her. poses (the Poses switch): your own picture for how she is placed, if you have one: images/<name>_pinned, _pinning, _faceup, _facedown, _side, _sitting, _air (or <species>_...; each falls back to the next nearest, then to _down), else (pose_fallback) her picture is posed by the program: on her back, flat on her front, on her side, sitting, braced on top, up in the air, on the ground with a shadow. Click a label and then the picture to place her parts on a pose picture of your own. pain_gauge (since build 249): two PAIN gauges under each fighter's energy bar, each a share of how much she can bear (100% = all she can bear; her resistance from finish.submission.tap: resist, resist_power, surge_resist). They decide nothing. OVERALL: the pain she feels now: each beat the sting of the blows and grips on her (sting times the damage they did to her parts) is added, and what she felt before fades (decay of it is left each beat), over a low floor her injuries keep up (chronic times her worst part plus second_part of the next two). PART: the part being held, pinned or struck this beat: in a submission (in a submission match) the tap check's own pain, which comes only from the gripped parts, with a choke's air hunger beside it; held otherwise, the gripped part's damage and the grip's pressure (press); struck, that part's damage and the blow's sting. labels: [below this share, the word shown]. show_max (since build 258): a share above it is shown as that and a plus (300%+), with far past what she can bear: once she is worn to nothing what she can bear sinks to its floor and the share runs into the thousands, which says nothing more; 0 = the share as it is. enabled false = no gauges.
window._card_zoom_comment: card_zoom (since build 273): the size of the fighter cards in the window, so both fit on one screen: the Cards − and Cards + buttons above them change it by 10% (40% to 160%) and it is kept for next time. At 100% the cards are drawn as before (click a label, then the picture, to place a part); at any other size each card's pictures and labels are drawn as the exported fight draws them and made smaller or bigger, and the bars under it are as wide as it (placing a point by clicking goes back to full size for that card). The story's own size is A− and A+ above it.
window._hold_panel_comment: hold_panel (since build 257): more of the fight on each fighter's card, in the window and in exported fights. A TAP METER (a submission match, while she is held): five steps filled to how near she is to tapping, the same ladder the narrator tells it by (1 holding easily, 2 getting to her, 3 close to her limit, 4 very close, 5 at the edge; a choke near her limit reads fighting the dark), this beat's tap chance (0% on a beat she can't tap: her first beat in it, the first beat past her limit she holds on through, or holding out at her breaking point), the pain against what she can bear, and why (refusals so far, the breaking point's stage, air gone in a choke). A HOLD PANEL: who holds which of her parts, in what hold and with what, for how many beats (a grip on her throat said so); the grips she has on others; a pin's count against its length; and how far she is from each other fighter (distance: narration.match_state). Her parts in a grip get a violet ring on her picture. meter_by (since build 283): what the meter's five steps and its words follow. chance (the default): this beat's real chance of a tap, one step past each of chance_steps (%): any chance at all = 1 (a tap is far off), 3%+ = 2, 10%+ = 3, 25%+ = 4 (close to tapping), 50%+ = 5 (at the edge); 0 = no chance yet. The pain against what she can bear is on the line under it, and when the pain is near or past it while the chance is small, the line says so and what keeps the chance down (the hold's build-up, still on her feet, stubborn, an adrenaline surge). Before, the steps followed how the pain felt, so the meter read 'at the edge of tapping' at 0% (Ripples on her feet in Seraphina's upright coil on its third beat). pain = the steps follow how it feels to her, the narrator's ladder above. enabled false = none of it.
window._vitals_animate_comment: vitals_animate (since build 293): the constriction strip's heart trace runs like a monitor's, at her own heart rate, in the window and in exported fights. It is a line redrawn a few times a second (no graphics-card memory). false = a still trace.
window._squeeze_figure_comment: squeeze_figure (since build 299, on by default): while coils squeeze her in a constriction, her card (and an exported fight) shows the squeeze as a picture of its own under the heart monitor: her torso from the front in her own colours (taken from her picture), the coiler's loops wound round it in the coiler's colours and as thick as the coiler is big against her (a Milotic's loops cover most of a Buizel's chest; only the coils on her are drawn), pressing her in harder as the squeeze builds, her ribs showing once it is crushing, her body paling as her blood is cut off; and beside it her heart, beating at her rate (vitals_animate), flattened between the coils when they are round her chest, smaller as less blood gets back to fill it, and still once it stops. false = the plain squeeze bar instead.
window._hold_picture_comment: hold_picture (since build 304, on by default): while a hold, a submission, a grab or a pin is on her, her card (and an exported fight) shows it as a picture beside its gauges: her body from the front (drawn by the program, so it reads whatever way her artwork faces), each part in a grip outlined in the holder's colours, and what the grip does drawn on it: a joint lock bends the limb past where it should go (further the nearer her pain is to what she can bear) with an arrow round the joint, a choke presses in at her neck, a crush squeezes her body from both sides, a head hold clamps her head, coils wind round a limb, a grab leaves grip marks, a pin bears down on her. Beside it each grip, a gauge (her pain against what she can bear, her air for a choke, a pin's count) and this beat's tap chance. Coils round her body have the squeeze picture instead. false = no hold picture.
window._alive_comment: alive (since build 306, on by default): the fighter cards in the window come alive, from her own artwork (nothing drawn over it). breathing: her picture rises and falls at her breathing rate (breath_rest a minute at rest, faster as she tires or hurts; fast and shallow in a constriction, a choke, or guarding hurt ribs; slow and faint once she is out); breath_depth is how far, as a share of her height. breath_min_px (since build 325): the least her picture rises at the top of a breath, in pixels, so a fast, shallow breath (ribs guarded, coils round her) still shows. pulse: the glow on her hurt parts throbs with each beat of her heart (from throb_from % pain on; throb how much brighter at the top of a beat). impact: when the window moves on a beat (or you step forward one), every part that was hit flashes and her picture jolts (jolt_px pixels for the hardest blows, over jolt_seconds). grey_in: as a choke or the coils near her black-out, her picture loses its colour and a dark edge closes in round it (from grey_from of the way to her limit on; vignette how dark the edge gets); exported fights show it too, still. grip_outline: the rings on her gripped parts are in the holder's own colours and pulse. heart_monitor: a heart monitor on every card under her bars: her heart rate and a trace moving at it, her blood pressure and her breathing, each with its normal beside it, and what is doing it (winded, spent, the pain she is in, her statuses, guarding her ribs, no air getting in). Her heart rises from her resting rate (fighters.json heart_rest, else heart_rest) with exertion (exert x how tired she is) and pain (pain x her pain against what she can bear), her statuses (adrenaline up; asleep, frozen, chilled down; paralyzed uneven), up to heart_max x her resting rate. While coils squeeze her, the constriction's own monitor and squeeze picture take its place. Rough numbers for the picture, never rolled against. fps: how many times a second the cards are redrawn. enabled false = none of it.
window._live_zoom_comment: live_zoom (since build 315, on by default): at another card size (Cards - / +) the card is drawn as at full size and then scaled, its pictures made at that size, so they still breathe and throb and sit on the window's own background (dark mode included). false = a still picture of the card, as before (it was white behind her in dark mode, and nothing moved).
window._live_ecg_comment: live_ecg (since build 315, on by default): the heart traces on her card run like a real monitor instead of one pattern repeating: each beat is laid down as its time comes, at her rate then. A healthy heart's gaps vary a little and each beat is a touch taller or shorter; an irregular one's gaps are uneven, now and then a beat is skipped, now and then one comes early, wide and odd-shaped with a pause after it; a stopped one is a flat line with a faint wander. A new rate shows from the next beat on. The beating heart beside the squeeze and the throb of her hurts follow the same beats. false = the old looping trace.
window._explain_comment: explain (since build 312, on by default): hover over her status line to see what each status on her is and what it does to the numbers (her blows 15% weaker, her dodging 40% worse, beats left), read from the rules in force; hover over a heart rate, a blood pressure, her breathing, the blood flow cut off or the squeeze to see what the number means, what is normal and what is pushing hers there. Nothing new is drawn on the card. /explain in the console gives the same, for everyone or one fighter (/explain Ripples) or one status (/explain dazed). The strip under the coils also lays its lines out by their real height now, so they no longer run into each other at a high display scaling. false = no hover tips.
window._limb_report_comment: limb_report (since build 324, on by default): hover over a part's label or its dot on her picture (or type /limb Ripples left foreleg) for that part in detail: its damage and resistance and what its wounds have cost her in health, what did it and when, how it looks now, what it is doing (throbbing with her heartbeat, swelling, bleeding, singed, frost-numbed, numb, tired from use, wet), the grips on it, and what it does to the rest of her: her blows and dodging with that limb, her pain, her blood and breath, her nerve, and the statuses it has given her, with their numbers. Read from the fight; it decides nothing. enabled false = the plain damage and resistance tip.
window._replay_button_comment: replay_button (since build 324): a Replay hits button over the cards: the blows of the beat shown flash and jolt on the cards again (alive.impact must be on). false = no button.
window._match_badge_comment: match_badge (since build 324): a line over the cards (and at the top of the console's stat block) saying what kind of fight this is (knockout only, submission, pins and knockouts...), how it ends, the arena and the weather. The Effects button turns it off and on. false = none.
window._sounds_comment: sounds (since build 329, on by default): the fighters' own sounds, played in the window as each beat lands, and carried in an exported fight: gasp (a light hit), grunt (a solid one), cry (a heavy one), scream (a devastating hit or a part ruined), strain (fighting a hold), whimper (held near her limit), choke (coils squeezing her in hard, or a choke), breath_back (her heart starting again), pant (spent or short of air: every breath_every beats at most, breathing false = never). No impact sounds. The files are yours: .wav (or .mp3) in sounds/<kind>/, any number, one picked at random; her own voice in sounds/<her name>/<kind>/ or sounds/<species>/<kind>/ comes first. A kind with no files is silent; panting and the breath back come with starter recordings (made by sim/make_breath_sounds.py; replace them freely). max_per_beat: sounds per fighter per beat. export: an exported fight carries the sounds it uses (up to export_max_mb), playing as you scroll to each beat once you turn them on at its top. /audio in the game, or the Effects button. enabled false = silence. (since build 330) Each fighter has one voice: her sounds in a beat play one after another, never on top of each other, and a long file plays to its end. overlap: what happens when a new beat's sound comes while she is still making the last one: voice (default) = the new one cuts the old one off, except a minor sound (strain, pant) no bigger than the one playing, which is skipped; queue = it waits its turn (at most queue_max waiting); mix = all at once (the old way). max_seconds: cut any sound after this long (0 = whole files). A beat's sounds play once, when it lands: going back to it is silent, and the Replay sounds button over the cards (or the speaker button on a beat in an exported fight) plays them again; Replay hits is silent now. /audio overlap voice|queue|mix, /audio max N, /audio stop. (since build 331) sounds/ is yours alone: git ignores it, so pulling an update never adds to, changes or deletes your files. The starter panting and breath-back recordings moved to sound_starters/; starters: they are used for a kind with none of your own files (false = that kind is silent). On Windows every file is opened by the DirectShow player first (the old wave player can't open many downloaded .wav files: 24-bit, 32-bit float), and a file nothing plays is written to errors.log. /audio test plays one file of each kind now and says what went wrong with any that won't play.
window._hold_picture_switch_comment: hold_picture can also be turned off and on from the Effects button (Hold picture), or /effects holdpic off.
window._dark_comment: dark (since build 258): the window (python window.py) in dark colours: dark backgrounds, light text, and the blues, reds and violets that mark things a shade lighter so they still stand out; the damage fill, the bars and the tap steps keep their colours. It is read when the window opens. enabled false = the light window.

text._comment: The story pane on the right of the window (since build 237). numbers: the stat lines are shown (the Numbers switch above the pane hides them, leaving the story). pointers: short notes under the numbers saying where they come from, with the numbers in them: occasional (each kind once, then again only after pointer_gap beats), always, or off (the Pointers switch). hover: resting the mouse on a dotted term in the numbers (the dice roll, scale, vital, pain against her resistance, exertion...) shows what it is and which setting it comes from. unwrap: in the window the stat lines are not broken at 100 characters as on the console; the pane wraps them itself, with the rest indented under the start. font_size: the story text size (the A- and A+ buttons change it for this session). progress: the narrator's [writing part 1/2] lines are shown (the Progress switch).

save._comment: save (since build 301): what a save file keeps beyond the fight itself (every save, the autosave too). history (on by default): the /undo history, the newest history_beats beats of it, so a loaded fight can be undone back through them as before it was saved (each beat about 40 KB in the file). The story, the window's beat history and every fighter's numbers after each beat are always kept (the window rebuilds its story and beat slider from them when a fight is loaded or a beat undone). What a beat's narration was written from is not kept, so /reroll works only on beats written after loading. false = a loaded fight can't be undone past the point it was loaded.

export._comment: auto: a finished fight is saved by itself to the exports folder, beat by beat with every fighter's picture, health and each body part's damage and resistance (an .html page and a .json file), and saved again after each aftermath beat. /exportfight does it any time. gauges (since build 252): beside each fighter, the window's tap tally (a submission match) and its two pain gauges (overall, and the part held or struck), as they stood after that beat; false = left out. Beats saved before build 249 have no pain gauge.

finish._comment: knockout_only (off unless you turn it on: /set finish.knockout_only true): a fight ends ONLY when someone is knocked out by a blow; a pin held to the end can't finish her (she kicks out at the last second, spent), and the director can't just declare someone out. The knockout chance starts below start_pct of her full health and rises to chance (for a decent blow, decent_loss_pct of her full health at once) at full_pct and below; a bigger blow raises it (up to 1.6x), a glancing one lowers it; below zero it climbs a little more (below_zero_per_50); devastating blows x devastating_mult; adrenaline halves it; never above max. no_pins (only with knockout_only on; off unless you turn it on: /set finish.no_pins true): no pins at all, so no pin openings and a submission held long stays a submission instead of becoming a pin. Off, fights end the usual ways: pins held to the end, and the rare knockout of moves.knockout.

submission._comment: A submission match (off unless you turn it on: /set finish.submission.enabled true): only a TAP-OUT or a PASS-OUT ends a fight; no blow knocks anyone out. A tap-out is resisted while she can. Each beat after the pressure lands, a fighter held two beats or more in a submission, a choke, a coil or any other hold that hurts (not a pin, and a grab only as tap.grabs says) weighs THE PAIN SHE MUST RESIST (the gripped part's damage, plus tap.second_part of the other gripped parts' damage, plus tap.per_beat for every beat it has been on after the first) against HER RESISTANCE (tap.resist x her overall strength as a share of full, to the power tap.resist_power; x tap.surge_resist on an adrenaline surge). Only pain past her resistance can make her tap, and never on the first beat it gets there (that beat she holds on through it): after that the chance is how far past it, over tap.span, never above tap.max. Within tap.near of her limit she is shown fighting the urge. A choke (a grip on the neck or throat) also builds air hunger, choke.air_per_beat a beat, against her endurance (choke.endurance x the same strength share): past it she may pass out (how far past, over choke.span; never above choke.max). no_pins (on by default): no pins at all in a submission match, and a submission held long stays a submission instead of becoming a pin; false = pins come as usual, and a pin held to its end still puts her out (she passes out under it). Keep finish.knockout_only off with it.
submission._allow_knockouts_comment: allow_knockouts (since build 282, off by default): in a submission match a knockout blow ends the fight too, as in any other fight (the /preset anything match: a knockout, a pin held to its end when no_pins is off, or a tap-out). false = only a tap-out or a pass-out ends it.
submission._tap_awake_comment: tap_awake (on by default): a fighter who TAPS OUT leaves the match awake and down (the recovery stage before back on her feet), not out cold; false = she starts the aftermath out cold like a knockout. A pass-out always starts out cold.
submission._tap_comment: tap.span: how far past her resistance the pain must go for the chance to reach 100% (before any ceiling): 80 past it with span 160 is 50%. tap.press: the grip itself adds pain, press times how hard it is pressing right now (that pressure climbs with its own tightening and holds.build), on top of the damage the part already carries. tap.climb: the chance never goes above a ceiling that starts at climb.start on the first beat she can tap and rises climb.per_beat every beat the hold stays on, up to tap.max; the ceiling is then lowered by her strength left (x (1 - climb.health_hold x her health share)): fresh she rarely gives in, worn she can. climb.enabled false keeps only tap.max. tap.grabs (since build 239): a GRAB (jaws or paws simply holding on) can make her tap too, once the part it is clamped on is hurt past grabs.min_damage (%), or she has no health left; before, a grab never could, and a match could run on with her far below zero in jaws she would never tap to. grabs.enabled false = grabs never count. tap.spent_no_grace (since build 239): with her health at zero or below, there is no beat of holding on through it first: the first beat past her limit can already be a tap. tap.overwhelm (since build 254): THE BREAKING POINT. Once a gripped part is in horrible condition (part_damage %: 300 = devastated) and the pain is past her resistance, the tap is coming, but not at once: she holds out a few beats first and cannot tap at all. How many comes from her: hold_min to hold_max, longer the more of her strength is left (an adrenaline surge counts), with a little luck in it. Each of those beats the story is told how far her resistance has broken down (the first of it, cracking, the last of it), so the pain, the struggle, the tells and the refusals show it giving way before the tap; nobody in the story knows how long she will last, and every beat after that her chance is at least `chance` (0.95: near certain). The count carries on while the same fighter holds her, even through a regrip. Before, the slow climb of the ceiling capped even this: in the build-253 lakeside fight Ripples refused at 26-50% a beat with a ruined hip in the grip and never tapped. enabled false = the climb caps it as before. tap.urge (since build 256): before she is near her limit (below tap.near), she is still shown fighting the urge to tap. In a SUBMISSION (urge.submissions) that is every beat it is on, from the first; in any other hold that hurts, from urge.from of her resistance, urge.chance of the beats. Each beat the narrator gets one sign of it (a fist squeezed tight, a paw that lifts and is yanked back to her side) and how hard to tell it, on one ladder from 1 to 5 that runs on into the refusals near her limit: 1-2 here (under half her resistance felt and held easily, then getting to her), 3-5 as she refuses near and past her limit (the paw shaking harder, rising and being yanked back as if telling it no, the thoughts breaking down), the nearer the tap the more visceral, with what she looks like and what she thinks. It is not a refusal and does not bring the tap nearer. enabled false = nothing is shown below tap.near. tap.blend (since build 264, on by default): THE TAP CHANCE comes from BOTH how hurt the gripped part is and how hurt she is overall, with a build-up. P = the gripped part's damage (plus second_part of the others) over part_full (300 = devastated), at most 1, to the power part_power (a lightly hurt part counts for little); H = her health gone (0 fresh, 1 at zero or below). The chance is part x P + health x H + both x P x H, never above max: fresh with a ruined part in the grip 30% a beat (she can fight it, but not for ever), worn out with a healthy part 8% (harder than fresh, still resistible), worn out with a ruined part 85%, fresh with a healthy part next to nothing. An adrenaline surge multiplies it by surge. THE BUILD-UP: on the hold's first beat she never taps, and after that the chance is multiplied by (beats past the first / ramp_beats) to the power ramp_power, so with 8 and 2 it is 2% of it on the second beat, 6% on the third, 14% on the fourth, 25% on the fifth, 39% on the sixth, 56% on the seventh, 77% on the eighth and all of it from the ninth. The dice still decide every beat, so anything can happen (a tap within two beats is possible, only rare), but a submission usually lasts 6 to 10 beats or more, and nearly always the struggle is shown first. From near (of the chance before the build-up) she is shown refusing it, as near her limit. blend.chokes (on by default): a choke's pass-out chance builds up the same way (before, a hurt fighter could black out on a choke's second beat). The upright rule still damps it while she is on her feet. With blend on, tap.span, tap.max, tap.climb, tap.overwhelm and the beat of holding on through it are not used; enabled false = they decide it as before. blend.past_limit (since build 309, on by default): the build-up runs faster the further past what she can bear the pain is: the beats count x (1 + per x the pain past her resistance over her resistance), at most x max. Pain twice her resistance (per 0.05) runs it x1.05; pain far past it, a crushed foot in the grip with almost nothing left, up to x1.35 (larger values shortened 3-tap matches by a sixth or more in testing) (the Seraphina vs Ripples log: pain 956 against a resistance of 42 was still 1% on the third beat). Not for coils round her body: those go by the constriction. enabled false = as before.

tap._falter_comment: tap.falter (since build 333, on by default): HOW FAR HER RESISTANCE HAS FALLEN shows by how near the tap really is. Each beat she refuses near her limit, the sign of it comes from the set for how near she is by THIS beat's tap chance: under closer_at the first signs (a twitch, claws curling, a swallowed word), from closer_at the nearer ones (her paw hovering over the ground, clenched and shoved against her own body, yanked back to her side), from edge_at the edge (the paw flat on the ground shaking, tears, saying no aloud). After refusals_step refusals, refusal_push of the time it shows one step nearer than the chance alone (worn down by refusing). The story is also told in a word how much of her resistance is left (holding, wavering, faltering, almost gone: almost_gone_at). Before, the step came mostly from how often she had refused, so on her second refusal she was often at the edge with a 1% chance. enabled false = the old way.
tap._paws_comment: tap.paws (since build 333, on by default): the signs follow which of her paws are free. A grip on a forelimb (her shoulder, an arm, a paw: the hold itself or any other on her) takes that paw: the story is told the other one is the free one; with both held, no sign needs a paw (her tail, her voice, her face, her body instead) and a tap is given as with her arms trapped in coils. enabled false = only coils round her body count.
tap._claws_comment: tap.claws (since build 333, on by default, like pin.control's claws): every grip in the hold that is claws or talons dug into her (said in the grip's words) makes it hurt more: pain x pain_mult and the tap chance x chance_mult for each, counting at most max_grips. The story is told where they are in. enabled false = claws count like any grip.
tap._meter_all_comment: tap.meter_all (since build 274, on by default): any hold that hurts (a squeeze, a crushing headlock, a coil, a held bite), not only a named submission, counts toward a tap, and the window's tap meter now shows it from that hold's first beat (she can't tap yet; no struggle is told for it that beat). A grab that doesn't count yet says on the hold panel how hurt the part must be first (tap.grabs.min_damage). false = the meter waits for the hold's second beat, as before.

submission._endure_min_comment: choke.endure_min (since build 265): her endurance under a choke never drops below this, however hurt she is (before, a fighter at zero health had none at all: the choke read 'air 2200% gone' on its first beat). The tap meter's 'air gone' is now how far she is toward blacking out for sure (her endurance plus choke.span), never shown past 99% while she is awake.
submission._constriction_comment: constriction (since build 283, on by default; a submission match): coils round her CHEST, BELLY or BACK (a coil's body grip: holds.coil) put her out the way a real constrictor does, by her blood more than her breath: the squeeze stops blood getting back to her heart, her blood pressure falls, her heart (racing at first with fear and effort) slows and stumbles, and her head runs short of blood until she blacks out. (Her breaths do grow shallow, the coils taking up the slack each time she breathes out, but it is the circulation that takes her.) A gauge builds like a choke's air: per_beat each beat the coils have been on, x (1 + extra_coil for each body coil past the first), x how hard the hardest presses against power_ref (between x0.5 and x2), x how much bigger the coiler is than her ((her length over the other's, holds.coil.size.sizes) to the power size_weight, kept between size_min and size_max), against her endurance: endurance x her health share to the power health_power x tap.surge_resist on a surge x (1 - part_weight x how hurt the worst coiled part is, up to devastated) x (1 - energy_weight + energy_weight x her energy share: spent from struggling, she goes sooner), never below endure_min. What sets it apart from a submission (pain against her will) and a pin (a clock): it goes mostly by the squeeze and her breath and energy left, and her health and the coiled parts count for less (health_power 0.5 against a submission's 0.8; part_weight). Past it she may black out: how far past, over span, never above max (the gauge builds from nothing, so there is no tap.blend build-up on top of it). Measured (Seraphina's upright coil on Ripples, no breaking free, 20 fights each): fresh about 10 beats (a plain submission, 10), at half health about 8, at half health and energy 40 about 7, a quarter and energy 30 about 6, most ending in a blackout. From near of her endurance the grey closing in can make her tap from panic as well: up to grey_tap more chance, growing as it closes in. The story is told it stage by stage, on the same curve as the numbers below (her heart pounding, to vitals.peak_at of the way to blacking out; then slowing and stumbling, her head swimming, pins and needles; from stage_grey of the way, slow and uneven, the grey closing in), the blackout as the blood, not a choke, and her blood coming back when the coils come off; the window's tap meter shows the blood flow cut off, and its chance is now of the hold ENDING this beat (a tap or blacking out, either one, for a choke too), with each beside it. heart_stop (since build 293): when she blacks out in the coils, chance of the time her heart, already slow and stumbling, stops altogether for a moment as she goes under: the monitor goes flat, the story tells it, and then, as the coils come off, it starts again on its own (a thud, another, ragged, a shuddering breath). tap_mult (since build 309): coils round her body make her TAP this much as often as anything else would (0.35): she blacks out in them far more often than she gives in, and her heart stopping as she goes under (heart_stop.chance, 0.6 since build 309; was 0.35) is likelier than a tap. 1 = taps as in any hold. It is never a death: it always starts again, and the blackout ends the match (or, in a several-tap match, counts as one) as any blackout does. enabled false = her heart never stops. Coils on her neck are a choke instead; on a limb they bind it. A pin with coils in it already ends in the constriction. enabled false = body coils only hurt, as before.
submission._constriction_vitals_comment: constriction.vitals (since build 283): rough numbers for her heart and blood pressure on the screen while the constriction is on (the stat lines and the tap meter; never in the prose, and never rolled against). As in constricted prey: fear and effort drive both UP at first, to peak_mult of her resting heart rate and bp_rise of her resting blood pressure by peak_at of the way to blacking out; then, with the blood unable to get back to her heart, her blood pressure falls toward bp_low of resting and her heart SLOWS toward low_mult of resting, beats skipping (irregular) once it has begun to slow. heart_rest: her resting beats a minute (fighters.json heart_rest for one fighter: a small fighter's heart runs faster); bp_rest: her resting blood pressure. enabled false = no numbers.

constriction._heart_comment: heart (since build 313, on by default): her heart under the coils is its own number, worn down beat by beat, instead of a roll when she blacks out, and it is what nearly always puts her out. Her heart's RESERVE runs from 1 (fresh) to 0 (it stops). Each beat the coils take: base x how far what they press with (the mmHg on her card) is past press_floor of her resting blood pressure x (0.5 + 0.5 x how far she is squeezed in) x where they are (her chest worst, her belly least; where_mult adds to it) x (1 + extra_coil for each coil past the first) x (1 + per_beat for each beat held, at most dur_max), divided by how hardy her heart is (her health and energy left; a surge x1.2), with a wobble of +-wobble (the dice, so the same squeeze never plays out quite the same). Her heart RATE follows it: racing at first (from start_mult up to vitals.peak_mult of her resting rate while the reserve is above slow_at), then slowing toward stop_mult of it as the reserve runs out, uneven below irregular_at; there, sudden of the time each beat (more, the lower it is) it gives out early. At 0 it stops, and she blacks out at once. The blood gauge can still black her out first, only gauge_out_mult as often (0.1); then her heart stops as she goes under only if it is already under going_under (the monitor says so beforehand). after_hold: once her heart has stopped, the coils stay on her from beats_min to beats_max more beats (rolled), as a constrictor waits for the heartbeat under her coils to go quiet: she is limp and knows nothing of it, nobody else touches her, and it does her no more harm; then the coils come off and her heart starts again on its own, at restart_reserve. In the match's final black-out it is told, not played. Coils off, her reserve comes back regain a beat (a re-coil soon after finds her heart part of the way down still). Never a death. enabled false = the black-out comes from the blood gauge and heart_stop.chance decides the heart, as before.

heart._min_beats_comment: min_beats (since build 328): the coils must have been on her at least this many beats before her heart can stop, by running down or by giving out early; until then its reserve stays at min_reserve or above (slow and uneven, but beating). 0 = no minimum.
heart._strain_comment: strain (since build 327, on by default): once her heart has stopped in the coils it is strained for the rest of the fight (only the fight: nothing carries over): each later squeeze wears its reserve down per_stop faster for every time it has stopped, never more than max times as fast, so a second or third stop comes a little sooner. enabled false = every squeeze starts it fresh but for restart_reserve.

constriction._weight_comment: weight (since build 327, on by default): a serpent far bigger than her (at least min_ratio of her length, holds.coil.size.sizes: a Milotic on a Buizel, an Arbok on a Vulpix) can crush her without wrapping her: the serpent's weight submission, a heavy length of her body laid across her back or chest and her middle, pinning her flat. It works like the constriction, her breath pressed out and then her blood held back, her heart racing, slowing, and maybe stopping; only slower: at mult of the pressure coils would put on, never squeezing her in past max_squeeze %, and the gauge toward blacking out builds at slower of the rate. It can end in a tap-out or a blackout like coils. It lasts as long as she has breath for it (holds.coil.energy), at energy_mult of what squeezing costs. Breaking out from under it is escape_mult as likely as from another hold (nothing to push up against), less still the flatter she is pressed. The director is offered it share of the time when it fits (coiling the rest), only on the ground. enabled false = no weight crush.
constriction._recovery_comment: recovery (since build 309, on by default; with compression on): coils let go and wound round her body again within beats beats find her not yet recovered from the last ones. What they did to her blood (the constriction gauge) is kept x keep for every beat since, and how far her chest was squeezed in x keep_squeeze (it springs back faster): so her heart starts the new squeeze still raised (racing as the blood came back, not slow and not below her resting rate), and slows and greys sooner than the first time. enabled false = every new coil starts from nothing, as before.
constriction._compression_comment: compression (since build 294, on by default): how far the coils have squeezed her chest and middle in (0-100%), kept from beat to beat while the same coils hold, and what drives the constriction. Each beat the coils gain on her: gain x how hard they press (against power_ref) x how much bigger the coiler is (size_weight) x (1 + extra_coil for each body coil past the first), divided by how well she braces against it (brace_base + brace_res x the resistance of the parts they are on, x her strength left); and each breath out they take up the room she gave up (ratchet), more when she struggles (struggle_ratchet: fighting it spends breath, and the coils take it), never above max. The constriction gauge then builds per_beat a beat x how far she is squeezed in: nothing below floor %, all of it at floor + span %, up to over x past that; x where_mult by where the coils are: her chest (straight on her heart and lungs), her belly (her gut driven up under her ribs: the breath pushed out from below, a little less on the heart), both, or her back. It also makes the coils harder to break (escape_mult x the compression off her chance), and the breath she loses (constricted energy loss x0.5 to x1.5). The story is told how far in she is and where, and the strip shows the squeeze. Measured with these numbers (Seraphina's upright coil on Ripples, no breaking free, 20 fights each): fresh about 9.5 beats, half health about 7.5, half health and energy 40 about 7, a quarter and energy 30 about 6 (as before compression); the squeeze closes in over about six beats. enabled false = the gauge builds by the beats held, as before.

compression._ring_comment: ring (since build 296, on by default): a coil round her body goes all the way round her, so it touches every part of that band, not only the part it was put on: round her chest, her chest (and ruff), her ribs on both sides and her upper back; round her middle, her belly, both flanks and her lower back. She braces with the resistance of the whole band, the worst-hurt part of it counts against her endurance, a coil on her back or flank counts as round her chest or her middle, the narrator is told it presses on her front, sides and back alike, and the squeeze bar draws the coils on all four sides of her. false = only the parts the coils were put on count, and a coil on her back is its own place (where_mult.back).
compression._ring_wear_comment: ring_wear (since build 297, with ring on): the coil wears the whole band it goes round, not just the part it was put on: this share of its pressure each beat is spread evenly over the rest of the band (her flanks, her ribs, her back...), the rest stays on the part it was put on. 0 = all of it on that one part, as before; 1 = all of it spread round her.

vitals._pressure_comment: pressure and girth (since build 300, both on by default): how tight the squeeze is in real-world numbers, shown on her card beside the squeeze picture (rough, like the rest of the vitals, never rolled against). pressure: what the coils press on her with, in mmHg so it reads against her blood pressure: base_mmhg at a full squeeze from a coiler her own size, x (the coiler's size / hers) ** size_exp (holds.coil.size.sizes), never past max_mmhg, scaled by how far she is squeezed in. Once it is past her blood pressure, blood can't get back to her heart. girth: round her chest or middle, before and now, in cm: per_m cm for every metre of her size, less up to max_loss of it at a full squeeze.

submission._choke_share_comment: choke_share (since build 234): when a submission opening is offered (to the director, and in /simulate), how often the hold it offers is a CHOKE (a sleeper, a triangle, head scissors: its main grip on the neck) when a lock on a limb or the body also fits, so a submission match ends in a choke only now and then. The director is also told chokes are the rare finish, and once one has been tried in a match, to go for a limb or the body. 1 = no preference.
submission._hold_mix_comment: hold_mix (since build 265, on by default): fewer chokes and jaw holds in a submission match. They still happen, only less often than the usual locks on a limb, the back or the body. When the director puts on a CHOKE (a named one, one of her own, or a hold on the neck), it stands hold_mix.choke of the time (0.35), and once a choke has been tried in the match only after_first of that again (0.5: 0.175). When it puts on a JAW HOLD (a bite clamped on and held), it stands hold_mix.jaws of the time (0.5). Otherwise the engine puts on a lock that fits instead, one with no jaws in it when one fits (the beat is told with the lock's own words). A choke or a bite with nothing else that fits stands. A grip added to a hold she already has on her is left alone, and so is every order of yours. The submission openings offered also pick a jaw hold only jaws as often as another, and the bite and choke ideas (director.throat_bite_chance) come hints as often (0.35). 1 = no change for that kind; enabled false = off.
submission._taps_comment: taps (since build 238; off unless you turn it on: /set finish.submission.taps.enabled true): the match needs MORE THAN ONE tap-out. taps.needed: how many tap-outs end it (3 = the third tap wins; a tap before that makes the holder let go, and the fight goes on, her limit and her refusals starting again for the next hold). taps.different_parts: the percentage of those taps that must come from a body part no earlier tap used (the worst-hurt gripped part is the one a tap counts for). It is rounded up to a number of different parts, never fewer than one: with 3 taps, 0-33 = any parts, 34-66 = at least two different parts (one repeat allowed), 67-100 = all three different. Once only as many repeats are left as the rule allows, a grip on a used-up part can't make her tap at all (she doesn't roll), so the fight has to go somewhere new. taps.pass_out_counts (on by default): a pass-out in a choke counts as one of the taps (she blacks out a moment and comes round as the grip comes off); false = a pass-out ends the match outright. taps.steer: how hard the fight is pushed toward a part that still counts. Each fighter has a TARGET PART (the worst-hurt part that still counts, a limb first; it sticks from beat to beat so the damage builds there, and is picked again after each tap). The director is told the tally, the used-up parts and the target. A blow aimed at a used-up part always moves onto the target, and any other blow moves there steer.strikes of the time. A hold on a used-up part moves onto the target, and any other hold moves there steer.holds of the time (submission openings offered favour holds that grip it). steer.enabled false = only the tally and the rule, no pushing. steer.ready (since build 240): once the target part is hurt past ready (%), it is READY: more blows there are wasted on it, so blows move off it onto the NEXT part (the worst-hurt one that will still count after it: steer.strikes of the time from the target, half that from elsewhere) while holds still go to the target, and the director is told to hold it now and soften the next one. Only while more than one tap is still needed; 0 = blows stay on the target to the end. taps.respite (since build 240): after a tap that isn't the last, the holder lets go (always) and steps back: for respite.beats beats nobody strikes or grips the one who tapped (whatever the director had them do to her becomes a step back), so she gets at least one clear try at getting up before the next hold (she also rolls to rise the beat she taps, once the grip is off). Your own commands still go through. enabled false = the fight goes straight on. Since build 277, serpent_different_parts: the same percentage for a serpent (a Milotic, an Arbok), who has no limbs to put in a hold, used when it is lower (50 = with 3 taps, two different parts are enough; null = serpents go by different_parts like everyone).
submission._long_ramp_comment: long_ramp (since build 247): a submission match that runs long wears its fighters down faster: past `after` beats, the damage blows and grips do to body PARTS (not health) is multiplied by 1 + per_10 for every 10 beats past it, never above max (with these numbers x1.15 at beat 50, x1.6 at beat 80, x2.5 from beat 140). Pain builds sooner, so the taps come sooner. only: 'taps' (only a match needing more than one tap, the default) or 'submission' (every submission match). The stat lines show it ('x1.60 for a long match'). enabled false = off.

taps._serpent_coils_always_comment: serpent_coils_always (since build 327, on by default): a serpent (a Milotic, an Arbok) fights with her coils, so coils round a body can always put her out, as an exception to different_parts: the blackout counts for a part of the band they go round that is still free if there is one, else for the worst-hurt part of it again. false = once every part of the band is used up, those coils cannot finish it.

finish._styles_comment: styles: how often each way of going out comes up (before the dice weigh what happened): instant (lights out on impact: likelier from a slam into the scenery, a charge, a spike, a devastating blow), scream (a raw cry cut off as she goes: likelier from a big blow), crumple (knees fold, one try to stay up, then out: likelier while she is still standing), fade (going under slowly from inside: likelier when she is already down or held, or the last blow was light). They apply to every knockout, knockout-only fights or not.

models._comment: Which Ollama models write the story and pick what happens. null = the default (mistral-small:24b, or --model). /model narrator <name> and /model director <name> change these.

_comment: All tuning lives here. Values marked GUESS are placeholders until you confirm your real rules.

body_templates._comment: Starting resistance (%) per body part. Fighters pick a template in fighters.json and can override any part. Resistance can go above 100%.

profile._comment: profile (since build 335): what a blow does to a part, split between its RESISTANCE (how worn down it is) and its DAMAGE (how injured it is). By the kind of blow: damage x the part damage it does, wear x the resistance it wears off, worn_bonus: + this much more damage on a part whose resistance is worn all the way down (in proportion). A heavy blunt blow pounds a part soft more than it injures it; claws, blades and teeth injure more than they wear, and tear deeper into a part already worn; a beam or a blast is in between. Her health is NOT changed by it: only the part's two numbers. A move can set its own in fighters.json ("profile": {"damage": x, "wear": y}). The story is told what kind of blow it was. false = every blow the same, as before.

moves._comment: Named moves live in fighters.json. Effective power = move power x type effectiveness x targeting. targeted = one body part (x2); spread = several parts (x1.25 each); whole_body = every body part (x1); hold = pressure on parts every beat until released.
moves._head_reach_comment: head_reach (since build 261): a head butt (or a skull bash, a head slam) thrown by a fighter on her feet at one on her feet lands where a head can reach: her head, neck, chest, shoulders, belly, back or arms. Aimed at her legs, feet or tail it lands on her chest instead (the build-260 log: a head butt to Ripples' left foot). enabled false = it lands where aimed.
moves._low_launch_comment: low_launch (since build 261): a blow whose main hit is on her lower legs or feet takes her legs out from under her: thrown or launched becomes knocked down, where she stood, and no blow catches her up in the air after it. A move that launches by itself (moves.json) still does. enabled false = the director's launch stands.
moves._improvised_comment: Moves the director invents on the spot (a headbutt, a pounce, a throw). Their base power comes from how hard they land; type and targeting then apply like any move.
moves._conjure_comment: conjure: a fighter may make a weapon of her own element (an ice blade frozen out of the water, a whip of water) and keep it beats beats: while she is ARMED her improvised blows land as its type, x power_mult. Only from a type she has (her own types or her moves' types, not Normal or Fighting). enabled false turns it off.
moves._plain_body_comment: plain_body (since build 252): an improvised move named for a plain use of the body (a head twist, a knee strike, an elbow, a wrench) with no word of her element in its name or the director's words for it (water, a jet, a splash, flame, frost, a spark...) lands as Normal even when the director typed it with her own element: before, a Head Twist typed Water hit as Water, soaked her and went into her mouth. A conjured weapon still sets its type. false = the director's type stands.
moves._same_move_comment: max_same_move_in_a_row: the director can't make a fighter use the same named move more than this many times in a row (0 = no limit). Your /commands aren't limited.
moves._sustain_comment: Sustained moves: a move marked "sustainable" (streams and beams like Hydro Pump, Flamethrower, Ice Beam) can be held for up to max_pulses pulses. Each extra pulse hits the same parts at pulse_mult power and costs energy_per_pulse. If the target is pressed against something, each pulse also slams her into it, and it may break (break_chance by surface): a heavy extra hit, the move ends early, and she goes down.
moves._grind_comment: grind: blows landed while she is held or pressed against something in the arena (a pummel against a tree, "pinned_against" on an ordinary strike) each drive her back into it too: power is the severity of that extra hit on her back, break_mult scales the thing's chance to break (from sustain.break_chance) for each blow.

grind._comment: Blows on a fighter held or driven against the scenery: each also drives what is behind the part it hit into it (her upper back behind her chest, lower back behind her belly, the back of her head behind her face); a blow on a limb grinds the limb itself in limb_chance of the time (limb_chance_down lying on the ground, where a limb is nearly always against it), and the shoulder or hip it hangs from limb_root_chance; when what is driven in is the struck part itself (the arm, the back of the neck), it takes self_mult of the surface's power (the same for moves.ground_back on the ground). power from severity.environment.

aim._comment: Where a blow aimed at one part really lands. The smaller or harder to reach a part is, the likelier a blow aimed at it lands on a part beside it instead (bigger and easier ones likelier): the torso is easiest, then the back, shoulders and thighs, the forelimbs, the head, the tail and lower limbs, and the neck hardest of all, tucked under the jaw. 'small' makes a named part harder still within its region (an eye, an ear, the throat). regions: chance (0-1) a blow lands where aimed, by body region. Easier on a fighter who is down or pinned (down_mult), held (held_mult), or open (staggered, dazed, doubled over, off balance, flinched, frozen, asleep, paralyzed: open_mult); harder for an attacker who is dazed, off balance or confused (shaky_mult). These multiply the chance to MISS; scale multiplies it once more (0 = every blow lands where aimed). Where it lands instead: a part beside it, the bigger and easier the likelier; one harder to reach than the part it missed only x harder_mult. A path of parts (a rake from cheek to hip) is not aimed as a whole, but each small, hard-to-reach part on it (aim ease at or below path_below: an eye, an ear, the throat) is rolled like an aim and lands beside itself if it misses; a pummel's run of blows and a whole-body move are never re-aimed.

ground_back._comment: A blow driven down into a fighter lying on the ground (face-up, face-down or on her side; not sitting up) drives her into the ground too: the parts she lies on take a light hit with each blow (power from severity.environment, x mult; x shallow_mult lying in shallow water; none in deep water). Blunt blows and blasts only, not rakes or bites. On top of moves.vulnerable.down.

sustain._crumple_comment: crumple (on by default, since build 235): a held stream that presses a fighter on her feet into the scenery leaves her pressed against it, and at the end of the beat she crumples to the ground or keeps her feet with the same roll as a charge crushing her there (moves.charge.crumple: the weaker she is, the likelier she goes down), shown on screen either way. false: she always slides down it.
sustain._ground_grind_comment: ground_grind (since build 336): a fighter who is down or pinned has nothing behind her but the ground she lies on, so a stream held on her with "pinned_against" the ground grinds her into it (each pulse presses what lies under her into it; the ground never breaks). false = with her down, a held stream only hits her again, as before.

moves._charge_comment: Charges: a move marked "charge" (Take Down, Aqua Jet, Dragon Rush...) or any improvised move can carry the target into something in the scene. The charge's own hit lands first; then her back hits the surface at slam_severity (from severity.environment) times the distance factor, on three parts; then the attacker's body crushes the parts the charge struck at crush_factor of the charge's power; it costs the attacker energy extra. The surface may break (break_chance by surface; empty = the same odds as sustained moves): a heavy extra hit and she goes down with it. Otherwise she is left pressed against it for the rest of the beat (follow-ups can't be dodged), and at the end of the beat she crumples to the ground with chance crumple.base + crumple.per_strength_lost x the share of strength she has lost (60% fresh, about 78% at half, 95% at nothing).

charge._reeling_comment: reeling_beats: after being driven into the scenery by a charge, a fighter can strike but cannot start or join a pin for this many beats (1 = only the very next beat; 0 = off). It comes only from a charge, never from damage or tiredness.

crumple._ways_comment: A fighter who crumples after a charge ends lying on her side, face-down, face-up, or SITTING with her back against what she was driven into; one who keeps her feet staggers clear, sags against it, drops to a knee and rises, or rebounds off it. The mix is under 'variety' (charge_falls, charge_stands).

charge._carry_on_comment: A charge that breaks what it drives her into may not stop there: carry_on_chance (scaled by the charger's strength and the distance, less for each obstacle already broken) that it goes on THROUGH into the next thing in the arena, at carry_on_power of the previous slam, costing carry_on_energy more. max_obstacles: how many things one charge can go into at most (0 = no limit but what the arena has).
charge._sheath_comment: A charge wrapped in its element (Aqua Jet, Wave Crash, Flame Wheel, Flare Blitz, Spark, Wild Charge, Volt Tackle...: "sheathed": true in moves.json, or the move's description says so) never leaves her between the hit and the slam: the water, fire or current stays on her the whole way back and keeps working on the struck part and the parts round it. power: each of those extra contacts as a share of the struck part's hit (times the distance); parts: how many parts round the struck one it reaches. power 0 = off.

moves._repeat_target_comment: Where the next blow of a pummel, or the next link of a chain, lands when nobody said: stay_chance that it goes to the same spot as the one before, otherwise somewhere new (near_share of those times right next to it, the rest anywhere she can be reached). Parts you name (in a /command, or in a direction the director follows) are kept as you said. stay_chance 1 = always the same spot.
moves._clash_comment: A CLASH: when a fighter fires a ranged move (a beam, blast, pulse or stream) at an opponent who is free to answer (on her feet, not held, pinned or stunned) and has a ranged move of her own and the breath for it, `chance` of the time she meets it head-on. The two powers, each with up to +/- `luck` in it, decide: one win_ratio or more stronger than the other and it wins; otherwise they CANCEL OUT. The attack pushing THROUGH lands at (1 - the weaker/the stronger) of its power, the defender's TURNING IT BACK hits the attacker the same way (between min_share and max_share). The defender spends the move's energy and a use. enabled false = off.
moves._into_mouth_comment: A Water stream (not a charge) that lands on her face, or on her while she lies face-up or pinned face-up, may go into her open mouth and up her nose: chance (x held_mult when the stream is held on her, x face_up_mult, x point_blank_mult; at most 0.9). She comes up SPUTTERING for `beats`: coughing it up, short of breath, no energy back, weaker escapes and dodges. Never drowning. enabled false = off.
moves._limb_limits_comment: A move thrown WITH a badly hurt limb lands weaker: a chop or a slash with a ruined paw or arm, a charge or a kick on a ruined leg, a bite with a ruined jaw, a horn strike with a ruined horn, a tail strike with a ruined tail. 'at': the damage % on the worst such part, and the power multiplier from there (150 = excruciating, 300 = devastated). Streams, beams and whole-body moves are not thrown with a limb. enabled false = off.

limb_limits._struck_limb: true: a blow thrown with ONE limb (a wing, an arm, a talon, a horn) counts the limb she throws it with: the one the order names ('her left wing'), or else her sounder one, since a fighter favours a hurt limb. A charge still counts the worst of them (all of them carry it). false = always the worst of the pair, as before.

moves._auto_spill_comment: A targeted strike that names only one body part also jars the parts right next to it (a jaw strike catches the muzzle and neck). parts = how many neighbors; factor = their power as a share of the move's base power. Set parts to 0 to turn it off.

auto_spill._comment: A single solid blow jars what's around it (half power by default). chance: how often it jars anything at all (a roll each blow); parts: at most this many neighbours, the dice pick 1 to parts.
auto_spill._carry_next_to_only: A strike the director names several parts for carries over only to parts that touch the main part (or one already on its path); a part across the body is dropped, not hit. false: every named part is hit.

moves._multi_hit_comment: Moves that hit several times in one go. The director may only repeat these (count > 1); other moves land once. Your own /move commands can still use a count.

guard._comment: Rare: the one attacked gets something in the way instead of dodging. block_chance (close single-target blows): caught on a forearm, foreleg, wing, horn or coils, landing there at block_share. deflect_chance (close) / deflect_ranged_chance (beams, blasts): turned aside, nothing lands, and a close attacker is OFF BALANCE for a beat. Both scale with how fresh she is; never while down, held, pinned or stunned.

missed_charge._comment: A charge that is dodged or turned aside may carry the charger into what's behind: chance (aimed_chance when the director named a target to drive into). She takes power_share of the charge's power on her front, and may go down (down_chance).

recoil._comment: Reckless moves hurt the user when they land: move name -> share of the move's power that comes back into her head, shoulders and chest (a move can also carry "recoil": share itself). enabled false turns it off.

vulnerable._comment: Caught open: a blow on someone who has no chance to roll with it, twist away or soften it lands harder. Only the biggest one applies. juggled: knocked up into the air by the last link of a chain; feinted: bit on a feint; down: lying on the ground (not pinned; close blows only); down_pummel: each blow of a pummel on someone lying on the ground (smaller, since every blow gets it). held: in someone's hold (not a pin), with nothing free to cover up.
vulnerable._pummel_comment: In a pummel every blow gets the bonus for being caught open (doubled over, off balance, staggering, dazed, flinching), so each gets pummel_share of it (x1.2 becomes x1.1 a blow).
vulnerable._moved_comment: staggered: knocked a step or more by a blow (moves.stumble) and still finding her feet, this beat and the next (no guard comes up either). rocked: the next blow in the SAME beat after one that turned her head or leaned her (not on a strong, fresh fighter); rigid: the same after lightning locked her.

feint._comment: A fake before the real blow (the director's "feint": true). Costs energy. chance the defender bites (higher when she is worn down; seen_mult per feint she has already seen from this attacker). If she bites, no dodge, clash or guard, and the blow lands at vulnerable.feinted.

last_stand._comment: Once a fight, a fighter below below_strength % may put everything into one blow (chance each attack): mult on its power, and her energy drops to 0 after it.

guarding_wound._comment: A fighter below below_strength % shields her worst part once it reaches at_damage %: blows there x covered_mult, blows on her other side x open_mult.

moves._side_spill_comment: side_spill (since build 278, on by default): a big blunt blow or a blast on her shoulder or upper arm that really moves her (staggers her, launches her, drives her back in a charge, or rocks her hard with min_damage x 1.5 or more) carries on into her side: the ribs on that side take power x power_mult, and the flank under them too flank_chance of the time (at 0.7 of that). Only blows of min_damage or more, only bodies with ribs or flanks; bites, claws and blades stop where they land. enabled false = off.

stumble._comment: A hard blow (min_damage part damage or more) on a fighter who is standing and free can knock her staggering: her head snaps round with a blow to the head, and she stumbles a step or more the way the blow was going (away from the side it hit; back from a front hit; forward from behind; sideways from a leg sweep). STAGGERED for a beat: dodging x status_effects.staggered_dodge_mult, the next blow lands x the caught-open bonus, her own blows x staggered_power_mult. Chance: base + per_damage per point over min_damage + weak x how worn she is, times kind_mult (blunt blows move her most) and region_mult, again_mult if she is still staggering, up to max.
stumble._rock_comment: Less than a stumble: a blow of rock_from damage or more that doesn't stagger her can still turn her head or lean her body with it (rock_chance), her feet staying put. How it looks only.
stumble._body_comment: Her body decides too: legs at bad_legs_at damage or more (sore_legs_at a little) can't brace, so staggers come easier (x bad_legs_mult / sore_legs_mult) and carry further; a blow on a spot already that hurt x hurt_spot_mult; under weak_below strength a stagger carries her further and lighter blows rock her more; over strong_above she catches it sooner and a middling blow moves her less.

jolts._comment: What a hard hit (min_damage part damage or more) can do for a beat: breathless (chest or belly left very painful or worse), dazed (head left excruciating or worse), doubled_over (a part that was already devastated). Chances per hit.

head._comment: head effects (since build 293, on by default; with it on, jolts.dazed is not used): the hardest blow to her head (min_damage part damage or more, at /scale 3: it goes up with the scale) rolls ONE of stunned, dazed or rattled. Each chance is chance.<name> x the blow's size (its damage over size x the damage scale, at most max_size: 60 at /scale 3 is a size of 1) x mult: blunt for a punch, a charge, a tail, a throw or a horn (sharp for a claw, a bite, talons, a beak; beam for a beam); held when her head or neck is in a grip and can't roll with it; / her toughness trait; adrenaline on a surge; concussed once she is. A stun is likelier on the jaw (jaw_stun: the jaw, chin, muzzle, beak) and the side of the head (side_stun: cheek, temple), and a second hard one while she is still dazed or rattled adds stun_when_dazed x the size. RATTLED: a blink and a head shake, a little slower to dodge. DAZED: her eyes won't focus, everything a beat late: far slower to dodge, more misses, weaker blows (status_effects dazed_*). STUNNED: the lights flicker: she loses her next action entirely (no attack, no grab, no dodge, no escape from a hold or a pin, no get-up), and after it her legs go (wobbly: worse at dodging and getting up, easier to bear down in a hold) and she is dazed a while. Then what that spot does besides (side.<name> x the size): the nose waters her eyes (eyes_watering: more misses), an ear or the side rings her ears (ears_ringing: a little slower to react), the jaw rattles her bite (jaw_rattled: her bites weaker), a dazing or a stun may double her sight (seeing_double: far more misses), a held head or a throw may give her whiplash (a stiff neck, slow to turn her head). beats: how long each lasts. concussion: once her worst head part reaches head_damage, or she has been dazed or stunned jolts times this fight, she is CONCUSSED for the rest of it: every later head effect comes easier (mult.concussed), getting up is harder, and the story carries the fog, the headache and the light hurting her eyes. enabled false = only jolts.dazed, as before.
head._concussion_comment: concussion.min_blows (since build 308): she is never concussed by one blow, however hard: it also takes at least min_blows separate blows to her head this fight (each one big enough to roll a head effect). 1 = as before.

body_jolts._comment: body effects (since build 293, on by default): what a hard blow (min_damage part damage or more at /scale 3, more at a higher scale) can leave on the rest of her for a few beats, each at most once at a time, its chance (chances) divided by her toughness trait, lasting beats: dead_leg (a hard blow to a thigh, a four-legged fighter's upper foreleg too: worse at dodging and getting up, easier to bear down in a hold), limping (a knee or foot left at 120% or worse: slower to dodge, her charges weaker), dead_arm (a shoulder or arm of a fighter who uses her arms: her punches and claws weaker), ribs_aching (her ribs or flank, hit hard or left at 120%: every breath catches; a little weaker and slower), back_spasm (her lower back: weaker blows, harder to get up), tail_numb (the base of her tail: her balance goes; slower to dodge), swollen_eye (her cheek or brow left at 150%: an eye swelling shut, more misses, for longer). What each does is in status_effects. enabled false = none of them.
