moves._reactions_comment: reactions (since build 308, on by default; reactions.py): what a body and a mind do with what is done to them, beyond the damage, kept short and small so fights run as long as before. body: what a hit leaves by what it was and where it landed: a NOSEBLEED (a blunt blow to the nose), BLOOD IN HER EYE (a cut on her brow or the side of her head: more misses), GRIT IN HER EYES (a Ground or Rock move, sand or dust, in her face: more misses), THROAT STRUCK (a blunt blow to her neck: coughing, a little weaker, less breath back), NAUSEOUS (blows to her gut adding up: weaker, less breath back), STINGING CUTS (cuts adding up), TWITCHING (after an Electric hit that didn't paralyze her: a little slower to dodge), OVERHEATED (Fire adding up: less breath back), NUMB WITH COLD (Ice adding up: weaker), a HEADACHE (Psychic adding up: slower to dodge), the STINGS SWELLING (Poison or Bug stings adding up). Those marked adding up need that much of it this fight first (the dose, at /scale 3), so one claw never leaves her bleeding all over. mind: SHAKEN by a big blow or a stun (a little weaker and slower) and the one who landed it EMBOLDENED (a little stronger); ANGRY after run blows in a row she couldn't answer (stronger, guarding less); FRUSTRATED after run misses in a row (wilder: more misses); PANICKING after held beats in a choke or coils round her body or throat (burns drain energy a beat). holds: what being held feels like, told once at each stage (from beat 1, 2 and 4 of it) by the kind of hold: coils round her body (each breath out the coils take up the slack; her face burning with blood that can't get down; her ribs creaking, a sick swimming feeling), coils round her throat, an air, a blood or a full choke, a joint lock, a bite, a bound limb, a plain grip. aftermath: what a hold kept on held beats or more leaves when it comes off: a HEAD RUSH (dizzy as the blood floods back: slower to dodge for a beat), PINS AND NEEDLES (a little weaker), a RAW THROAT (less breath back), a STRAINED JOINT (a little weaker), BITE WOUNDS, and WARY of the grip. At most max_body body and max_mind mind reactions on her at once, never the same one again within its beats + cooldown. chance_mult, size_mult and dose_mult scale all chances, the blow sizes and the doses; tune.<status> changes one (chance, beats, size, dose, run, held, power, dodge, aim, regen, drain), e.g. /set moves.reactions.tune.nosebleed.chance 0.2. effects false = told in the story only, nothing changes in the numbers. body, mind, holds, aftermath false = that kind off. enabled false = none, as before.

exhaustion_mistakes._comment: A fighter under below_energy energy or below_strength % sometimes overcommits (chance per attack): the blow lands at mult and she ends up off balance for a beat.

moves._knockout_comment: knockout: very rarely a beat knocks a fighter OUT with no pin: only when she ends it at max_health_pct % of her full health or lower, it cost her at least min_loss_pct %, and the damage came from a held stream, a pummel, a chain, a charge into the scenery, a spike or a catch in mid-air, a drop from a height, or a slam (or landed devastatingly). Chance base + per_loss_pct for each % past min_loss_pct + below_zero_per_10 for each 10 % below zero, x devastating_mult for a devastating blow, at most max.

knockout._sim_comment: sim (since build 317, on by default): a knockout goes by WHERE the blows landed, not only by how much they cost her. Blows to her head (jaw, muzzle, temple) and to her body (gut, flanks, ribs, chest: the liver, the solar plexus) each build a shock that fades between beats (x decay a beat); the knockout chance is x (1 + head x her head shock / ref + body x her body shock / ref, each counted up to twice), more again if her head is already rattled, dazed, stunned, wobbly or concussed (+0.25 each, up to x2) or her body is doubled over, winded, ribs aching or sick (+0.15 each, up to x1.6). A beat of blows only to her limbs, back or tail: x limb_mult. A clean hard shot (clean_head % of her full health on the head at once, clean_body % on the body) can knock her out on its own, without a pile-up. A head knockout is out cold; a body knockout folds her round it, unable to rise (told as such, and she more often crumples). The health gates (max_health_pct, min_loss_pct, and finish.start_pct in knockout-only fights) still apply, so it stays rare in a normal match. false = by the health and the kind of beat only, as before.

devastating._comment: Very rarely a blow lands DEVASTATINGLY: its power x a roll in mult, and health.soft_cap is much looser for that one hit (per_hit and per_beat x cap_mult, with room_mult x the room past them), so it can swing the fight. chance per landed attack (not pummels), x weak_point_mult on a part already devastated (300%+) or hurt_part_mult on one excruciating (150%+), x open_mult when she is caught open (moves.vulnerable); at most max_chance. ground_chance: a hard landing on a fighter with two or more badly hurt parts finds every sore spot at once (x ground_mult). The narrator is told why it was so severe.

severity._severity_comment: Used for hits that aren't named moves: improvised blows, environmental damage (landing on stone, slamming into a wall, being dragged).
severity._comment: The director picks a severity WORD; the engine turns it into attack power (rounded to a whole number).
severity._environment_comment: Power for each body part that hits the arena when a fighter is knocked down, thrown, or launched (a stalactite, a boulder, the stone floor). Every part on every surface takes one hit.

damage._comment: damage_scale multiplies every hit's damage (and so the health it costs). It does NOT change how fast resistance wears down (that's resistance_scale, below). 1 = the base numbers; the default is 3 (the one the balance is tuned for since build 146; it was 5 before, with faster wear: parts went from sore to ruined in two or three blows). Change it here or in the program with /scale.
damage._roll_comment: roll: every instance of damage (a move, each press of a pin or hold, a landing, an impact) is rolled within plus or minus this share of its number (0.17: a 30 lands as 25 to 35), so no two hits are quite alike. Severity words already vary by severity.variance on top. 0 = off.
damage._resistance_scale_comment: resistance_scale multiplies how fast resistance wears down (resistance lost = power x loss_per_power x resistance_scale). It does NOT change damage. 1 = normal; 2 = parts soften twice as fast; 0.5 = half as fast. Change it in the program with /resscale.
damage._part_curve_comment: part_curve: a body part's damage number counts every blow in full up to `knee` (300%: devastated); past it, it climbs ever more slowly (soften 150: about 630% after another 700% of blows, about 1,100% after 3,000%). Health, the size of the blow in the story, and everything else use the FULL blow, so fighters lose exactly as much health as before. enabled false = the old open-ended numbers.

resistance._comment: Damage % = power x the part's CURRENT resistance bracket mult x damage_scale. Then resistance drops by power x loss_per_power x resistance_scale. Health lost = damage x health.loss_per_damage_point x the bracket's health_mult, so hits on a worn-down part cost far more health. Brackets are checked top to bottom.
resistance._loss_per_damage_comment: loss_per_damage: resistance ALSO lost per 1% of damage the hit really did (times resistance_scale), on top of loss_per_power. 0 = off (the old rule: wear depends on the blow's power only). With it on, a part that takes a great deal of damage softens faster, so heavy hits change how the next ones land. /wear shows and changes it.

smooth._comment: A gradient instead of thresholds: a part's damage mult and health mult slide smoothly with its resistance, along straight lines between these anchor points [resistance, damage mult, health mult] (flat beyond the first and last). The anchors sit in the middle of each bracket, so the overall pace stays close to the brackets'; the brackets themselves still give the labels and icons. enabled false = the old thresholds.
smooth._points_comment: build 183: the low end flattened (a ruined part took x1.6 and a worn one x1.0; now x0.9 and x0.6), so a hurt part still takes several times what a fresh one does but no longer swallows nearly every later blow; health loss per damage point went up to keep fights the same length

resistance._max_loss_per_hit_comment: max_loss_per_hit: the most resistance (in points) one blow can take off a part, however devastating, the soft cap's extra wear included. 0 = no limit.
resistance._relative_comment: relative: a part's CONDITION is its resistance measured against how it started. A part starting at or above `sound` (85) is judged by its resistance as it is. One starting below it (a soft throat, a thin fin) counts as sound while untouched, so a gentle brush there is little; every point it loses is a bigger share of what it had, so it becomes sensitive fast (the damage and health curve, the icons and the narrator's 'toughness' all use the condition). vulnerability: such a part also takes (sound/start)^vulnerability more from every blow (start 63: x1.11; start 25: x1.53). enabled false = raw resistance. wear_exp: such a part loses resistance x(start/sound)^wear_exp per blow, so its condition falls only a little faster than a sound part's (1 = exactly as fast; 0 = raw points, which can take a very weak part from sound to ruined in one blow); max_loss_per_hit counts in condition too.

health._minimum_comment: null = health can drop below 0% with no floor. Set a number (like 0) to stop it there.
health._comment: Health lost per 1% of body-part damage (times the resistance bracket's health_mult), per beat from exhaustion, and per beat for badly hurt parts.

after_win_drain._comment: Once the fight is won, the badly hurt parts drag at the winner less and less: the pain drain is multiplied by each for every beat since the win (0.5: half, then a quarter...). enabled false keeps the full drain.

health._soft_cap_comment: A hit on a badly hurt part costs a lot of health (its low resistance makes sure of that), but nothing swings wildly. One HIT costs at most about per_hit of the fighter's own full health (0.05 = 5%), rolled up or down by jitter (0.15 = plus or minus 15%) and smaller for a light knock (power under power_ref scales it down, to no less than power_floor of it): past that the extra levels off, adding at most room x that cap more however big the raw number. Everything that lands on her in one BEAT is softened the same way past per_beat. A devastating blow gets far looser limits (moves.devastating cap_mult, room_mult). The stat block shows 'softened from' when it applies.

soft_cap._to_resistance_comment: to_resistance: the health the soft cap keeps from her is not simply lost: this many resistance points come off the hit part for every point of health softened away (0.1: a blow softened by 100 health wears the part 10 points more). 0 = off.

health._part_weights_comment: How much each body part matters to OVERALL health. Health lost from a hit (and the per-beat drain from a badly hurt part) is multiplied by the part's weight: 1 = as before; the throat, neck, chest and stomach count for more, limbs for less, ears, fins, horn and tail for much less. The part still hurts just as much and takes the same damage %; only what it costs her overall changes. A word in the part's name decides first (the longest that fits), then its region. /vital shows every part's weight; /vital ear 0.3 changes one; /vital off = every part counts the same (the old rule).
health._collapse_comment: collapse: below 0% health she fights on, but at the end of a beat, standing and free of holds and pins, her body may give out on its own: chance base + per_10_below for every 10% she is below zero, at most max (x adrenaline_mult during an adrenaline surge). She goes down and can get up again as usual. After a collapse it can't happen again for cooldown beats. stand_grace (since build 243): once she is back on her feet after a collapse, her body can't give out on its own again for stand_grace beats, so she is not left lying there most of the fight (blows can still knock her down at any time; 0 = off). repeat_mult (since build 243): each collapse she has already had this fight multiplies the chance of the next by this (0.6: the second is 60% as likely, the third 36%); 1 = no change. Build 243 also lowered base (0.08 to 0.05), per_10_below (0.03 to 0.02) and max (0.4 to 0.25).

story._comment: reasons: why the two wild fighters are fighting. One is picked from the file for each fight (fitting the arena); one fighter is the holder (there first, or holding what is wanted), the other the comer. The opening tells it, every beat carries a short note (thought_chance: now and then one thought either of them might have), interludes get it in full, and the aftermath gets its ending. Off by default: /reason on (or choosing one with /reason <n>) turns it on. Only for one-on-one fights. /reason to see, choose, write your own, or turn it off.

narration._repeat_across_comment: repeat_across (since build 313, on by default): a turn of phrase the story already used in the last `beats` beats (four words in a row with three that mean something, or five with three) is caught like one repeated within a beat, and rewritten or cut (the notes' own words for an injury may be said again). The within-beat check also counts five-word runs now ('her vision greying at the edges' three times in one beat got through). false = within a beat only.
narration._blow_feel_comment: blow_feel (since build 313, on by default): when every blow this beat was blunt (a head-butt, a tail, a body slam; nothing that bites, claws or cuts), a sentence telling it as a cut (a line of fire, a blade, a stroke drawn across her) is caught and rewritten: a blunt blow thuds, jars, aches and bruises. false = off.
narration._coil_room_comment: coil_room (since build 313, on by default): a fighter the coils have squeezed in `from` % or more has almost no room: a sentence that has her twisting round to look, spinning, arching her back, thrashing about or lunging is caught and rewritten to small movements (a twitch, a strain, her head turning a little). false = off.
narration._character_comment: character (since build 281, on by default): who each fighter is beyond her body, from fighters.json. personality: a few sentences on how she thinks and behaves, given to the narrator with her description and voice. history: her past, as far as the story may use it; a fighter with veteran true may remember past fights in a thought (the program otherwise cuts such memories), and nothing beyond what her history says. relationships: what each other fighter is to her (name -> a sentence), given only when the two of them are in the fight. moments: when one of her quirks decides something (stubbornness keeping her from tapping, a hold she has never met, an ambush, a huge blow dodged or landing, a blow that would stagger anyone else), the narrator is told so in one line, to show in what she does; the screen shows it with a star. The polishing model (Venice) gets the same character notes as a CHARACTER line unless narration.polish.character is false. Edit them on the Profiles window (the Profiles button) or in fighters.json.

story_checks._comment: Story checks added in build 267 for mistakes the model made in the build-264 saved fight although the notes had it right. Each one, when found, has that paragraph written again with the mistake named (or the sentence cut, like any other slip). getup_order: she gets up this beat, but the story tells a failed try AFTER the one that got her up (beat 10: Ripples stood, then 'her third attempt to rise was no more successful'). after_tap: the holder still pressing or striking her after the tap (beat 22: 'Nerine's knee drove into Ripples' right shoulder' after the tap); the tap ends the grip, so everything else in the beat is told before it. bite_place: a bite told landing on a part it never touched, or next to one ('her teeth sank between the toes' for a bite on her back). move_names: 'Nerine's Aqua Jet' when she threw a Water Gun this beat and has never used an Aqua Jet in the fight is put right with no model call (only when she used just one move this beat). fresh_worn (since build 269): a fighter still fresh (strength at fresh_from % or more) told as tiring, fading or running out, or someone wondering how much she has left ("how much did Ripples have left in her?" on the opening beat). locked_gap (since build 272): a space, a gap or strides between them told while a grip joins them at the end of the beat ("the space between them, unchanged, a few paces of grass" with Nerine's tails round Ripples'). enabled false = all off; each switch on its own.

narration._inner_blocks_comment: inner_blocks (since build 267, on by default): story_blocks.txt ideas for what happens inside her, offered from her own side when the engine says it happens: a surge of adrenaline or a second wind (surge, moment first/second), her sight greying (grey_out), her health past zero (running_on_empty), and a try at getting up that fails (getup_fail). The submission ideas (narration.sub_blocks) also gained a choke told from the inside (choke_fight, by how near the dark is) and breaking out of a submission, from both sides (sub_escape_held, sub_escape_hold). false = none of the inner ones.
narration._constriction_feel_comment: constriction_feel (since build 293, on by default): each beat of a constriction (finish.submission.constriction) the story gets one idea of what the coiler feels of the other's heart through her coils and does about it (waits for the breath out, eases a fraction, holds it there), and one of what the one held feels of her own heart (loud in her ears, then slowing and skipping, then faint with gaps in it), following the same stages as the constriction. Feelings and choices, never numbers. The heart's rate and the blood pressure the screen shows are given to the story as words (racing, slowed, slow and heavy; up, falling, low) so the two agree. verify: when she blacks out in the coils, the coiler doesn't let go at once: she holds a while longer, feeling for any fight left, until she is sure it is over (through the silence of a stopped heart too, constriction.heart_stop), and only then unwinds; false = she unwinds as soon as she feels her go slack. enabled false = none of the ideas.

polish._comment: polish (since build 268; off until you turn it on with /polish on): after the local model has written a beat and every check has run, the finished beat and a short fact sheet of what really happened are sent to a stronger online model to improve the prose without changing what happens. Venice.ai is the default service (base_url); any service that speaks the OpenAI chat format works. Its version is kept only when it is not a refusal, keeps every '— Name —' part label in order and every fighter, is at least min_ratio of the local length (no longer than max_ratio of it, when that is set), and the program's own sentence checks find no more wrong in it than in the local version (allow_new_slips more at most); otherwise the local version stands, and /compare shows both. when: every (each beat) or big (taps, knockouts, the finish and other big moments only: fewer requests). model: /polish models lists what the service has; a larger one edits better. The key is never kept here: /polish key writes polish_key.txt (left out of git), or set the POLISH_API_KEY or VENICE_API_KEY environment variable. extra_body: sent with each request to Venice (its own system prompt off, so the editor's instructions are the only ones). By hand instead: /polish copy puts the request in polish_request.txt and the clipboard; paste Venice's answer into polish_reply.txt and type /polish paste: the same checks decide, and the fight stays in the game.
polish._length_comment: min_ratio and max_ratio: the polished beat must be at least min_ratio of the local version's length (cutting more than that loses what happened). max_ratio (since build 303: 0 = no upper limit, the default) caps how much longer it may be; before build 303 it was 1.5, and a longer, better version was thrown out for it. expand (since build 303, on by default): the editor is told it may make the beat longer where that makes it better (more of what each fighter sees, feels and thinks, the big moments given room), never with anything new happening; the program's checks still decide whether it is kept. false = it is asked to keep to about the draft's length.
polish._condition_comment: condition (since build 269, on by default): the fact sheet also says how each fighter is at the end of the beat: her health as a share of full, her pain overall (the window's gauge: bearable, hurting badly, near her limit, past what she can bear) and her four worst-hurt parts in the story's pain words with their damage ('left upper arm very painful (95%)'), so the editor sizes every hurt right and never has a fresh fighter tiring. The prompt (/polish prompt) can be your own: polish_prompt.txt.
polish._body_comment: body (since build 325, on by default): the fact sheet also has a BODY line for each fighter, the numbers the window's heart monitor and hovers show: her heart rate against her own resting rate and what it means (pounding, racing, slowing under the coils, uneven, stopped), her blood pressure (normal, low, raised), her breathing (how fast, how deep, why), her core heat (flushed, heat-exhausted, shivering), her air, her blood and where she bleeds, her footing, her composure, her adrenaline, and in coils how hard they press: squeezed in, the blood flow cut off, the pressure, her girth, her heart's strength left, each grip's pressure and how fast it tightens, and the grey. The editor is told to show these in what she feels and what can be seen, never as numbers or medical words. false = no BODY lines.
polish._setting_comment: setting (since build 269, on by default): the fact sheet also starts with WHO each fighter is (her appearance from fighters.json, up to look_chars characters, whole sentences only, so the editor gives her only the body she has) and WHERE they are (the arena, up to place_chars), and ends with her statuses (soaked, chilled...), the tap count in a match of several taps, and how far apart they are.
polish._batch_comment: history and batch_max (since build 271): the game keeps every beat (history 0, since build 272: no limit; a number keeps only that many of the latest), with its local text and facts, saved with the game, for polishing by hand several at once. /polish copy 5-9, /polish copy 7, /polish copy last 4 or /polish copy all puts up to batch_max of them in one request, each between '=== BEAT n ===' and '=== END BEAT n ===' lines with its own beat number; /polish paste puts each answer back on its own beat by that number, checked and kept or not by itself (/polish paste 7: an answer with no markers, for beat 7). Keep batches small: a chat window may cut off a long answer.
polish._keep_fights_comment: keep_fights (since build 273): what the narrator knew about each beat (so a polish pasted back later gets every check, not only the label, length and hit-part ones) is also kept on disk, in polish_states/, one small compressed file a beat, for the last keep_fights fights; older fights' files are removed as new ones come. 0 = in memory only (lost when the game closes).

compact._comment: Shorter notes for the narrator, to try out (each can be turned off on its own; enabled false turns them all off and the notes are as before). rules_when_needed: the rule about breath being knocked out comes only in beats with a grip, a pin, a pummel or a winding blow, and the Buizel-tails rule only when one is fighting. beat_rules_in_message: this beat's own rules (swearing, talk, no pin clock...) go at the top of the message instead of the end of the fixed instructions, and the author's instructions come before the style sample, so the start of the prompt is the same from part to part and beat to beat and Ollama can reuse its work on it (faster). fighters_once: the fighters' full notes in part 1 of a beat; later parts keep each one's appearance, tells and voice but not her description. checks_merged: no 'how much it hurts' line for a fighter the MEASURED PAIN note already covers. sounds_where_hit: the full rules for sounds only in the part where the blows land, one line elsewhere. craft_trim: the Craft rules in about two thirds of the words (none dropped; the style sample shows the rest). rules_trim (build 231): the Hard rules in fewer words: every rule kept, the ones said two or three times in different words (only the listed events, in order; the tone; nobody dying) said once; the program's own checks still catch a slip of any of them afterwards. author_trim (build 231): the author's instructions (story_prompt.txt) without what the narrator already has: its TONE section when rules_trim is on (the hard rules carry every point of it), the note on where the length is set, and the bullet on grapples, chains and tumbles in a beat with none of them. The file is untouched and the director still reads all of it. repair_lean (build 231): a call that writes one paragraph again (its mistake named) gets the part's facts, plan and card but not what was there for writing a whole part (its building blocks, how deep to go, the camera). blow_detail_where_landed (build 231): how each blow lands (the body under it, how it moves her, its sound, the reaction ideas for each hit, the devastating blow's ways to sell it) only in the part where the blows land; the attacker's side, the aftermath and a watcher's part get what each blow is, where and how hard. That part never tells the landing again anyway, and the notes for the other parts are a good deal shorter.

bench._comment: The narration test bench (/bench). save: keep each beat's narrator inputs in folder (next to play.py), the last keep of them, so /bench can tell them again under other settings and compare (reports go to reports). A saved beat is a few hundred kB.

card._comment: The beat card (on by default since build 225; enabled false goes back to the plain prompt, and /bench compares the two): a short block at the END of each part's prompt, right before the model writes, where a small model pays most attention. WHO (each fighter, her kind and her role this beat), WHERE (posture, in the water or on land), CONTACTS (every grip as owner's limb -> owner's part, both named), THIS PART (what lands in this part and how much it hurts, or that nothing lands yet), MIND (inner_lines facts for the fighter the part is told from, from narration.rich.inner) and the JOB last. It repeats facts the notes already give, in fixed note form, so the model has one place to check them; nothing in it is new. hold_events (build 228): a HOLDS THIS BEAT line for every part after contact: a grip closing (marked new, so it is shown clamping on), its pressure, her refusing to tap, a break-out, and in the last part the tap-out; without it the card listed only the blows and the model left the rest out.

rich._comment: Richer, longer narration (slower beats). enabled false turns all of it off. length_mult: each beat's word target times this (more words also means more parts). words_per_paragraph: each part is asked for at least its words / this many paragraphs. inner: an INNER LIFE note from the engine (what each fighter has learned this fight: her moves that land or miss, the move that keeps hitting her, attacks she has dodged, what her worst wounds stop her doing, how tired she is, the wound she can see on her opponent, what the last beat cost her) for her thoughts and plans; wound_from is the part damage that counts as a bad wound, wounds_listed how many, max_lines the most facts a fighter gets, low_energy / tired_energy the energy lines, big_loss the % of strength a beat must take to be called out. senses: each part leans on one sense (sound, smell, touch, temperature, taste, light), the one the fight has used least. closing_thoughts: the last part of a beat gives each conscious fighter a few sentences of her own mind. extra_thoughts: italic thoughts allowed per part on top of talk.thoughts_per_part. budget_mult: the beat time budget (beat_budget_minutes) times this. body_detail: each blow that lands gets a note on how it works on the body in that instant (the pressure of contact, the head snapping round from a blow to the cheek, the chest driven in, fur and skin stretching or flattening), by the kind of blow, where it lands and how hard; a fighter held fast gets the pressure, not the movement. no_linger: with body_detail on, no LINGER ON ONE MOMENT note as well (every blow already gets its slow telling; both had the same blow told three or four times). interlude_words: an interlude (narration.interlude) is this long with rich on, and gets the INNER LIFE note too. wound_watch: from the second beat, each part's fighter takes stock of her own worst wounds once (parts at wound_watch_from damage or more: how they feel, what they stop her doing), and gets two or three visible signs of her opponent's hurt to notice, picked from how far gone she is and where her worst wound is (the body rising and falling with each breath, an eye half-closing on each breath out, winces, a held limb, weight off a leg, a sway). Each is told in one part of the beat, not every part; a wound she has already taken stock of comes up again only when it gets worse or after wound_watch_again beats, and the signs she notices rotate (none offered two beats running when there are others). quiet_mult: a beat where nobody is hurt (a breather, two attacks cancelling out) gets its word target times this: a pause told short instead of padded (1 = the full length).

narration._roll_notes_comment: roll_notes (on by default, since build 226): a blow whose damage roll (damage.roll) came up near the top or bottom of its range, within edge of the end (0.7: the outer 30% each side, about three blows in ten), is told how: it caught her just right, landed flush, found her breathing out; or she turned a fraction, half rolled with it, braced in time. Landings the same way (came down on an edge / on the flat). Only the picture: the numbers already hold it. Not on devastating blows. enabled false: no such notes.
narration._tap_last_comment: tap_last (since build 236, on by default): when a beat is written in several parts, the tap-out or pass-out that ends the match is kept for the LAST part: the earlier parts are told it is not theirs to tell, and one that tells it anyway has those sentences (and the holder letting go right after) taken out, so it is told at the end, after everything else that happens in the beat. false = any part may tell it.
narration._cuts_comment: cuts (since build 238, on by default): mends the program makes to the finished story by itself, with no model call. cuts.first_beat_past: on the first beat nobody has been hit before, so a past that can't be there is cut ("still sore from the earlier blows" goes; "from her last dive" is taken out of its sentence). cuts.ache_repeat: how many sentences in a beat may only say how one hurt part feels (an ache, a throb, a burn, with no blow, grip or move in it): past that many, the rest are cut (0 = off). cuts.labels: a move label copied as words ("Nerine's plain blow hit" -> "Nerine's blow hit"). cuts.handoff: the hand-over between parts said out loud ("Nerine's reaction would follow.") is cut. cuts.run_on_thought: a thought run straight into the next words gets its full stop ("That leg needs to go Her mind" -> "go. Her mind"). cuts.enabled false turns them all off. Since build 239: run_on_thought also mends a thought in its marks run into the next words ('*I can't give up now* She steeled') and a run-on into A or An; caps: a note's word copied in capitals ('was RUINED') written as a word; salt: no saltwater or saltiness in fresh water (a lake, a pool), only by the sea; end_stop: a paragraph that ends with no full stop gets one.
narration._tap_shown_comment: tap_shown (on by default): a beat that ends in a tap-out or a pass-out must show it; a passage that leaves it out gets a short passage of its own for it, like any other left-out event. Since build 228 that passage is checked too: if it still does not show the tap (or the pass-out) it is asked for once more, then said in one plain sentence, and it always goes at the very end of the beat. false = not checked.

tap_build._comment: Submission matches (finish.submission). Each time a fighter refuses to tap to the same opponent, SHE WON'T TAP climbs: the first time her paw twitches toward the ground and stops, the second it touches the ground and she drags it back, from the third it lies flat on the ground shaking and she holds it still (and her reason for holding on is gone: only stubbornness, or a plea for it to stop on its own). From holder_from refusals past what she can bear, WHAT THE HOLDER FEELS THROUGH THE GRIP: the twitch and the stop, her own grip tiring, what she thinks of her still refusing, and maybe one low word to give up. A tap-out also asks for the after: the loser curled round the hurt part, the winner standing over her. enabled false keeps the one plain line every time. vary (on by default, since build 226): the twitch, the touch and the flat paw are no longer the same three steps every match: each refusal shows ONE sign picked from a set for how near she is (variety.tap_tell_first, tap_tell_closer, tap_tell_edge: a twitch, claws curling, a swallowed word, a paw she traps under herself, a 'no' said aloud, tears...), never one she showed in her last few. How near goes mostly by how often she has refused, but pain far past what she can bear pushes it a step nearer and now and then (one in five) she finds a little more in herself and it comes a step back. Past her limit she also gets a reason she is holding on (variety.tap_reason: pride, anger, not to HER, hoping it slips, stubbornness, a plea; the last two likelier the longer she refuses) and the holder a feeling about it (variety.tap_holder). A choke's fight against the dark (variety.tap_dark) and the tap itself (variety.tap_way: slaps, frantic pats, a cry, one quiet word, her body giving in first) vary the same way. vary false: the fixed three steps.

hold_tries._comment: Getting out of a hold, told the way a held fighter really works through it. Each beat she is in a hold (not a pin: pins have their own), WHAT SHE TRIES THIS BEAT names one real way out of THAT kind of hold (a choke: tuck the chin, haul the arm down for a breath; a leg lock: turn with the twist, drop her weight, peel a finger back; an arm lock, a tail, a body hold, the head), and lists the ones she has already tried in it so she never tries the same thing twice. The tries go from thought-out (fresh) to wild (her health under thrash_below %, thrash_after beats in, or the part at pain level thrash_pain) to spent (health under spent_below %, or spent_after beats in). remember = how many earlier tries are listed. The engine's 'she fights the grip' note uses the same try. under_blow: a blow that lands on her while she is held brings the reader back to the grip after it, still on under everything. enabled false turns both off.

plan_notes._comment: The narrator's side of director.game_plan. On the first beat (up to open_by), WHAT EACH CAME IN FOR: the part of the other each one means to take apart, shown as a look and a thought, never a speech. Then, on the at-th time (2nd, 4th, 7th, 11th) she gets a blow onto that part, HER PLAN, WORKING: a flicker of it in her, and from the third time the other knows it too. enabled false turns both off (the director still gets the plan).

hold_position._comment: On the first beat of a hold, DRAW THE POSITION: the narrator is asked to set out plainly where each fighter is and faces, what each of the holder's limbs is gripping and what she has free, where the trapped part points and which way the force goes, in plain directions, so the reader can picture it. A blow the holder strikes while her hold is still on is told as coming from what she has free (a gripping paw comes off for that blow alone; the grip holds). And a tap is put where she can reach: the ground if she is down, the holder's arm or shoulder if she is held on her feet. enabled false turns all three off.

style_read._comment: Notes from what really happened in this fight. From from_beat on, every every beats, HOW EACH HAS FOUGHT SO FAR: up close and physical (grabs, throws, slams, charges into the scenery), from range, or trading blows, counted from her attacks so far, so the prose keeps the style she has actually shown even where her description says she usually fights another way. And THE SAME PLACE AGAIN: a fighter put into a piece of standing scenery (a tree, a rock, a wall) she was put into before remembers it as she hits it. opponent_read: from read_from on, every every beats (between the style notes), WHAT SHE HAS LEARNED OF HER: each fighter's read of the other from what has really happened (the part she keeps coming back to, the move she reaches for again and again, how many times she has got back up, how many attacks she has slipped), for her thoughts about her to reason from and change as the fight goes. enabled false turns all of it off.

build_up._comment: Reactions that build instead of staying one note. enabled false turns all of it off. holds: a hold, pin or coil that goes on, and hurts more, makes the held fighter fight it harder each beat (testing it, then squirming, then thrashing, then desperate), and climb within the part when it is very painful. old_wounds: a blow or landing of old_wound_hit damage or more on a part already at pain level old_wound_from (2 = hurting, 3 = very painful) takes her over for a moment (rolling, curling, grabbing at or rubbing it, arching, gasping), by where it is; old_wound_chance of the time (a landing, throw or slam adds 0.25). climb: several blows on one fighter in one attack get reactions that grow, the last the worst. carry_on: a part hurt that way, or left excruciating, keeps being felt for carry_beats beats after (nursing it, a wince when she moves it, favouring it as she gets up).

narration._mend_thoughts_comment: mend_thoughts (since build 305, on by default): thoughts mended with no call: a thought given a voice ("*I won't lose,* she thought, her voice calm": a thought isn't heard) loses the voice; a first-person thought slipped into the past is put back in her present ("*I needed to finish this*" becomes "*I need to*"); a thought said again a moment later goes; and a thought one fighter had, given almost word for word to the other in her own part, goes from the second. false = thoughts left as written.
narration._mend_fragments: true (build 231): a sentence a cut left with no verb of its own, opening on a body part ('Nerine's left paw, her forearm fin flaring wide as she met the attack') gets a plain one ('Nerine's left paw came up, ...'; tails 'swept round'); false leaves it.
narration._trim_past_contact: true (build 231): the attacker's part is meant to stop at the instant her blow lands; sentences after that about the one hit feeling it (her yelp, the pain flaring) are cut from it when the next part, the one hit's own, tells her anyway. false leaves them.
narration._tense_words_first: true (build 230): present-tense sentences that survived the rewrites have their common verbs put into the past by the program first (no model call); the copy-editing call is made only when two or more are still left. false = the call whenever two or more are found.
narration._hit_counts: true (build 230): a count of blows the story makes up ('Ripples had landed one hit so far', seven beats in) is put right from the attacks that really landed; false leaves it as written.
narration._old_memories: true lets story blocks and lines reach back before the fight (an old fight, training, a lesson, something long ago). Off by default: the story has no past before the fight.

checklist._comment: Optional help for a small local model: each part of a beat also gets a short CHECKLIST of what it must contain (who uses what on whom, where each blow lands and how hard, how that part hurts now, who ends up where, a knockout), straight from the engine and kept apart from the colour ideas. Nothing in it is new: it is the notes in short. Off by default; try it on if the model skips hits or gets parts wrong, and turn it off again if the writing gets stiffer or list-like.

guided._comment: Engine-led narration (trial): the engine hands the narrator more of the facts ready-made, so fewer drafts come back wrong. enabled false turns all of it off. fact_lines: a draft that leaves a blow out gets a sentence for it put in where it belongs (its shape picked by the dice) instead of a whole rewrite. paragraph_plan: in the part where the blows land, a PARAGRAPH PLAN, one paragraph per blow (the jarred parts with it, the rest after), each given as the facts in note form (who, with what, which part and side, how hard), never as wording, so the story still tells each blow its own way; max_paragraphs caps it. marks: VISIBLE WEAR says when each mark was made (new this beat, or how many beats ago), 'no cuts and no blood anywhere' for a fighter only ever struck blunt, and 'no marks that show yet' for one with none. reads: now and then (read_chance a beat, never two beats running for the same fighter: read_gap) the attacker gets one tactical read from what the engine knows before she commits (the part of her opponent that is going, her own weak spot, who is wearing down faster, a flyer's failing wing), to show as a thought or a look in her own voice. sided_check (build 230): a blow on one side isn't counted as told by the other side's part (Aqua Tail on her right thigh was taken as told by 'her left thigh twitched'), and a fact line put back for a part a blow only jarred doesn't count as the whole blow told; false = the old looser test.

phrase_memory._comment: Stock phrases kept from repeating, across fights and runs of the program (phrase_memory.json next to play.py: copy it along to a new build's folder to keep the history). The phrases: stock_phrases.txt (edit it; one per line), and the four-word runs a fight leans on (worn_phrases), learned and kept. Each has a running total and a heat: a use adds 1, and heat halves every half_life_beats beats. Before each beat the warm ones are RESTED (listed for the narrator to leave alone this beat): at always_rest heat or more always, from rest_from by a roll of the dice weighted by heat, so a phrase used a moment ago is nearly always kept out and one unused for a long while drifts back in by itself. Nothing is ever offered for use, so no phrase gets pushed. max_listed: at most this many a beat. forget_below: a learned phrase that cools below this is dropped. /phrases shows the totals.

narration._hits_comment: Telling the hits: a hit under name_hits_from damage (measured as at the default /scale 3) that changes no pain level can be grouped with the rest or left with no body part named; every_hit_chance of beats go through every hit one by one instead (each told a different way).
narration._comment: story_prompt.txt holds your plain-English storytelling instructions. style_sample_file is writing for the narrator to imitate: a plain file is shown from its start, up to style_sample_chars characters; a file written in sections (lines starting with ==, like style_sample_scenes.txt) gives the narrator the passage that fits the part it is about to write. /sample lists the samples in the folder and switches between them; your earlier ones are style_sample.txt, style_sample_previous.txt and style_sample_intense.txt. sample_copy_check: a sentence copied word for word from the sample is cut. max_words caps each response. context_window is the model's working memory in tokens: raise it for longer stories if your GPU has room, lower it if responses get slow.
narration._story_state_comment: story_state: before each beat the narrator is told where the fight stands as a story (early, middle, late, near the end), how each fighter is doing and who has been pressing whom, how it sits with her (confident, worried, desperate...), whether the fight has just turned, and whether this beat is a turning point or an ordinary exchange. All of it is worked out by the program from the dice; it decides nothing. false turns it off.
narration._turning_comment: turning_point_length: a turning point (a fighter pinned for the first time, a pin broken after it had begun to tell, the pressing changing hands) and the beat that ends the fight are given this many times the usual words. Ordinary beats are never shortened. 1 turns it off.
narration._pov_labels_comment: pov_labels: each part of a beat is headed with whose side it is told from (a line '— Nocturne —', or '— Both —' for a part about both of them), so it is always clear whose eyes these are. The labels are only for you: the models are shown the story without them. false = no labels.
narration._raw_reactions_comment: raw_reactions: when a real blow lands on a part that was ALREADY very painful, excruciating or devastated, the narrator is told to make the reaction visceral, scaled by how hurt the part was, how big the blow is (a brush on a ruined part is far less than a real blow there) and how much strength she has left: most of her strength = she fights to keep it in (a hiss, a bitten-off cry); middling = a real scream and shaking; nearly spent = a raw scream that cracks, shaking she can't stop, streaming eyes. One big reaction per fighter per beat; later blows that beat build on it. Never sobbing. false = off.
narration._jarred_size_cap_comment: jarred_size_cap: a part only jarred by a blow aimed beside it (moves.auto_spill, a fraction of the power) is sized in the notes as at most this (glancing, solid, heavy or tremendous), however much it hurt a worn part. Words only.
narration._arena_detail_uses_comment: arena_detail_uses: how many times in one fight each of the scene's details (scenes.json: details) may be offered to the narrator as 'the place, glimpsed in passing'. Once every detail has had its turns, the parts go without one (the place is still in the scene text). 0 = no limit.
narration._size_cap_by_pain_comment: size_cap_by_pain: a blow is sized in the notes (and its impact examples and reaction ideas picked) as at most this when the part it hit ends the blow at that lasting pain level: a blow that leaves the part minor is at most solid, sore at most heavy (no 'heavy blow' with a cry torn out of her on a part that barely hurts). Levels not listed are not capped. Words only.
narration._blocks_comment: Story building blocks (story_blocks.txt): a large file of ideas (reactions, sensations, how a hurt spreads, breath, what an opponent can see of an injury, ways to stage a move, thoughts, feelings, takedowns, pins, getting up, landings, aftermath). Before each part of a beat the program offers the narrator up to per_part of them that FIT the fight as it stands (the size of the blow, how much each part hurts now, who is fresh or spent, what her body has), preferring the least-offered and never one offered in the last cooldown_beats beats. They are suggestions to reword, never new events. remember: what was offered is kept between fights in blocks_memory.json. /blocks shows the counts; /blocks off turns them off.
narration._light_effect_max_level_comment: blocks.light_effect_max_level: a not-very-effective (or no-effect) blow gets its matchup ideas (it hardly marks her, it breaks against her, she shrugs it off) only while every part it hit ends this beat at this pain level or lower (minor, sore, hurting, very painful, excruciating, devastated). A weak blow that still leaves a part hurting is told by its hurt, not by the matchup.
narration._sub_blocks_comment: sub_blocks (build 227): in a submission match, while a submission hold is on, each part of the beat is also offered ideas and a finished line for what the hold is like by now, from the side that part is told from: the one held (sub_held in story_blocks.txt and story_lines.txt) or the one holding it (sub_hold), by how long it has been on (held: early, middle, long) and how badly the worst held part hurts (level). false: no hold ideas.
narration._lines_comment: lines: the library of finished sentences (story_lines.txt, same format as the blocks). One that fits is offered to the narrator per part, to use word for word if it fits; a bare line of told resolve the program cuts ("She would not be defeated.") is replaced by one that shows it. cooldown_beats: how long before the same line can come back. Used lines are remembered in lines_memory.json.
narration._style_repairs_comment: style_repairs_max: how many paragraphs a part may be written again for WORDING alone (filler, a phrase already used this beat, a stray label, a sound standing alone). Mistakes about what happened, reactions bigger than her injuries and wrong anatomy are always fixed. Lower it for speed, raise it for polish.
narration._reaction_caps_comment: reaction_caps: how big a fighter's reactions may be, from her overall health AND her worst part. strong_from % or more: covered pain (a sharp cry at most, even on a ruined part; a devastating blow one step up, a brief scream). mid_from to strong_from: screams, no writhing or convulsing. Below mid_from: no limit, raw. strong_from matches where the notes stop calling her 'winded' (60%: still fast and dangerous), so a fighter told as still strong never gets 'too worn to hold it in'.
narration._full_chokes_comment: full_chokes (on by default, since build 233): the hard rule on breathing lets a CHOKE cut off her air or the blood to her head COMPLETELY (and the two kinds are told apart, as the engine reads the grip: an AIR choke shuts the windpipe, her chest heaving on nothing, slow; a BLOOD choke squeezes the sides of the neck, she still breathes but her head fills, roars and greys, quick; jaws or hands round the throat do both: every beat a grip is on her neck the notes name its kind and how far it has gone), since held long enough that is how a choke ends: she passes out (in a pin the choke ended, or a pass-out in a submission match). She only faints, and only when the events say so; once it lets go she breathes again. A submission hold on the neck is told as a choke that can take her out, and the story passages offer the long chokes and the pass-out itself. false: as before, breath is only ever stopped for a few seconds at a time.
narration._passages_comment: passages: the library of showpiece passages (story_passages.txt, same format as the blocks): two to four finished sentences for the big moments (a heavy blow, a cut, a bite, a choke by its kind and the pass-out from it, a hold, a pin, a landing, a knockout, and for flyers a blow on a wing or a beak, the fall out of the air and the tumble down locked together), each fitted to the part, how hard it landed, how badly it hurts and her body. Rarely, the biggest moment of a part gets ONE: chance is how often a part that has such a moment gets one, min_gap_beats how many beats must pass before another (one per beat at most). place_share of them are offered to be set in word for word in place of the narrator's own telling of that moment; the rest are offered as inspiration only (its senses and rhythm, never its words), and with copy_check a sentence copied from one of those anyway is cut. cooldown_beats: how long before the same passage can come back; used passages are remembered in passages_memory.json (delete it to start again). enabled false: none at all.
narration._plan_comment: blocks.plan: the blocks are laid out as numbered steps whose order changes from beat to beat (false: a plain list). blocks.open_and_end: the plan gives an image to open a beat on and one to end it on. arena_detail: one detail of the place the story has not used lately, as background (from the scene's details list in scenes.json). callback_memory: when a part that an earlier blow hurt is hurt again, the narrator is pointed at that earlier blow, once per part in a long while. leaned_words: describing words the last few beats used min_count times or more are named, so the narrator reaches for others.
narration._words_comment: words_per_beat: target length. With two_pass_pov on, the attacker's side and the receiver's side are written as two separate halves, which keeps long narration coherent.
narration._scene_intro_comment: scene_intro: false skips the opening narration that sets the scene (the arena and the fighters arriving); the first Enter goes straight to the first beat. /set narration.scene_intro false
narration._linger_comment: Chance per beat (0-1) that one blow gets a long, slow reaction, and how many extra words it gets. 0 turns it off.
narration._linger_min_share_comment: The lingered-on blow is one of the beat's real ones: a part that just crossed its breaking point if there is one, else a hit at least this share (0-1) of the heaviest hit this beat. 0 lets any hit be picked.
narration._gore_comment: gore_check: if a draft goes past gore_level (below), the narrator rewrites it once with those phrases flagged, then cuts any sentence that's still too graphic. Set to false to turn off.
narration._gore_level_comment: gore_level: "mild" (default) allows a little blood, small cuts, and bites that break the skin, and only rewrites EXTREME gore (torn or shredded flesh, exposed or breaking bone, pooling blood, severed parts, death). "none" rewrites any blood or wounds. "off" turns the check off.
narration._swearing_comment: "rare" (default): an occasional single curse, at most one every swearing_gap beats. "never": none. "free": no limit. /set narration.swearing never
narration._numb_tier_comment: true: parts at 1000%+ damage go 'numb with shock' (⚪). false: they stay 'devastated' (⚫). Toggle with /numb on|off or /set narration.numb_tier false
narration._bone_break_comment: Bones may always crack or bruise. Broken, fractured, or shattered bones are allowed only on a part with at least min_part_damage damage, on a fighter whose health is below max_health. boneless: words of part names with no bone in them to break (a stomach, a throat, a fin); those parts are never listed as able to break.
narration._accuracy_comment: accuracy_check: if a draft skips a listed hit (never mentions that body part) or skips a pin struggle it was told to show, the narrator rewrites it once with the gaps flagged.
narration._best_of_two_comment: best_of_two: "important" (default) writes two drafts for big moments (a pin starting or ending, a launch, a breaking point, an adrenaline surge, a knockout) and keeps the one with fewer problems; "always" does it every beat (twice as slow); "off" never.
narration._variety_comment: variety_check: a draft is rewritten if it uses any overused_phrases more than once, or one that a recent beat already used, or repeats a recent thought or spoken line word for word. Add or remove phrases freely.
narration._repair_comment: paragraph_repair: when a draft has a mistake the program can point at, only that paragraph is written again (up to repair_tries times, at most repair_paragraphs_max paragraphs a part) and the rest stays word for word; a whole rewrite happens only when something is MISSING (a hit, the escape, the get-up). false = the old way: the whole part is rewritten for any problem. reader_check: after that, the model reads the passage back against the facts and lists contradictions in its own words (one short extra call per part); what it finds is rewritten the same way, never cut on its word alone. reader_model: a different model to do that reading (empty = the narrator's). reader_on_cpu: when reader_model names a different model, run it on the CPU in system memory (Ollama option num_gpu 0), so the narrator is not unloaded from the graphics card for every reading; slower per reading, no swapping. reader_max_fixes: paragraphs it may send back per part.
narration._reader_gate_comment: reader_gate: a second reading's finding only counts when the program's own look at the quoted sentence agrees it could be that kind of mistake (a posture finding needs a sentence that states a posture the fighter has at NO point of the beat, and so on); the rest is set aside and shown in the log. reader_confirm (off by default since build 95): what passes is asked about a second time ('is this fine?') before any paragraph is rewritten for it (one more short call per finding). In a real run the second ask talked the reader out of a finding that was right, and a finding only ever causes a rewrite, so the program's own gate is trusted instead. /reader confirm on brings it back.
narration._repeat_memory_comment: repeat_memory: a short sentence (4-10 words) the fight has already used word for word, however many beats ago, is cut the next time it turns up ('The cave held its breath.'). false = only the last few beats are checked.
narration._passes_comment: Long beats are written in focused parts of about words_per_pass words (max 4): 2 parts = attacker's side + receiver's side; 3 adds the aftermath; 4 adds the lead-up. Short parts keep the detail dense. Change length live with /words.
narration._more_comment: /more (or +) stays in the moment: the narrator adds about more_words words on the stillness and what the last blows left behind, without the fight moving on. more_after_attacks: add that many such passages on their own after every beat with an attack (0 = only when you ask; /more auto <n>).
narration._sampler_comment: repeat_penalty above 1 discourages looping/repeated phrases (1.05-1.2 is typical). min_p and top_p trim unlikely words. Lower temperature = steadier, higher = wilder.
narration._top_up_comment: If a beat ends up shorter than top_up_below x its target length (usually because repeated or copied lines were removed), one more pass continues it with new detail. 0 turns it off.
narration._max_rewrites_comment: 1 = one rewrite per draft; 2 = one more try when the text still gets the events wrong (an invented fall, a missing hit).
narration._beat_budget_comment: beat_budget_minutes: once a beat has taken this long, the optional extra passes stop (a second whole rewrite, a second draft, wording-only fixes, the second reading); past 1.5 times it, no whole rewrites at all, only paragraph fixes. Every part is still written in full and the program's own checks and cleanup still run, so no detail is cut to save time. 0 = no budget. show_timing prints where each beat's time went. Set with /budget.
narration._notes_decay_comment: notes_decay (off by default: it only shortened late notes by about 5%; /set narration.notes_decay.enabled true to use it): small details leave the narrator's notes once they are stale, so later beats read shorter notes. origin_beats: how a part was hurt ('from Ripples' Ice Beam, then...') is kept while the part was hit in the last this-many beats; after that only its pain level stays, unless one huge hit did it (big_hit: that much part damage in one go): that hit is remembered for the rest of the fight. Its visible marks shorten to the main one. wear_beats: surface details (grit in her coat, a scuff) last this many beats. Pain levels, injuries, posture and everything that happens are never trimmed. 0 = keep forever.
narration._big_wounds_comment: big_wounds: each fighter's few hardest single hits (at least notes_decay.big_hit part damage in one go, the biggest first, up to max) are named in the notes as the wounds that matter most, so the story gives them more weight. One short line; no extra model calls or checks.
narration._settling_in_comment: settling_in (since build 306, on by default): hurts come on in the beats after a blow, not all at once. A part hit at least a beat ago and untouched since, whose damage has passed the next of the from steps (60 stiffening, 150 swelling and favored, 300 barely used), gets one line in the notes, SETTLING IN, by where it is (a foot or knee: a hitch when she puts her weight on it, then favoring it; ribs: each breath catching; a jaw or cheek: swelling, throbbing with her pulse; a shoulder: rising slower), for the story to show once in how she moves; the next step only once it is that bad. Only for max_age beats after the hit, per_beat lines a fighter at most (the worst first). It is worked out once a beat (a rerolled beat gets the same) and kept with her, so undo puts it back. false = none.
narration._interlude_comment: interlude: now and then, after a beat, a LONG passage where the fight draws breath (nobody attacks; thoughts, the body taking stock, the place in detail, why they fight). chance per beat, about words long, at least min_gap beats apart, not before beat from_beat. /interlude now writes one at once, /interlude next after the next beat. not_in_holds (since build 249): none comes by itself while a pin, a hold or a submission is on (the fight isn't drawing breath then); /interlude still writes one.
narration._interlude_retold_comment: interlude.retold_cut (since build 259): an interlude sentence that tells again what the story just said in other words goes: when this share or more of its content words (it needs 6 or more) are in one sentence of the last part of the story, or of the interlude before it; a sentence right after it that leans on it (But it..., And that...) goes with it. Beat 9 of the build-254 Ripples vs Nocturne log retold its own beat in the interlude. 0 = off.
narration._engine_mends_comment: engine_mends (since build 259): the finished prose of each beat and interlude is checked against what the engine knows, and the slips put right in place, with no extra call to the model. species: with two fighters of different species, 'the Buizel' told of the Absol becomes her name, when the sentence says so: a part only the other one has (the Buizel's horn), a hurt only she has (the Buizel's right hip when only Nocturne's is wrecked), the other's grip, or, in a part of the beat told from the Buizel's own side, a sentence opening 'The Buizel' right after one about the other alone, or one that names the Buizel as someone else. grip_part: a grip told closing on (or bearing on) a part it is not on ('the twin tails whipped around Nocturne's right knee' when the grip is on her left forepaw) is told on the gripped part, or the nearest gripped part on that side, unless the beat struck that part. roles: the held one given the grip ('Ripples wriggled ..., but Nocturne's grip was unyielding' when Ripples holds Nocturne): the two names trade places in that sentence (a grip on the ground, a tree and so on is left alone). order (since build 260): a blow and then a grip from the same fighter on the same one, with the grip told first ('Her grip on Nerine was tight' two paragraphs before the Aqua Jet it followed): the grip's paragraph goes after the one where the blow lands, when both are in the same part of the beat. harmless (since build 260): in a beat where a blow did damage, 'harmlessly' goes (a not very effective Aqua Jet told as rippling off harmlessly). enabled false = none of it.
narration._tap_fight_shown_comment: tap_fight_shown (since build 261): every beat of a submission (and any hold she is fighting the urge to tap in) must show her fighting the tap, and the more it hurts the more of the passage it takes: at least sentences[level - 1] sentences of it, by the 1-5 level the narrator is told (1 felt and held easily ... 5 at the very edge): with the defaults 1, 2, 2, 3 and 4. A draft that gives it less gets a short passage of its own for it, and if that still leaves it out, the program tells this beat's sign of it (her paw rising and yanked back, a fist clenched against it) plainly. Not on the beat she taps. enabled false = not checked.
narration._talk_comment: How much fighters talk. spoken_per_beat: spoken lines allowed in a beat; spoken_gap: beats of silence after someone speaks; thoughts_per_part: italic thoughts allowed in each part of a beat. /talk quiet|less|normal|free sets presets. hold_exchange: in a beat where she fights not to tap out of a submission (or taps), up to hold_exchange.spoken short spoken lines between the two (the holder telling her to give up, her answer through her teeth), whatever the gap; enabled false = the usual limits.
narration._dwell_comment: After a blow or squeeze on someone already badly hurt (strength at or under max_strength %, or the part now at one of part_levels), the beat may get an extra part from HER side that stays with what it did: the hurt settling in, her body, her breath, the sounds she tries to hold in, her thoughts. Nothing new happens in it. chance per eligible beat; words for the part. watch: the same moment from the side of the one who did it, studying her (every twitch, what each tells her); also on holds, pins and grapples on the ground once the one held is at hold_max_strength % or less. moment_cooldown_beats: beats to wait before the same kind of part comes again. enabled false turns either off.
narration._self_look_comment: self_look: chance that a fighter who is hit gets a cue to LOOK at her own hurt body (the wound, the shaking, whether the limb still answers) when one of her parts is very painful or worse. Always offered in the dwell and read parts.
narration._repeat_pass_comment: repeat_pass: one short model pass over the finished beat that names sentences telling an event a second time (the same blow, slam or fall); the program cuts those it can confirm. It only names them, so it takes seconds. false turns it off.
narration._roles_note_comment: roles_note (on by default): while a grip is on, every part of the beat is told who holds whom (the holder grips and keeps it on, the held one hurts in it and fights it), so the two never swap. Not used with narration.card, which has its own WHO line. false = off.

filler_trim._comment: Cuts the filler the model leans on. The stock tails go from a sentence (', a stark contrast to the cool breeze', ', a constant reminder of the blows', ', a testament to her strength'; what follows a ', but' stays). A sentence that is nothing but the place (the breeze, the leaves, the birds, the water, the light, with nobody in it) is kept at most max_ambient times a beat, once a paragraph, and never when it says again what one this beat or last beat said; the beat's first sentence and a paragraph's only sentence are kept. enabled false = left as written.

stock_limit._comment: Since build 251. The padding the model leans on (padding_phrases.txt: 'her mind raced', 'she could feel', 'her breath came in ragged gasps', 'every muscle screaming', 'she wouldn't give up'...; edit it, one per line) is allowed per_beat times a beat, and not at all once the last window_beats beats used it per_window times. Past that it is mended with no model call: 'could feel the X' becomes 'felt the X'; a phrase in a side clause loses the clause; a sentence that is nothing but padding is, by a roll of swap_chance, swapped for a line the program builds from the fight (her real worst wound and what it does to her, her breath by how far gone she is, or a short thought from what she has learned this fight: the move that keeps hitting her, the one that works, the part she can see her opponent favouring), else cut. A sentence that also tells something that happened (a hurt part, a sound, a move) only ever loses the clause. No swapped line comes back within 3 beats. enabled false = left as written.

paragraph_cap._comment: Since build 251. With narration.rich on, each part is asked for at least N paragraphs (its words / words_per_paragraph); this also asks for at most N + extra, and says a part ends when it has nothing more to tell (the build-249 logs ran 8 to 12 paragraphs of padding a side). enabled false = no upper limit.

positions_check._comment: Since build 251. The director's words for where each fighter is are put right against the engine: a piece that has her on, against or beside something that has broken in this fight goes (Nerine stood 'on the boulder' every beat after she was driven through it), and while she is down, held or holding at the foot of what a charge drove her into, a piece putting her somewhere else ('in the shallows') becomes 'by' that thing. The soaked line says only the place. The narrator is also told what has broken, and a sentence with someone standing, sitting or leaning on it is cut. enabled false = the director's words as they were.

match_state._comment: Since build 255. What the engine keeps track of about the match as a whole, for the story. distance: how far apart each pair of fighters is (locked together, in reach, a few strides apart, well apart), worked out every beat from what happened: a blow that lands or is slipped leaves them in reach, a throw or a launch puts a few strides between them, a grip or a pin locks them together and breaking out leaves them in reach, a ranged move crosses whatever gap there is and changes nothing. It goes to the narrator (DISTANCE in the condition notes and on the beat card, with how far apart they were when the beat began) and to the director (DISTANCE NOW), so nobody 'closes the gap' on someone already in reach. start: how far apart they are before anything has happened. breather_room: a breather taken in reach opens a few strides of room (unless she is down or pinned). fresh_is_early: a few beats in with both all but untouched (both above 97%), the fight is still told as its opening, not its middle (until beat 9). enabled false = all of it off.

body_slips._comment: Since build 253. Body slips in the prose mended with no call. head_snap: a head (or chin, muzzle) that SNAPS or whips back when no blow or grip this beat reached her head, face or neck becomes a jerk instead, and a 'force of it' clause after it goes (pain can toss a head about; only an impact snaps it back). one_rise: a fighter who got up once this beat, told getting up again later in the same part ('pushed herself up onto her feet' and then 'with a final heave, she lurched upright'): the second telling goes. favor: a fighter 'favouring' a part (or a side, a leg) nothing has hurt, or anything at all before anyone has been hurt, is cut. wet_source: 'the water from the aqua jet still dripped from her fur' names the Water move that really soaked her last. Each false = that one left alone; enabled false = none of them.

stand_signs._comment: Since build 253. The signs of hurt one fighter sees on the other leave out stepping, swaying and weight shifted off a leg when she is down (since build 252) and, with holder_down, when she is crouched over a fighter on the ground holding her there. holder_down false = only when she is down.

never_down._comment: Since build 252. A sentence that has a fighter 'get back up' or come 'back on her feet' when she has not been down once in this fight ('allowing Nerine to get back up too quickly', two beats in, with Nerine never down) is cut. Fights from saves before build 252 aren't checked (they didn't keep who had been down). enabled false = not checked.

wrong_owner._comment: Since build 251. Checks for what belongs to one fighter given to the other: a frost, burn or shock wound on the one that element never touched (Nerine 'feeling the sting of the icy wound' when Ripples took the Ice Fang); her 'own' move that only the other has used ('Ripples knew her Aqua Jet should have done more'); this beat's attack called by another move's name; her sight swimming when nothing struck her this beat and she isn't dazed; and (since build 252) a grip told the wrong way round ('Nerine's foot curled as Ripples' twin tails tightened round it', when the tails were Nerine's, on Ripples), and a chilled patch on one no cold touched. Such a sentence is cut (cut_first's 'isn't hers'). enabled false = not checked.

narration._worn_phrases_comment: worn_phrases: four-word phrases the story has used in min_beats or more beats of this fight ("the breeze turned the leaves", "a stark contrast to") are listed for the narrator before it writes, at most max_listed of them, so it finds fresh words. Words that describe the fighters, their moves and the arena are never counted. No extra model calls. enabled false = off.
narration._read_comment: read: the other way round from watch. After a blow, when neither dwell nor watch is told, the one who was hurt may get an extra part studying the one who did it (her stance, breath, injuries, face, where her eyes go, what she plans), and what each sign tells her. Needs the blow to leave the part very painful or worse, or her strength at max_strength % or less.

fading_thoughts._comment: A fighter under below_strength %: on chance of beats her italic thoughts come in fragments. The prose keeps its full detail.

camera._comment: Each part of a beat is told CLOSE (tight on bodies) or, on wide_chance of parts, WIDE (both bodies and the place). The dwell and watch parts are always close.

sounds._comment: Pained sounds. how_often: always (every hit that hurts gets a sound) | often | sometimes | rarely. write_out: how often a sound is written out as one italic word (*Hhk*, *Nngh*, *Hss*): often | sometimes | rarely | never. Every sound is described (kind, where from, pitch and shape) and fitted to each fighter's voice from fighters.json. /sounds changes them. enabled: false turns the note off. drawn_out: a part at from_level (very painful) or worse, on a fighter at or under from_pct % of her strength: her cries are long ones, an elongated yelp, a scream that goes on, a choking squeal (enabled false: off).

impact_motion._comment: How a blow that lands moves the body, now and then: a slash sweeping the struck limb along the cut or twisting her round, a blow knocking her back a step, a bite yanking her toward the biter, a blast shoving her back, lightning locking her rigid, a fighter on the ground rolled or shunted. chance per landed blow, + hard_bonus when it hits hard (hard_at % damage or more), + weak_bonus when she is under half strength. Never with a knockdown, throw or launch, never while she is pinned, held at point-blank or pressed against scenery, and she stays where the engine has her.

narration._context_window_comment: context_window: how many tokens the model reads at once (prompt + answer), for the narrator, the director and the reader. 20480 with Ollama set to OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 (half-size context memory) uses about what 12288 did before. If `ollama ps` shows any CPU share, step down to 16384; if it's still tight, 12288. The narrator trims the oldest story first when a prompt doesn't fit.
narration._check_tiers_comment: Checks are ranked. Anything wrong about what happened (a missing hit, attack, escape or escape blow, an invented fall or pin, wrong anatomy, pain past the limit) is always fixed. Tense, too much talk, the same hurt told again and blood with no wound are fixed by rewriting that paragraph (wording-only ones capped by style_repairs_max). cleanup_only: findings that never cost a model call: the program's cleanup handles them (filler swapped for a finished line, a leaked move label cut, a bare sound put in italics). reader_when: big = the second reading only on beats that change something (a pin starting or ending, a knockdown, a devastating blow, the arena, someone out); always = every beat.
narration._cut_first_comment: cut_first (since build 240): slips a paragraph rewrite rarely mends (the /checks tally and the build-238 logs: 'N of them still came back wrong' nearly every beat) are CUT straight away, with no model call: a paragraph whose every slip is one of marks loses just those sentences, and is written again only if that would leave it empty. marks are words from the check's finding: an invented wound, a game term or number, copied lines, a body part nobody in the fight has, blood with no wound, a thing not in this arena, a stock phrase. Remove a mark to have that slip rewritten again; enabled false = every slip is rewritten first, as before. Saves a minute or two a beat on a slow model.

marks: has never been down in this fight
nobody in this fight has that
nothing has cut or hurt her enough to bleed

narration._reader_timing_comment: reader_timing: when the second reading checks a beat that is written in parts. 'beat' (default): once every part is written, part by part, each against the text before it, with the same rules and limits; the narrator's long prompt then stays in the model's memory from one part to the next, which saves re-reading it (about 45 s a part on a partly-CPU setup). 'part': right after each part (the old order).

pain_tiers.label: minor
pain_tiers.reaction: Once the impact passes, little lasting effect; uses the part normally.

pain_tiers.label: sore
pain_tiers.reaction: Brief wince or grunt, shakes it off quickly. Still uses the part fully.

pain_tiers.label: hurting
pain_tiers.reaction: Clear pain: grimaces, rubs or checks the part, slightly slower to use it.

pain_tiers.label: very painful
pain_tiers.reaction: Strong pain: cries out, clutches the part, favors it, hesitates before using it. Opponent may notice and target it.

pain_tiers.label: excruciating
pain_tiers.reaction: Overwhelming pain: screams, may collapse or writhe, can barely or cannot use the part, struggles to think about anything else.

pain_tiers.label: devastated
pain_tiers.reaction: Past pain: the part barely works, trembles or goes limp, and every touch on it brings cries or broken whimpers.

pain_tiers.label: ruined
pain_tiers.reaction: Past devastated (since build 242; ruined.enabled): the part has stopped working. A ruined leg folds when weight goes on it, a ruined paw can't close, a ruined tail hangs. Her own movements jar it: a deep breath, a turn, her heartbeat. She can no longer hold anything in: the sounds come on their own, the shaking doesn't stop, and the one who did it can see it plainly.

pain_tiers.label: numb with shock
pain_tiers.reaction: Beyond pain: the part has gone numb, heavy, and strange, with shock spreading around it. New hits there land as a dull, heavy jolt and a cold rush of shock rather than sharp pain; she may not even feel them at first. Her breathing goes shallow and her face pale. It never makes her collapse on its own: overall strength still decides that.

health_tiers.label: fresh
health_tiers.reaction: Fully in the fight: quick, strong, upright, attacking freely. A badly hurt part is favored and guarded, but she does NOT collapse, go limp, or stop fighting; knocked down, she wants straight back up (how fast she manages it is the engine's to say).

health_tiers.label: winded
health_tiers.reaction: Breathing harder, but still fast and dangerous. Shakes off big hits within a moment (how fast she gets up is the engine's to say).

health_tiers.label: tired
health_tiers.reaction: Heavy breathing, a beat slower to rise and recover, but still attacking with real force.

health_tiers.label: exhausted
health_tiers.reaction: Gasping, slower and sloppier, takes a moment to get up, attacks lose some sharpness. Still conscious and still fighting.

health_tiers.label: spent
health_tiers.reaction: Barely able to stand, swaying, slow to rise, near collapse, but still conscious and still trying.
health_tiers._reaction_air_comment: reaction_air / reaction_down (optional, any tier): the same, for a fighter up in the air (no feet to stand on), or lying down or lying on top of a pin (no ground to drop to). Left out: reaction is used.
health_tiers.reaction_air: Barely able to stay up: her wingbeats ragged and failing, sinking and labouring back up, near collapse, but still conscious and still trying.
