health_tiers.reaction_down: Barely able to move, slow and shaking, near collapse, but still conscious and still trying.

health_tiers.label: past the limit
health_tiers.reaction: Running on nothing but will: wobbling, dropping to the ground between efforts, but still conscious. Only a completed pin puts her out.
health_tiers.reaction_air: Running on nothing but will: her wings failing, sinking between strokes and dragging herself back up, but still conscious. Only a completed pin puts her out.
health_tiers.reaction_down: Running on nothing but will: shaking, sagging limp between efforts, but still conscious. Only a completed pin puts her out.

health_tiers.label: greying out
health_tiers._comment: since build 242 (below_zero): the stages past zero are told apart. -20% to -50% of her full health: greying out.
health_tiers.reaction: Further past the limit than she should be able to go: the edges of her sight grey now and then and the sounds go far away; she sways, catches herself, drags herself back to the fight. Every move costs her visibly, and she knows it. Still conscious and still trying.
health_tiers.reaction_air: Further past the limit than she should be able to go: her sight greys at the edges, her wings miss beats and she drops and claws back up. Still conscious and still trying.
health_tiers.reaction_down: Further past the limit than she should be able to go: her sight greys at the edges, she goes slack and drags herself back. Still conscious and still trying.

health_tiers.label: her body overruling her
health_tiers.reaction: Below -50% of her full health: her will says fight and her body has stopped agreeing. Her legs give without warning, her hands shake too hard to grip well, sounds come out of her she doesn't choose; she fights in short bursts between moments where her body simply stops. Still conscious, still choosing to go on, and that choice is the whole story now.
health_tiers.reaction_air: Below -50% of her full health: her wings stop answering for moments at a time and she drops before they catch. Still conscious, still choosing to go on.
health_tiers.reaction_down: Below -50% of her full health: her body has stopped agreeing with her: limbs that won't push, shaking she can't stop. Still conscious, still choosing to go on.

holds._unrolled_words_comment: The director's own words for a beat can tell things the engine never rolled. Since build 230 a hold whose words throw her to the ground, slam her or pin her loses that clause (a takedown is its own move, with its own roll), and a breather's words about a grip on her ('wriggling free of Nerine's jaws') lose it once nothing holds her. blows (since build 283): a hold or a submission whose words strike her or drive her into the scenery first ('whips Ripples with the tail, and charges her into a tall pine') loses those clauses too, since those blows were never resolved; with no grip left in the words, the engine names the hold itself. blows false keeps them. enabled false keeps the words as written.
holds._backstop_comment: backstop (since build 260): a hold as bodies can really do it. A press with something that only pushes (her chest, her side, a knee, an elbow, her head) hurts only if something behind the one pressed pushes back: the ground she is down on, scenery she has been driven into (or named in pinned_against), or the holder's own arms, tails or legs wrapped round her body or neck hauling her into it (a bear hug, a sleeper from behind: the chest is the anvil, at anvil_share of its pressure). Otherwise the press is dropped from the hold: a chest against the back of a fighter standing in the open is contact, not a grip (the build-259 Ripples vs Nerine log: Ripples' chest 'pressing' Nerine's twin tails and shoulder). Her weight bearing down counts as backed (gravity pushes back), and so does every hold in the engine's own list. A hold that is nothing but such presses is refused, and the director tries again. Holds the director invents and submissions it invents are both checked. enabled false = not checked.
holds._grip_share_comment: grip_share (since build 260): one hold, one body's strength. One limb pressing on several parts splits its pressure (each x 1 / n to the power same_limb: her chest on two parts presses each at x0.71); every grip after the first is a lesser one (x second); and a hold has at most max_grips grips (the rest are left off). The five-grip body lock in the build-259 log did 36% damage in its first beat, three times the Aqua Jet before it. Submissions keep their own main and second grips. enabled false = every grip at its full severity.
holds._invented_check_comment: invented_check (since build 261): a hold the director writes, and a submission it invents, checked grip by grip against what the holder's limbs can really do; a grip that can't happen is left off (and a hold with none left is refused, so the director tries again). trapped: a limb caught in the other one's grip can't grip back with it. wrecked: a limb at ruined_at damage or worse (300 = devastated) can't take hold. busy: one limb grips one part and a pair (both paws, twin tails, her legs) two, counting what that limb already grips on anyone else. reach: one limb's (or one pair's) parts must be near each other on the body (not her neck and her foot; coils are long and are not limited). main_grip: an invented submission's main grip goes on a joint, a limb, the back, the tail or the neck, never an ear, a nose or a cheek. words: a submission from the engine's own list whose words (the director's) grip with a limb its grips don't use ('Nerine's twin tails wrap round her leg' for a heel hook turned with her arm and legs) is told in its own words instead. enabled false = none of it.
holds._busy_limbs_comment: busy_limbs (since build 266): a pair of limbs a fighter has locked in her own hold can't throw a blow as well: both legs in a triangle choke leave no knee to strike with, both paws bending an arm up in a chicken wing no punch (her jaws in a bite hold already couldn't bite). A grip with one of the pair ('her right paw') leaves the other free. The director is told to strike with something free or let go first. A Knee Strike now counts as a blow with the leg. enabled false = only the jaws are checked, as before. coils_use_tail (since build 311, on by default): a serpent's coils are her own body. With two coils or more wound round someone her tail is used up: no tail strike (Dragon Tail, Iron Tail, Aqua Tail). With one coil (usually her middle), the end of her tail is left loose tail_free_chance of the time (rolled once when the coil goes on): she can strike with it, at tail_free_power of the power (no body behind it). The director is told which. false = only the coils counted against the number she has, as before.
holds._held_no_launch_comment: held_no_launch (since build 311, on by default): a fighter held in the attacker's own grip or coils can't be knocked down, thrown or launched into the scenery by that attacker's blow: the grip holds her where she is (the build-310 log had Ripples hurled from inside Seraphina's coils into a pine). Throws and slams from a hold (manhandle) are not affected. enabled false = a blow can send her flying out of the grip, as before.
holds._holder_reach_comment: holder_reach (since build 266): from where she holds her in a submission, the holder's own blows land near the hold: a bite within bite_near steps of the parts she grips (a step = the next part along: upper back, then shoulder, neck, lower back), a paw, a knee or a tail within strike_near. Fired moves (a stream, a beam) aren't limited. In the build-264 log Nerine, on Ripples' back in a chicken wing, bit her foot. enabled false = as before.
holds._ground_reach_comment: A fighter LYING on the ground can't put a new grip on a standing fighter's high parts (lying: those regions, e.g. her head, neck, throat, shoulders and back): the director is told to grip low (a leg, a foot, a hip, her tail) or get up first. One SITTING up can reach everything but sitting (her head). A pin is checked by its own rule. enabled false = any part can be gripped from the ground, as before build 230.

lying: head same_target (since build 265): a limb already gripping HER in another hold counts as busy too (both paws bending her arm up in a chicken wing have nothing left for a new grip on her thigh; before, only grips on someone else counted); false = as before.

holds._held_reach_comment: Since build 249: a fighter on the ground held by someone (a submission, a hold) can only hurt the holder with what reaches her. The holder is where her grips are: tangled round her leg in a heel hook, she is down at her feet, out of reach of her jaws and paws; behind her in a chinlock, at her head. Each list names the held fighter's OWN body regions a weapon of hers reaches from the ground (bite: jaws, horns, a beak; arm: paws, claws, wings; leg: kicks, talons; tail): if no grip on her is in one of them, that weapon can't reach the holder and the move is refused (the director is told what does reach). sitting_adds: the regions she reaches besides, sitting up (leaning forward to her own legs). A bite must also land near the holder's gripping limbs (bite_near: how many regions away from them, 1 = the region next to it; -1 = anywhere). Moves fired across the gap (beams, streams) and whole-body moves aren't limited. On her feet (an upright hold) nothing is limited: the holder is right against her. enabled false = no limit, as before.
holds._release_as_escape_comment: A release the director writes for the HOLDER in words that are the held fighter fighting free ('head butts her in the nose, she writhes and twists to escape the hold'): before build 229 the hold simply ended. Now it is the held fighter's try at breaking out, and the end-of-beat break roll decides it. A release that says she lets go stays a release. enabled false goes back to ending it.
holds._second_limb_comment: A second limb put on a spot one of her grips already holds (her tails bound round the knee her jaws are on): before build 228 the new grip was folded into the old one and its pressure lost. Now both stay on, said together ('her jaws and twin tails'), and the hold presses at the stronger of the two plus add x the weaker. enabled false goes back to folding it in.
holds._keep_as_is_comment: keep_as_is (since build 239): a grip the director only KEEPS on (it was already there) presses as it was: its own tightening and holds.build do the climbing, and a grip the held fighter has worked looser (a near miss on her break-free roll) stays looser. A second limb added to the spot still adds its share, once (before build 239 it was added again every time the grip was kept, and a kept grip jumped back to the director's pressure). false = a kept grip presses at least as hard as the director's words say.
holds._free_blow_comment: free_blow: each beat a pin or a submission is on (not the beat it closes), the chance the one holding her gets a quick extra blow in with what she has free: one of her own moves (a jab, a bite, a Water Gun at point-blank) at power_mult of its power, costing energy_share of its energy. Rare and light, and separate from the punishment for a failed escape. 0 = never.
holds._comment: first_beat_damage: a hold (jaws on the throat, tails round a leg, coils) hurts from the beat it starts: the clamp itself lands as that much of one beat's pressure (1 = a full beat's worth, 0.5 = half, 0 = nothing until the next beat, as before build 93). Change live with /holdstart. A pin's presses have their own setting, pin.first_beat_damage.
holds._max_power_comment: max_power: a tightening grip (hold_ramp tightening) climbs to this power and no further ('crushing' is 25; coils cap at holds.coil.max_power; submissions are limited by submissions.max_beats). An easing grip that reaches 0 lets go.
holds._build_comment: build: a hold kept on without breaking (not easing, not a pin: a pin has pin.ramp) bites deeper every beat it stays on, at three rates. per_beat / max: into the gripped PART (its damage and wear): pressure x (1 + per_beat x beats held), up to max. health_per_beat / health_max: into her overall HEALTH, slower, so a long hold wrecks the limb before it empties her. pain_per_beat / pain_max: the PAIN she must resist to keep from tapping (submissions.tap.press), fastest. All on top of a tightening grip's own climb. Before build 216 one rate (0.08, up to 1.5) did all three. enabled false: only the grip's own ramp.
holds._health_cap_comment: health_cap: a hold (not a pin: a pin has pin.pressure_cap) on a worn-down part costs her overall health at most health_mult x for the wear (1.3 in build 217, 1.1 since build 218) (a blow on a soft part can cost up to the bracket's full health_mult). The part itself still takes its full damage and the pain still climbs, so a long hold ruins the limb and drives her to tap well before it empties her. Submissions take the lower of this and submissions.damage_cap.health_mult. enabled false: the bracket's full health_mult.

slow_bite._comment: A hold wears the part down before it tears into it. Every hold that presses (a submission, a coil, a grip; not a pin's own presses) has its damage multiplier flattened: as the part's resistance falls, the multiplier still climbs from what it was on the sound part, but only as (worn / sound) ** exp (0.5: a climb of x4 becomes x2; 1 = the full climb, as before build 224). Holds that don't grind already (submissions: submissions.grind) also bite at start_mult on a sound part, rising to the full bite on a worn-out one, and wear the part's resistance x wear_mult. Tested on a steady hip grip held 8 beats: the hip at 151% damage instead of 277%, its resistance at 15 instead of 40. So early beats mostly soften the part, and the damage comes later, once the resistance is going. enabled false = before build 224.

holds._coil_comment: A COIL (Wrap, Bind, Constrict, Tail Bind, or tails, coils or a body wound round her): a hold that tightens by `tighten` every beat (up to max_power) and leaves her CONSTRICTED while it holds (breath squeezed: no energy back, weak blows from trapped limbs, hardly any dodge). It is harder to wrench out of (break chance x break_mult). A coil can become a PIN, and a coiled fighter is easy to pin (an opening at least pin_opening of the time): the coiler bears her down in the coils and they become the pin's presses. A pin with coils in it takes her under by CONSTRICTION (her circulation cut off, her heart slowing, never stopping; she wakes as usual), and faster (x pin_fade_mult).

coil._energy_comment: energy (since build 298, on by default): keeping coils on her is WORK. Each beat it costs the coiler per_beat energy, plus per_beat_growth for every beat the coil has been on (she tires the longer she squeezes), x (her size / the coiler's) ** size_exp kept within size_min..size_max (a serpent many times her size squeezes more easily), x (1 + extra_coil) for each coil past the first; and a coiler gets no rest bonus while she coils (energy.rest_bonus), only the ordinary regen_per_beat. Under energy.tired_below she holds less surely: the break chance x tired_escape_mult. At spent_below or less she has to let go, unless she can feel the fight about to end (her tap or black-out chance at least near_chance, the grey closing in on her, or her health at near_health % or less): then she digs deep and hangs on, with chance hang_on, x hang_on_decay for each beat she has already hung on like that. Coils then last as long as the coiler has breath for them, not submissions.max_beats. /energy gives a fighter energy. enabled false = coils cost nothing to keep on, and a named coil submission ends at submissions.max_beats, as before.
coil._wear_first_comment: wear_first (since build 297, on by default): a coil works by pressure over time, so while the parts it lies on are sound it goes almost all into WEARING THEM DOWN (their resistance), with little damage and so little health: its damage x min_mult on a part in better than until % condition, climbing steeply (as the square) to the full bite at full_at % and below; its wear on the part x wear_mult. Early in a coil she is softened all round more than hurt; once the band is worn through, the coil does full damage (still under holds.health_cap), and her worn parts let the squeeze close in faster (constriction.compression). It takes the place of holds.slow_bite for coils. enabled false = coils use slow_bite like any hold, as before.
coil._size_comment: size (since build 275, on by default): A SERPENT MANY TIMES HER SIZE COILS HER MIDDLE. A coiler with no limbs (Milotic, Arbok) at least ratio times her length (sizes, in metres: by fighter name or species; a fighter missing from it is never affected) can't wrap one of her arms, legs, paws or tails alone: its body is thicker than her limb. When the director puts its coils only on her limbs (or her neck), the main coil goes round her belly or chest instead, at the strongest of that pressure, and each limb stays bound in under it limbs_too of the time (otherwise it slips free). A grab with its coils becomes a loop round her middle. An invented submission keeps its limbs, worked from coils round her middle. A coil already round her middle is left alone, and more grips can be added to it. Your own commands are never changed. escape_mult: wound round the middle by such a coiler (a hold or a pin), her chance to wrench or buck free is multiplied by this. With ratio 3: a Milotic (6.2 m) dwarfs a Buizel (0.7 m) or a Charizard (1.7 m) but not a Dragonite (2.2 m); an Arbok (3.5 m) dwarfs a Buizel but not an Absol (1.2 m). enabled false = coils go wherever they are put, as before.
coil._contest_comment: contest (since build 279, on by default): two fighters coiled round each other at once fight it out. Once both coils have been on for a beat, each beat they strain against each other and both spend energy_cost energy. stall_chance of the time both coils hold; otherwise one out-coils the other. The chance goes by each one's coil strength: her strength (0.25 + strength/100), her size in metres (holds.coil.size.sizes) to the power size_weight, her energy (0.5 + energy/200), and adrenaline_mult in a surge. The loser's coils are torn away, and the winner's tighten by tighten power and take over: the loser gets no roll to break them that beat. enabled false = both coils just go on side by side as before.

size._too_small_comment: too_small and takedown (since build 314): the other way round. A fighter the other one is too_small times the size of can't wind her tails or coils round that one's body or neck (a Buizel's two short tails round a serpent nine times her size): she can still bind a limb or the thin end of a tail, and the director is told so. And one takedown times her size she can't take down into a hold: the hold goes on with her upright, or not at all. 0 = no limit.

coil._scope_comment: Round her body (chest, belly, back) or her throat a wrap CONSTRICTS (her blood held back, her heart slowing, energy draining, it can put her out in a pin). Round one limb or a tail it only BINDS that limb (status_effects.bound_power_mult, bound_dodge_mult): no energy drain, no heart slowing.

holds._endurance_comment: endurance (since build 308, on by default): coils and submissions can run on longer. Each beat's break-free roll against one is x (mult x (her might / the holder's) ** strength_exp), kept within min..max, where might is her strength (0.25 + strength/100) x her size in metres ** size_weight x her energy (0.5 + energy/200). Against an equal she gets out less often (mult); much stronger than the one holding her, she can still tear out early, about as easily as before; it is a roll every beat either way. grow_mult: x how fast a submission's escape chance grows with every beat it is on. coil_energy_mult: x what keeping coils on costs the coiler (holds.coil.energy). shake_mult: x the chance a hard blow to the holder shakes her coils or her submission loose (holds.shaken). A submission that becomes a pin (submissions.becomes_pin_after) goes on by the pin's rules. A plain grip is not changed. enabled false = as before.
holds._break_comment: A plain hold (not a pin) has no time limit. Each beat after the one it starts in, once its pressure has landed, the held fighter gets one roll to wrench free. Chance = base x her condition against the holder's ((0.25 + her share of health) / (0.25 + the holder's), between 0.3 and 2.5) x how light the grip is (reference_power / the grip's power, between 0.4 and 1.5) x how hurt the gripping limb is (up to x2 at 150% damage) + per_beat for every beat the grip has already been on; x below_zero_mult once her health is below zero; half when paralyzed, x1.5 on an adrenaline surge; never above max; none while she is asleep or frozen. base 0 = no roll: only the director, a knockdown or a throw ends a hold. Change live with /holdbreak. shove_needs_standing (since build 253): she breaks free by shoving the holder back half a step only when both of them are on their feet; false lets it happen with either one lying down.
holds._shaken_comment: A fighter who is holding someone (a plain hold, not a pin) and is hit hard may lose her grip. One roll per attack that lands on her: chance = the share of her full health that attack cost x per_health_share, never above max. Attacks costing less than min_share of her health don't roll. At /scale 5 about one attack in six costs 2%+ of her health; a top-5% hit (about 5.5%) shakes a grip loose about a quarter of the time, a top-1% hit (about 10%) half the time. per_health_share 0 = never. Change live with /holdshake.
holds._loosen_comment: break.loosen_band / loosen_mult / strain_band: the break-free roll has near misses. A roll that misses the chance by up to loosen_band of it (chance 20% -> rolls from 20 to 32) LOOSENS the grip: it stays on, pressing at loosen_mult of its strength from the next beat. The next strain_band of it (32 to 60) is a visible struggle that changes nothing. Anything higher, she simply endures. loosen_band 0 = no loosening.

pin._control_comment: control (since build 332, on by default): a pin is only as good as what it holds. The engine looks at every point of contact for what it pins and what it pins it with: her legs (a thigh, a knee, a foot held; one side held is half her legs), her forelimbs (a shoulder, an arm, a paw), her middle (weight on her chest, belly or back: the pinner's own chest, body or weight counts in full, a paw or a knee there trunk_by_limb of it) and her head (a grip on her neck or head: jaws in full, anything else head_by_limb). Each way out needs something (a bridge her legs and middle, prying her forelimbs, a bite her head): the more the pin takes, the weaker her ways out, and her escape odds go x her two best ways' room over reference_freedom. Claws or talons in a grip dig in: x claw_mult per clawed grip, a failed try is punished on a clawed spot at claw_punish_mult, and breaking out she tears loose and the claws rake her (claw_tear severity, x pin.damage_mult; "" = no rake). Jaws on her neck: x jaws_neck_mult (she can't turn her head; any move risks the teeth); on a shoulder x jaws_shoulder_mult. Weight on her middle counts by size (holds.coil.size.sizes): x (her size / the pinner's) ^ weight_exp, between weight_min and weight_max, so a bigger pinner is far harder to shift and a smaller one easier. The whole is held between min_mult and max_mult. She tries the ways the pin leaves her more often (way_exp: how much a poor choice costs her). settle: a pin is not set the moment it goes on; she gets one scramble first (settle.base x her health share ^ strength_exp x the same multiplier, between min and max): if it works the pin never holds. Not rolled on a fighter taken down into the pin, one asleep, frozen, stunned, limp or paralysed, or for a second pinner piling on. health: her own condition decides how much the build costs her. A healthy fighter has the strength to fight even a tight pin: its tightness counts only healthy_share at full health, all of it as her health runs out (curve 2: it comes on mostly in the last half, so a tight pin at half health still leaves her a real fight) (and her health already sets the escape odds themselves, pin.struggle). And she fights with the parts it holds: the more hurt the parts under its grips are on average, the less she can do with them (x 1 / (1 + damage / part_scale), never under part_min). The settle scramble counts both the same way. Any pin the director builds is kept as it is: this only scores it. enabled false = the old odds (her health and the clock alone).

control._serpent_ways_comment: serpent_ways (since build 337): a pinned SERPENT has no legs or forelimbs to be held, so her ways out are her own: thrash her whole length, coil back round the pinner, roll, rear up, lash her tail, squirm, bite. Her tail counts like a pair of limbs (one tail part held is half of it; most of it held is all of it); weight on her middle, coils and jaws on her neck count as before. false = scored like any fighter, her missing limbs counted as held.
control._pinner_comment: pinner (since build 334, on by default): THE PINNER'S OWN CONDITION. Her overall health already loosens a pin (a hurt pinner holds less surely: x 0.8 to 1.4 on the escape odds); now it counts against the settle too (settle_health), and so do the parts of her body she pins WITH, read from each grip's words (her jaws for a bite, her forepaws, her hind paws or legs, her chest and belly for her weight, her tail): x (1 + part_max x their average damage over part_scale) on the pinned fighter's escape and settle odds. Hurt parts from note_from % damage are told to the story. enabled false = only her overall health, and only against escapes.

pin._wear_comment: wear (since build 334, on by default): HOW A PIN WEARS HER DOWN. THE ACHE: a pin hurts more the longer it is held, even where nothing has hurt her yet (held limbs cramp and burn, the weight on her ribs makes every breath work), so each beat of the fade (pin.fade) takes ache_start of a beat's worth on the pin's first beat, rising to ache_top by ache_beats beats held: she starts out fighting it hard and fades faster and faster. HER ENDURANCE: rolled once for each pin, between endurance_min and endurance_max (most often endurance_mode): the fade goes that much slower, so some pins she lasts longer and some she goes sooner. ESCAPES: longer pins give her more tries, so each try is x escape_mult (a pin is won about as often as before). With the ache, pin.fade.typical_beats is 7 (was 6): pins run about 7 or 8 beats, now and then 5 or fewer, now and then 10 to 12. CONTACT: what each grip is decides the harm its steady pressure does (x pin.damage_mult as before): claws or talons in her (claws) and teeth (teeth) in full; a plain paw, foot, knee or hand pressing a limb plain_limb (it holds her, it doesn't injure her: the ache does that); weight or a body bearing down on her middle, her head or her neck weight. Plain pressure does more the more hurt the part already is (all of it at hurt_full % damage: weight on a broken paw is agony), the heavier the pinner is against her (x (pinner size / hers) ^ heft_exp, between heft_min and heft_max) and the harder what she is pressed into (ground: spiky ground (thorns, gravel, shards, jagged rock, grating), hard (rock, stone, steel, ice), soft (sand, mud, grass, snow, water)), never above max. Coils and tails as before. A pin ends with her passing out from the pain or from the choke (a grip on her neck: her air or the blood to her head), whichever has gone further (as a chance: how far the choke has drained her against how far the pain has gone, the ache counting ache_pain toward the pain once it is at its worst). enabled false = the old fade and the old pressure.
pin._setup_comment: setup (since build 332, on by default): a NEW pin goes on quick or slow. quick: slammed on all at once, before she can react (the old way). slow: the pinner takes her time over a fighter who is clearly down, hurt and slow to rise (on the ground and stunned, dazed or limp, or down a beat already, or under hurt_below % strength): she settles her weight, eases her head over to clear the neck, brings her jaws in slowly, grips, presses, twists, and works the pressure up. Every grip goes on at start_mult of its pressure and reaches full over ramp_beats beats; the grips sit exactly where she wants them (pin control x placed_mult); the scramble before it settles (control.settle) is x slow_settle_mult on one slow to rise, but x alert_settle_mult on one who isn't, since the time it takes is time she gets. The director may ask for either ("pace"); when it doesn't, a pin on one slow to rise is slow slow_chance of the time. A takedown into the pin is always quick, and so is your own /pin unless asked. enabled false = every pin quick.
pin._neck_comment: neck (since build 317, on by default): most pins have a grip on the throat or the neck in them (jaws clamped on the throat, a forearm barred across it, coils looped round it). When a pin the director puts on has none, chance of the time the pinner adds one with what she has free (her jaws first; face-down, the back of her neck). In a pin it chokes slowly (body.air.pin_choke): it is a pin, not a choke. enabled false = only what the director put on.
pin._comment: Story pins. Each beat of a pin covers seconds_per_beat seconds of the clock. Every beat the engine rolls the pinned fighter's struggle: an escape, a partial break (they land a hit on the pinner), or a failed attempt the pinner punishes. Odds depend on both fighters' remaining health and fade as the clock runs down. Holding for duration_seconds makes the pinned fighter faint (if faint_at_end).
pin._make_sure_comment: make_sure: true (default) = when the pinned fighter passes out, the pinner keeps her grip and her weight on for a moment or two longer to be sure it isn't a trick, and only then lets go. Story only: it adds no damage. false = she eases off as soon as she feels her go limp. Change live with /makesure on|off.
pin._aftermath_comment: aftermath (since build 341, on by default; needs make_sure): the end of a pin told in full. When she passes out the pinner does not just hold a moment: she keeps the pin on for several seconds more, making sure of the win (her breathing, her eyes, nothing pushing back; she may ease a fraction and wait to see if anything comes), then lets go grip by grip (her jaws off the throat, her weight off the chest...), gets off and stands over her, and watches her slump: with the weight gone her body settles further, head rolling to one side, limbs falling slack, only her breathing moving. The story is asked for all of it, and when the passage leaves the slump out a short closing line puts it in. Story only: no damage. false = the short version (a moment longer, then she lets go).
pin._timing_comment: seconds_per_beat can be anything (1, 5, 10...). Pin pressure damage and struggle odds below are written for a 10-second beat (reference_seconds) and scale automatically, so shorter beats show more, smaller moments with about the same overall outcome. pin_words_per_second sets narration length per pin beat (capped at words_per_beat). Change live with /pinbeat and /pinlength.
pin._rules_comment: The director (not your /commands or typed directions) must follow these. require_downed: true = the opponent has to be on the ground before a pin; false (default) = a pin can come at any point, and a standing opponent is taken down into it. attacks_between_pins: attacks she must take after one pin attempt before the next (a fighter who hasn't been pinned yet has no wait). How OFTEN there is an opening for a pin is director.pin_urge. director_can_eliminate: false means only a completed pin puts a fighter out.
pin._double_pin_comment: A second fighter can join a pin that is already running (max_pinners in all): both press at once on the same clock. Each extra pinner multiplies the pinned fighter's escape and break-loose chances by double_pin_escape_mult. If one pinner is knocked away the pin carries on with the other.
pin._secure_comment: secure: when enabled, a pin can only be WON if the pinned fighter has at least min_parts body parts at part_damage % or more AND her strength is at or below max_strength %. Until then her escape chance is multiplied by unmet_escape_mult every beat, and if the clock runs out she kicks out at the last second final_kickout_chance of the time. Encourages spreading the damage. Toggle with /secure on|off.
pin._pinner_energy_comment: Holding a pin is work: pinner_energy_per_beat comes off the pinner's energy every pin beat, and a pinner who is tired (below energy.tired_below) holds less surely: the pinned fighter's escape chance x tired_pinner_escape_mult.
pin._aftereffects_comment: What a broken pin leaves behind: the fighter who got out is STIFF for stiff_beats (trapped limbs numb and slow: weaker blows, poor dodges) if the pin lasted at least stiff_after_beats; a pinner who held on cramped_after_beats or more comes off CRAMPED (slow to dodge) for cramped_beats. enabled false = off.
pin._pressure_cap_comment: A pin wears her down; it doesn't wreck her. Its steady pressure on each pressed part, and the extra press that punishes a failed struggle, never use more than these multipliers, however worn the part is: mult (damage; 0.45 = as if the part were only 'sturdy') and health_mult (health). Blows are not capped. Set enabled false for the old rule, where pressure on a ruined part hit as hard as a blow.
pin._damage_mult_comment: damage_mult scales ALL damage done to a pinned fighter by her pinner: the pressure on every point of contact each beat, the extra hit when the pinner punishes a failed struggle, any strike or technique the pinner lands on her while the pin runs, and /pinsuccess. 1 = full, 0.5 = half (the default since build 87), 2 = double. Change it live with /pinpower <number>; your choice is kept in my_settings.json, so it survives a new build.
pin._fade_comment: fade (on by default since build 98): a pin has NO fixed length. Each beat of a pin brings the pinned fighter closer to passing out by a varying amount (100 / typical_beats on average, between (1 - spread) and (1 + spread) times that), and she goes out when it reaches 100. So it usually takes about typical_beats beats, sometimes fewer, sometimes more, and nobody in the story can count toward the end: the narration has no clock, no seconds and no time left. A beat where she breaks loose for a moment counts for less (break_loose_mult); a double pin, and a fighter whose health is below zero, go faster; a fighter still above half her strength goes slower. It never takes fewer than min_beats. enabled false = the old rule: a clock that ends at duration_seconds, with the seconds marked in the story. Change live with /pinfade.

fade._sim_comment: sim (since build 317, on by default): the pin wears her down by what it really does to her. The pain under the press counts the whole way (x 1 + pain x the worst pressed part's damage over 300), not only past agony; claws, talons or teeth driven into a paw or a foot, where the nerves bunch, x nerve; a grip on her neck in the pin drains her blood or her air (body.air, at only body.air.pin_choke of a real choke's rate: it is a pin, not a choke) and adds x 1 + choke x how far gone she is, and once it has run out she passes out. What she passes out from (the choke or the pain) follows which of them has gone further. A pin still never ends in a tap. false = as before.
fade._cause_comment: A fighter held to the end of a pin goes out from one of two things, and the story is told which: the CHOKE (a grip on her neck or throat) or the PAIN (the worst-hurt part under the press). With no grip on her neck it is always the pain. With one, pain_out_share is how often the pain gets there first anyway (less when nothing under the press is at least very painful). At 0.22 about 3 pass-outs in 10 are by pain overall at a high damage scale; raise it for more, lower it for fewer (0 = always the choke when there is one; 1 = always the pain). pain_mult: when the worst-hurt part under the press is in agony (150% damage or more), each beat takes her under up to this much faster.
fade._neck_blood_comment: neck_blood (since build 335): pressure on her neck in a pin (jaws round her throat, a paw or a forearm on it, weight across it) USUALLY ends the pin by the BLOOD: the arteries squeezed shut, the blood to her head cut off (told as a blood choke; when her windpipe was pressed too, the story may say her breath came short, but the blood is what takes her). Not always. pain_share: at most this often the PAIN gets there first, more the worse the parts under the press are hurt (from 90% damage, all of it at 240%) and the longer the ache of the pin has gone on (up to half of it). air: by the kind of grip on her neck, how often it is her AIR that goes first instead (air = a press across the front of her throat, both = jaws or hands closed round it: then told as air and blood together, blood = something closing on the sides). In a pin a press on the front of her neck drains the blood to her head too, at press_blood of a blood choke's rate. About 7 in 10 neck pins end by the blood, the rest by her air or the pain. false = the choke or the pain by which has gone further, and the kind of choke by the grip, as before.

pin._first_beat_comment: first_beat_damage: how much of one beat's pressure a pin's presses deal on the beat the pin starts (0 = none: the pin starts hurting on its next beat; 1 = a full beat, still times damage_mult). Change live with /pinstart.
pin._restrain_comment: restrain: when the pinner lands an attack on the fighter she's pinning (a claw in a nerve cluster, a trapped paw, a ground-down joint), there's a chance it also leaves her RESTRAINED for beats beats: her escape chance is multiplied by escape_mult, but only fully once her strength is at or below full_effect_below %; a healthy fighter barely notices it (it scales in between).

struggle._odds_comment: attempt_chance: how likely the pinned fighter is to try at all each beat. Escapes stay LIKELY while she has more than escape_easy_above % of her health: each try works escape_chance of the time at full health, sliding to escape_chance_at_edge at that mark (65% -> 40% by default). Below it the chance halves for every escape_halves_every points of health she loses: about 28% at 40% health, 17% at 25%, 10% at 10%, 7% at 0, and on into negative health. Over a whole 60-second pin that works out to roughly 95% escapes from full health, 70% from 65%, 55% from half, 35% from a quarter, 10% from almost nothing. That is the 'escape %' on the pin clock line (before the clock's fade and the pinner's own condition). partial_chance: if the escape roll fails, her chance to break loose for a moment and hit the pinner; it falls on the same curve. escape_steps true = drops in whole steps instead of smoothly. escape_easy_above 0 = the old curve (halving from full health; use escape_halves_every 25 with it). A hurt pinner raises the odds a little; late in the pin (after fade_from) they fade.
struggle._escape_hit_comment: escape_hit: when she breaks free, the blow that frees her also lands on the pinner (somewhere a pinned fighter can reach: face, neck, chest, belly, forelimbs) at escape_severity (light, solid, heavy, brutal; heavy is about a named move). false = she just slips out and the pinner is unhurt.
struggle._below_zero_comment: escape_halves_every_below_zero: once the pinned fighter's health is BELOW ZERO, her escape and break-loose chances halve again for every this-many points (percent of her own full health) she is under zero. 5 = at 10% under zero an escape is about four times less likely than at zero, at 20% under about sixteen times. A large number (1000) switches it off.
struggle._escape_points_comment: escape_points: below escape_easy_above, the chance one escape attempt works (before the clock's fade and statuses) follows these [health %, chance] points, in straight lines between them and flat past the lowest. Empty = the old halving curve (escape_halves_every). escape_floor / break_loose_floor: however hurt she is and however long the pin has run, an attempt never has less than this chance (never impossible). escape_floor_at_minus_25 (since build 332): below zero health the escape floor sinks toward this, reached a quarter of her health under zero: a small chance, never none.
struggle._buff_comment: After she breaks loose, her escape chance is multiplied by break_loose_buff for the next break_loose_buff_beats beat(s). It doesn't stack; another break-loose just restarts it.
struggle._keep_jaws_comment: keep_jaws: when she breaks out of a pin that had the pinner's jaws in it, the chance those jaws hang on: the rest of the pin is gone, but the bite goes on as an ordinary hold (shown on screen and told to the story; she can wrench out of it like any hold). Not if the pinner is thrown down. 0 = every grip always comes off.
struggle._pinner_down_comment: pinner_down_chance: when the pinned fighter breaks out, the chance the pinner is thrown down beside her instead of being shoved off on her feet. She then rolls to get up from the next beat like anyone else. 0 = the pinner always keeps her feet.

pin._takedown_comment: takedown: a standing fighter is taken down into a pin in one of several ways (the mix is under variety -> takedown). hard_landing_chance: how often the landing itself hurts: landing_parts parts on the side she lands on take a landing_severity blow from the ground before the pin closes. 0 = takedowns never hurt (the old rule).
pin._against_comment: against_escape_mult: a pin jammed against something in the arena (a wall, a boulder) is this much harder to break out of. The director is offered that shape rarely (director.pin_shape_weights.wall_choke).

second_wind._comment: Breaking out of a pin held after_beats or longer: chance of FURY for beats (harder blows: status_effects.fury_power_mult).

pin._openings_from_beat_comment: openings_from_beat: the first beat a pin opening can be rolled (1 = from the start, a rare lucky opening; 2 = never on the opening beat, before anyone has traded a blow: in 300 simulated fights that moved Nocturne from about 60% to 69%, so it is off). Your own commands can always pin.

contacts._comment: How many points of contact a pin aims for (weights; it never goes below what the pin shape itself uses). Each pin is filled out from whatever the pinner still has free: jaws on the neck (if nothing else is there), her chest or weight on the front (her back if face-down), her paws gripping the forelimbs with the claws in, her feet or hind paws on the flanks, her tails across the legs. Nothing is used twice. min: a pin the director writes with fewer points of contact than this is filled out the same way (so a small fighter doesn't pin a big one with one grip).

pin._ramp_comment: ramp: a pin's held pressure builds the longer each press stays on: x(1 + per_beat x beats held), up to max (0.12 a beat, at most x1.6, reached on the 5th beat).

getting_up._comment: A fighter on the ground tries to get up at the end of each beat after the one she went down in. Score = her strength share / (1 + damage of her worst 3 limb parts / limb_damage_halves_at), plus per_beat_down for each extra beat down, plus a little luck (adrenaline +0.2, paralyzed -0.3). Score >= thresholds[0]: up on the first try; [1]: second try; [2]: third try; lower: fails all three and stays down. After max_beats_down she always makes it on the third try.
getting_up._sit_up_comment: sit_up_chance: when a fighter on the ground fails to get up, the chance she at least makes it to SITTING (still down; front and back both in reach). 0 = a failed get-up always leaves her lying.
getting_up._fall_comment: fall_chance: when a failed get-up try drops her back down HARD (her legs give out, or she slips), the chance the drop hurts: the limb that gave out (or what she lands on) takes a small jolt of fall_power. Sinking back dizzy or out of breath never hurts. 0 = failed tries never hurt.

evasion._comment: Dodges: the engine rolls whether a single-target or spread attack misses. Chance = base x (0.4 + 0.6 x the defender's strength share) x a penalty for hurt legs, feet, and tails, capped at max. Chilled halves it, low energy x0.7, adrenaline x1.3, a paralyzed attacker x1.3, spread moves x0.5. Nobody dodges while down, pinned, or paralyzed, or a whole-body move. counter_chance: after a dodge, the chance to land a counter-hit. Your own /commands always land.
evasion._chain_comment: chain_mult: in a chain (two or three attacks by one fighter in one beat, each leading into the next) a link that lands leaves her rocked: her chance to dodge the next link is multiplied by this. A link she dodges ends the chain.
evasion._leg_manners_comment: leg_manners: the ways of dodging (rules.json variety.dodge) that need her legs. Their weight is divided by (1 + her worst-hurt leg's damage / leg_manner_halves_at), so a fighter on wrecked legs ducks or twists rather than springing back or stepping aside. Not in the air (she dodges on her wings).

status_effects._comment: from_move_type: a move of that type that lands may give the target this status for this many beats. paralyzed: weaker attacks (paralyzed_power_mult), no dodging, worse pin escapes. chilled: half the dodge chance. soaked: Electric hits do soaked_electric_mult more (anyone the director places in water, or who lands in water, is soaked too). flinched: can't attack next beat.
status_effects._from_move_type_always_comment: statuses from from_move_type that a move of that type gives even when it has effects of its own (a Water Pulse that may confuse still soaks her): the plain facts of the element, not a side effect.
status_effects._stiff_comment: stiff (after breaking out of a pin) and cramped (after holding a long one): power and dodge multipliers.
status_effects._constricted_comment: constricted (held in coils): power of what she throws with her trapped limbs, dodge, and energy lost each beat. sputtering (water in her mouth): power, dodge, pin escape.
status_effects._more_comment: Statuses from moves.json moves: asleep and frozen can't act or dodge (and barely fight a pin), confused may hurt herself instead of attacking (confused_self_hit_chance), burned hits a little weaker (burned_power_mult) and takes burn_power on a hurt spot each beat, poisoned loses poison_health_pct % of her max health each beat.
status_effects._head_body_comment: (since build 293) what the head and body effects do (moves.head, moves.body_jolts): dodge multipliers (stunned can't dodge at all), aim misses (seeing_double, eyes_watering, swollen_eye: her blows slide off what she aimed at more), power (wobbly on everything; jaw_rattled on bites; dead_arm on punches and claws; limping on charges; back_spasm and ribs_aching on everything), getting up (taken off her get-up score), and legs_gone_bear_down (added to a hold's chance of bearing her down while wobbly or with a dead leg).

energy._comment: Stamina (0-100). Each move costs energy: by target type here, or a move's own "energy" in fighters.json. Everyone regains regen_per_beat each beat, plus rest_bonus if they sat the beat out. Below tired_below a fighter dodges worse. The director can't use a move she can't afford; your /commands always work.
energy._fresh_breath_min_strength_comment: The notes' stamina line says 'fresh breath' (energy 70+) only while her overall strength is at least fresh_breath_min_strength % (the 'fresh' tier: a winded or tired fighter reads 'breathing hard'); below breath_back_below_strength (an adrenaline refill on a spent body) it says her breath is back but not her strength. Past her limit (below 0%) it always reads gasping, and while the wind is knocked out of her it says so. Labels only.

_ruined_comment: ruined (since build 242): a damage tier past devastated (the pain tier 'ruined', at min %, 500 by default; 'numb with shock' stays above it when on). It isn't only a word: a ruined LEG folds under her when she puts weight on it (buckle_chance a beat: she catches herself, off balance for a beat, and doesn't go down); any ruined part is jarred by her own movement now and then (jar_chance: a deep breath, a turn, told in the story, no damage); getting up costs her getup_penalty for each ruined leg (up to two); a grip on a ruined part adds tap_pain to the pain she must resist in a submission match; and the story is told she can't hold anything in any more, and the one who did it sees it. jar_cooldown (since build 243): after a jar is told, no other for that many beats, so it doesn't fill every passage. enabled false = no ruined tier: those parts stay devastated, as before.
_below_zero_comment: below_zero (since build 242): what happens as her health falls past zero, by stage (at: her health as a % of her full, 0, -20, -50 by default; she is in the lowest stage she has reached). She is never stopped from fighting by it. Each stage: power (her blows land at that much), getup (added to her get-up roll: less to rise with), tap_mult (in a submission match, her tap chance x that), grey_chance (each beat, her sight may grey out for a beat: she sways, dodges at status_effects.greyed_dodge_mult and hits at greyed_power_mult), second_surge (with her one adrenaline surge long spent, each beat the chance of a second wind of second_surge_beats, once a fight). refuse_moment: the first time she goes below zero, the story gives her one passage of refusing to go down (her own thoughts, the one she is fighting, what she came here to do), once a fight. The story is told each new stage as she reaches it (and health_tiers tells it apart: past the limit, greying out, her body overruling her). health.collapse still has her body give out on its own now and then below zero. grey_cooldown (since build 243): after her sight greys, it can't again for that many beats. part_ramp (since build 244): below zero health, the damage each blow or grip does to her BODY PARTS is multiplied, more and more the deeper she goes: 1 + per_10 for every 10% of her full health below zero (0.08: x1.4 at -50%, x1.8 at -100%, x2.6 at -200%), never above max. Her health loss is unchanged; worn-out parts just give way faster, so pain builds and the next tap comes sooner. only: where it applies: 'taps' (a submission match needing more than one tap, the default), 'submission' (every submission match), 'all' (every fight). part_ramp.enabled false = off. enabled false = none of it (the health tiers stay).
_low_health_comment: low_health (since build 246): what a fighter at the very end of her strength (at_pct % of her full health or less) does by herself, each a told event, at most once every cooldown beats. idle: on her feet and left alone that beat (she neither acted nor was acted on), chance she shows it: sways, leans on something nearby, blinks blood away, spits, tests a badly hurt leg, fights for breath; the other one sees it and closes in, waits or circles. squirm: down and free (not the beat she went down or got up), chance she drags herself toward the other or away, claws at the ground, or curls round her worst part. tells: chance her body gives her away: shaking, ragged breath, or (a limb at dead_limb_damage % or more) a limb that doesn't answer, so moves thrown with it can't be used next beat (the director is told). last_stand: after her once-a-fight last-stand blow (moves.last_stand: everything she has left in one blow), she is wide open the beat after (dodge x open_dodge_mult). (Build 246 had a separate last stand of its own here; build 247 folded it into moves.last_stand, which already did the blow.) foe_read: chance the other one reads her state (she's done, finish it; careful, she has one more in her; why is she still standing, only while she stands below zero), told as a thought and passed to the director. enabled false (here or on any part) = off.

below_zero._tap_comment: tap (since build 328, on by default): below zero, giving in comes sooner. A hold's build-up to a tap or a pass-out (finish.submission.tap.blend ramp_beats) runs per_100 faster for every 100% of health below zero, at most max times as fast (with these numbers x2 at -100%, x4 from -300%), and (blended) the stages' tap_mult now counts with tap.blend on too (it was skipped). Before, a fighter at -6000% health in a submission match was still asked to tap at 0-8% a beat. enabled false = as before.

adrenaline._comment: The first time a fighter's strength drops below below_strength %, she gets one surge for this many beats: power_mult on her attacks, escape_mult on pin escapes, better dodging, and an energy refill.

recovery._comment: After a fighter is put out (a completed pin, or /eliminate), they slowly come around through these stages, one at a time. Each beat after min_beats_per_stage, the chance to move up a stage is chance at full health, halved for every halves_every points of health lost (never below min_chance). Getting up doesn't change who won.

setup._comment: setup (since build 282, on by default): the questions asked before a run begins. First: Enter begins at once as things are; a preset number or name sets that kind of match and then asks only the arena and the fighters; o goes through every question in questions, in this order. WHERE AND WHO: scene (the arena), fighters (who fights), variants (which version of a fighter, when she has more than one), players (whether you play as one fighter, several or all, and then with which dice: fair, strict or free). THE MATCH: intro (the opening passage on or off), match (the kind of match: a preset), taps (how many tap-outs win, in a submission match), pins (how often pin openings come, when there are pins). THE STORY: plan (close, dominate, comeback, winner...), focus (where attacks aim), targeting (how many parts an attack catches), reason (why they fight). BALANCE: length (about how many beats), damage (the damage scale). THE WRITING: traits (traits and quirks on or off), character (personality, history and relationships on or off), words (swearing and gore), story (how much is written each beat: short, normal, long), hazards (the arena acting by itself), polish (Venice, when you have a key). ANYTHING ELSE: more (any other /commands, one per line), begin (Enter to go beat by beat, or a number of beats for the director to run on its own). A preset at the first question asks only scene, fighters, players and begin. Enter keeps what is set at every question, and any /command works at any of them (one that starts the fight ends the questions). Take a name out of questions to skip it. enabled false = only the arena question (scene.ask_at_start), as before. (since build 323) weather (after the arena: the weather over the whole fight: the arena's own, random, clear or a kind; not asked indoors) and body (THE BODY: each part of the simulated body on or off: air, heart, blood, adrenaline, tissue, bones, footing, heat, mind, limbs). Both are saved to my_settings.json, as /weather and /body do. A questions list kept in my_settings.json from before still gets these two, where they go; skip: a list of questions never to add that way.

presets._comment: presets (since build 282): /preset <name> sets a whole kind of match at once, each line as /set would (saved to rules.json and my_settings.json; add nosave for this session only). /preset lists them, /preset <name> ? shows what one changes without changing anything. Add your own: a name, a description, and its settings (rule path -> value). anything also sets submissions.becomes_pin_after 0, so a submission stays a submission and can end in a tap (held 4 beats it would otherwise become a pin, before a tap could come); pins sets it back to 4.

submission.description: A submission match: only a tap-out or a pass-out ends it. No knockouts, no pins.

submission3.description: A submission match won by the third tap-out, from three different body parts (two for a serpent).

knockout.description: A knockout match: only a knockout blow ends it. No pins, no submissions.

pins.description: A pin match: a pin held to the end of its clock wins, and a knockout blow can still end it. No submissions.

anything.description: Whatever happens: a knockout blow, a pin held to its end, or a tap-out (or a pass-out) in a submission, whichever comes first.

reacting._comment: reacting (since build 336): how each fighter REACTS to being hurt, her temperament under pain, set in fighters.json as "reacting": {trait: 0-1, "sensitive": {...}} (reacts.py). Traits: stoic (keeps it in: her reactions shown up to 2 sizes smaller and quieter), expressive (shows everything: a size bigger), vocal / quiet (how much sound), and how she MOVES with pain: squirmer (writhes and squirms), recoils (jerks away from it), curls (folds round the hurt), rigid (locks up, goes still), lashes_out (turns the pain straight back on her attacker); sensitive: kinds of damage (blunt, claw, blade, bite, blast, fire, cold, shock, mind, grip) or words in a part's name (ear, tail, paw...) x how much more (over 1) or less (under 1) she reacts to them. Each landed blow gets one reaction: barely, small, marked, big or violent, from the real thing: blow x the part damage it added over blow_ref, part x how hurt that part now is (/100), overall x how hurt she is (/50), all x her sensitivity, cut at steps. Her temperament changes what shows, never past what is real: a part at agony_at damage or more (150 = 'excruciating', the story's own pain word), a blow adding huge_blow or more, or her health under spent_below % always shows at least big; a big real reaction can be hidden by one size at most. How she moves comes from the kind of damage (fire makes anyone recoil, a shock locks her rigid, cold curls her up, a grip makes her squirm) plus her traits; held or down she has nowhere to jerk away to, so she squirms or locks up. The narrator is told the size, the movement and the sound. In a pin her nature is told too (a squirmer never still, a stoic quiet then a sudden heave). pin_effects: in a pin a squirmer wears herself out faster (x 1 + squirm_fade) and tries to escape more often (x 1 + squirm_tries); a stoic wears slower (x 1 - stoic_fade); enabled false = told only. false = no reaction traits at all.
reacting._finished_comment: finished (since build 336): a big reaction when she is under below % health (or a violent one at any health) can leave her FINISHED for the moment: she goes down if she was standing, and for beats beats (between the two, rolled) she can't act, dodge, get up or fight a grip off, a pin opening is all but certain (director.pin_urge.helpless), a submission opening at least sub_opening, her resistance to a tap x resist_mult, and a knockout likelier. It looks like her nature: lying still (a stoic, or one who locks up), curled round the pain in agony, or thrashing and squirming on the ground. Chance: big or violent, x 1 + how far under below she is (up to x3), / her toughness, x adrenaline_mult with adrenaline running, at most max. Never again within cooldown beats of the last. It always passes. enabled false = never.

styles._knockout_match_comment: knockout_match (since build 338): in a knockout-only match (finish.knockout_only with finish.no_pins) only a knockout ends the fight, so every fighter reaches for her heavy blows: her big moves x big, her quick light ones x quick, status moves x status (the director is told; /simulate weighs her moves by it). No fighting style steers her off a big blow there (a swarmer still swarms, but with her heavy shots in it). Works whether or not styles are on. false = as in any other match.
styles._move_on_comment: move_on (since build 341, on by default): WHEN SHE LEAVES A PART FOR ANOTHER. A blow aimed at a part she has had enough of moves, chance of the time (x 1 + her opportunist or dismantler strength x style), to the part beside it that is worth it most (the most hurt of its neighbours still under ruined_at: stomach to chest, ribs or flank; an arm to the shoulder), or the worst-hurt part left if none. She has had enough of a part when: it is RUINED (ruined_at damage or more: little more to take there, and the pain has stopped telling her she is hurting it), it is GUARDED (her opponent is shielding it, moves.guarding_wound: guarded x the chance), or she has gone there streak times running (her opponent is reading it). The opportunist's worst-hurt pull also skips a ruined part ruined_skip of the time. The director is told why she moved (the story: a fresh target, the covered part left alone for now). She can still come back to it. It is only ever a chance, about even with the defaults: a fighter with a strong opportunist or dismantler style moves on from a ruined or over-used part about half the time and keeps hammering it the other half (one with neither style a little less than half), and she can always come back to it later. Raise chance for more moving on, lower it for more repeated attacks. false = she keeps going to the same part as before.
styles._comment: styles (since build 335): FIGHTING STYLES, how each fighter likes to fight beyond the moves she favours. Set per fighter in fighters.json as "fighting": {style: how strongly, 0 to 1}. Each style below can be switched off (enabled false) or retuned. A style does four things: (1) MOVES: what she reaches for, by kind of move (close, ranged, big, quick, breaker = a heavy blunt blow that wears a part down, cutter = claws, blades and teeth that tear into it, bite, charge, wide = catches several parts, hold, status), x the number at full strength (a style at 0.5 gets half of the change), with more by the moment in `when` (down, pinned, grab, holding, open = staggered/off balance/dazed..., against = driven against something, hurt = under 40% health, fresh = over 70% and nothing wrong). The director is told it each beat (FIGHTING STYLE) and the no-model fights in /simulate weigh her moves by it. (2) AIM: how often (x her strength in the style) a blow aimed somewhere else is moved to where the style wants it: dismantler = the one part she is taking apart (kept until it has done_at damage, then the part beside it least hurt so far; heavy blows first while it is still sound, cutting ones once it is worn under soft_at % condition), opportunist = her worst-hurt part (from hurt_from damage), wear_down = somewhere still fresh, head_hunter = her head, body_worker = her body, hobbler = her legs. Never onto a part she can't reach (the usual reach checks put it back). (3) CHANCES: how much likelier a grab, a chain, a pummel, a feint or a throw/knockdown is (x the number at full strength). (4) A few small engine effects, named in each: brunt/shed (dismantler: when a blow catches several parts, the one she is taking apart takes brunt more, the rest shed less), point_blank (setup_artist: a big blow on a fighter who is down, held, pinned or driven against something), on_down (ground_pounder: close blows on a fighter who is down), wear (wear_down: her heavy blows wear the part's resistance down more), counter (counter_puncher: her counter after a dodge), devastating (opportunist: a devastating blow on an opening), slip (out_fighter: slipping a grab). enabled false = no styles at all.

dismantler.label: takes her apart one part at a time

traits._comment: traits and quirks (since build 280, on by default): how each fighter fights, set in fighters.json. traits is a set of multipliers on today's rolls, 1.0 = as before: speed (her chance to dodge, to counter after a dodge, to meet a move with her own), hold (how hard her grips bite when they close, and how hard they are to break), escape (her chance to break a hold or escape a pin), toughness (how easily she is staggered or rocked: the chance is divided by it), stamina (what her moves cost her: divided by it), striking (landing where she aims: the miss chance is divided by it; and her chance of a devastating blow), learning (1.4 or more: she reads a move after seeing it once, not twice). favors (fighters.json): move name -> how much she prefers it (the director is told her favourite and her seldom-used moves; /simulate weights its picks by them). style: a sentence for the director. quirks: named rules of her own, each below with its numbers, each switchable (enabled false). Balance: fighters without traits are as before; the pairs were simulated after setting them. enabled false = no traits or quirks at all (fighters.json keeps them).

quirks._comment: stubborn: once past her limit in a submission her tap chance is x tap_mult (she holds out longer). out_of_depth: new to submission holds: her escape is x start at first, + per_hold for every hold she has been caught in this fight, up to x1. cocky: after a blow of hers that did big_hit damage or more, chance that her next attack overreaches (sloppy, half force, off balance), while her strength is until_below % or more. water_born: in the water her speed and escape x mult. ring_sense: experience: her chance of overcommitting when tired x mult. clinch_fighter: her free-blow chance while she holds someone x free_blow_mult. works_the_hold: her holds tighten ramp_add more each beat. predictable: an opponent reads her moves after one sight of them, not two. weak_paw_grip: a grip she makes with her paws presses x power_mult and is x break_mult easier to break (jaw grips are normal). disaster_sense: the chance of a devastating blow landing on her x mult. ambusher: her moves (moves) land devastatingly x mult more often on someone staggered, off balance, dazed, flinching or down. hates_water: soaked or in the water, her speed and striking x mult. overwhelming: her moves of base power big_from or more hit x power_mult and are x dodge_mult easier to dodge (a big wind-up). patient_constrictor: her strength in a contest of coils x contest_mult. unshakeable: her toughness x mult.

director._comment: initiative: once one fighter has made initiative_after attacks in a row (and an opponent still has at least initiative_min_strength % of full strength), each beat there's a chance the director is told to shift the momentum: initiative_chance at first, +initiative_step for every extra attack in the streak, up to initiative_max. Streaks can run long, just not usually. With /plan dominate, the winner's streaks shift only initiative_dominate_factor as often. initiative_after 0 turns it off.
director._words_to_parts_comment: words_to_parts (since build 261): the director's words name one of her parts and its action another (told to work her right hip, it wrote 'wrapping tightly around Nerine's left knee'): the engine resolves the action's parts, so a part of hers named as hers in the words ('Nerine's left knee') is put right to the action's part. What the attacker uses is never changed. enabled false = the words stay as written.
director._flavor_words_comment: flavor_words: the author's or director's one-line direction for an action is kept to at most this many words (a label, not a paragraph); a longer one is cut there (an order cut mid-sentence reads wrong, so keep this generous).
director._pin_urge_comment: How often there is an OPENING for a new pin on a fighter, rolled each beat before the director chooses (the director can only start a pin where there is one; your /commands and typed directions always can). standing: on her feet with at least weak_below % of her strength (rare, but a pin can come at any point). downed: knocked down, same strength. weak_standing / weak_downed: under weak_below % of her strength; these then climb toward max as she nears 0. helpless: asleep or frozen. When there is an opening and you just press Enter, the director is told to go for it.

pin_urge._comment: scale (set with /pins): every chance below is multiplied by it, so 0.5 = about half as many pins and 2 = more; 0 = the director never starts a pin. The chance of a pin opening on a fighter each beat. It follows how hurt she is: standing / downed_fresh at full strength (knocked down while still strong barely raises it: she is up again in a moment), rising along a curve to weak_standing / weak_downed at weak_below % strength, then toward max as she nears nothing. Each part at hurt_at %+ damage adds hurt_bonus (up to hurt_cap): her opponent knows where she is hurt. No time factor: pins come more often late in a fight only because she is more hurt by then. helpless: asleep or frozen.

director._game_plan_comment: Each fighter comes in with a plan: one zone of the other's body she means to take apart (legs, neck, head, core, the belly, the back, arms, wrists, ankles, tail, weighted by zones; in a submission match the weights are multiplied by match_weights, and the plan is to finish with a hold on it; neck 0.75 since build 234, so a plan to choke her is rare). Rolled once at the start, from a copy of the dice, so it never changes the fight's own rolls. A fighter with a /focus has her focus as her plan. On nudge of the beats (0-1) the director is reminded of it, as a pull and not an order. The narrator shows it with narration.plan_notes. enabled false: no plans.
director._focus_comment: Where attacks aim (set with /focus). '*' = everyone; a fighter's name = that attacker only. focus_strength (0-1) = how often an off-target pick gets moved onto the focus zone; 0 = a prompt nudge only.
director._plan_dominate_comment: plan_dominate (since build 277, on by default): /plan dominate <name> makes her opponent rarely fight back. Each beat the opponent gets a beat of her own (an attack, a grab, a pin on the winner) only with chance rival_turn_chance; on the other beats the director is told the beat is the winner's, and an attack it still gives the opponent becomes a struggle against the grip on her, or a step back. Her chances to fight back on the dice (dodging, countering after a dodge, meeting a move with her own, breaking a hold, escaping a pin) are multiplied by defence_mult. A direction you type yourself is never changed. enabled false = /plan dominate is only the director nudge it was before.
director._throat_bite_comment: Now and then the director gets an optional idea to bite the neck or throat: throat_bite_chance per beat in open fighting (when someone has Bite, Crunch, Ice Fang...), throat_bite_pin_chance per pin beat. 0 turns it off.
director._sustain_comment: sustain_chance: each beat with no direction from you (and no pin running or about to start), the chance the director is pointed at a HELD ranged attack: a stream or beam (any move marked sustainable) kept on the target for 2-4 pulses and pressing her against something in the scene, which adds environmental damage each pulse and may break. 0 = never suggested (the director can still choose it).
director._double_pin_chance_comment: double_pin_chance: while a pin is running and another fighter is free (on her feet, not the pinned fighter's ally), the chance each beat that the director is told to have her pile on for a double pin.
director._charge_chance_comment: charge_chance: each beat with no direction from you (and no pin running or about to start), the chance the director is pointed at a charge that carries the target into the scenery. At most one of the two big-moment ideas (held stream, charge) is given in a beat. 0 = never suggested.
director._grapple_comment: grapple_chance: each beat with no direction from you (and no pin running or about to start), the chance the director is pointed at one fighter seizing another who is on her feet and throwing her into the scenery or slamming her down. It shares the one big-moment roll with the held stream and the charge, so at most one of the three is suggested in a beat. 0 = never suggested (the director may still choose a throw by itself).
director._clinch_comment: clinch_chance: each beat with no direction from you (and no pin running or about to start), the chance the director is pointed at a GRAPPLE: one fighter seizing another who is on her feet, keeping hold, and working her over at point-blank (short blows, a bite, a held stream) in the same beat and the next. chain_chance: the same for a CHAIN, two or three attacks by one fighter in one beat, each leading into the next. Both share the one big-moment roll with the held stream, the charge and the throw, so at most one of the five is suggested in a beat, and the director may still decline. 0 = never suggested (your own /grapple and joined commands still work).
director._big_moment_overdue_comment: big_moment_overdue: when this many beats have gone by with no big moment at all (no held stream, charge into the scenery, throw or slam, grapple, or chain), one is suggested for certain on the next open beat, and more firmly, so a fight of ordinary length has at least two or three. 0 = never forced. Change the five chances and this number together with /bigmoments.
director._injured_focus_comment: For /focus injured: a part counts as hurt from min_damage % up. Hurt parts are chosen most (more, the worse they are), the parts right around them at around_weight. If one side of the body (left or right) has at least side_damage % in total and side_ratio times the other side, that whole side is in play at side_weight.
director._pin_shape_comment: pin_shape_weights: when there is an opening for a pin, the director is handed one way to build it, so pins don't all look alike (never the same shape twice running). The numbers say how often each is suggested compared with the others; 0 = never. throat_bite = jaws on the throat, weight on the chest. trapped_arm = jaws pinning a paw or forearm to the stone while a forepaw or forearm bars the throat. tail_choke = tails or coils looped round the neck, paws on the shoulders (only fighters whose tail can coil). twisted_arm = an arm wrenched out straight and pinned. leg_tangle = both legs trapped. lifted_leg = one leg hooked and hauled up off the ground, folded back (kept rare). coil_crush = constriction as a pin: tails or coils wound round her chest and arms, bearing her down inside them (only fighters whose tail or body can coil; she goes out from the constriction). dunk = held face-down in the shallows, her head pushed under and let up again (only in an arena with shallow water; a choke by water, never drowning). The throat-bite ideas above now also offer chokes with other limbs and jaws clamped on a limb. Change live with /pinshape.
director._reposition_comment: The director may roll a downed fighter over (or onto her back, front, side) or haul her up off the ground before an attack or during a pin. reposition_cooldown = beats before the same fighter can be moved again (your /roll ignores it).
director._manhandle_comment: manhandle_cooldown: beats a fighter must wait after throwing, slamming or dragging someone before she may do another (the director's 'throw', 'slam' and 'drag' actions). 0 = no wait (the default since build 100); 3 was build 99's. Your own /throw, /slam and /drag commands ignore it. Their energy costs are under energy.costs.
director._reposition_chance_comment: reposition_chance: each beat that an opponent is lying on the ground, the chance the director is pointed at moving her first: rolling her over to reach the other side of her, sitting her up, lifting her off the ground for a slam or a throw, or dragging her onto her feet. It is only a suggestion. 0 = never suggested (the director can still choose it).
director._manipulate_comment: manipulate (since build 328): two more ways for the director to handle a fighter who is down or in her own grip, to get at something: turn her head (her jaw or head taken and wrenched up and aside: her throat and the side of her neck open for 2 beats, blows and grips there x open_mult, and she cannot block them) and pull her arm away (the arm she guards with dragged away: no guarding or blocking this beat). They are offered among the reposition ideas (reposition_chance, raised to 0.2 in build 328 so she is handled and moved more often). She may fight it off like any handling (down.resist_handling).
director._autofight_comment: /autofight stops a fight that still has no winner after this many beats and moves on to the next one.
director._story_state_comment: story_state: the director is also told where the fight stands as a story (who is ahead, who is pressing, how it sits with each of them), so its choices fit: it changes no rule and no number.
director._chain_comment: chain: a chain of attacks in one beat has no fixed length either. Before the third link and every later one the engine rolls whether the chain ends there: break_start for link 3, plus break_step for each link after it, raised when the attacker is tired or the defender still fresh and lowered the other way. It ends with her dodging that link (and maybe countering) or, when she cannot dodge where she is, with the attacker having nothing left to follow with. hard_cap: a distant limit on links in one beat (0 = none).
director._target_variety_comment: target_variety: with no /focus set, the chance that a blow aimed at a region this attacker has just been hitting is moved to a part she has left alone (the less hurt, the likelier), and the chance per beat that the director is reminded what has not been touched yet. 0 = off.
director._weak_spot_comment: weak_spot_chance: with no /focus set, the chance per beat that the director is pointed at one of the opponent's weak spots (a soft part like the throat, or one already worn down), so weak spots are gone for sometimes but not all the time. 0 = never; /focus vulnerable or /focus injured makes them the aim.
director._face_comment: face_chance (since build 308): the chance per beat, when no other target idea ran, that the director is reminded the opponent has a face (her Muzzle, Nose, Snout or Beak) as well as a Head; left alone it picks Head, Neck and Chest and almost never the face. 0 = never.
director._weak_spot_reach: weak-spot hints pick the softest parts, a little less often the ones hard to reach (moves.aim: a throat, an ear, an eye): 0 = reach doesn't count, 1 = it counts fully
director._weak_spot_repeat_comment: weak_spot_repeat: of those nudges, the share meant for a run of blows (a pummel, a combo, a chain, a grapple worked at): one weak spot hit again and again, a group of parts worked together (one side's foreleg top to bottom, the ribs), or a few weak spots in turn.
director._weak_spot_menu: a WEAK SPOTS hint (the plain kind, not a worked run) offers a short list to choose ONE from, or none: up to badly_hurt parts at 150%+, up to hurt parts between 30% and 150% (picked at random), and up to soft untouched places, shuffled. Spreads the blows over what is hurt instead of always the worst of it.
director._flight_comment: flight_chance: each beat, the chance the director is reminded that a winged fighter on the ground could take off (x1.5 when her opponent has nothing that reaches the air). air_attack_chance: for one already in the air, the chance she is pointed at a dive or a carry (Sky Drop). 0 = never.
director._grudge_comment: grudge_chance: per beat, a PAYBACK idea for a fighter with a wrecked part (go for the same place on the one who did it). drag_to_pin_chance: per beat, when someone is down and not pinned, the idea to drag her to a wall or the water and pin her there next.
director._move_variety_comment: move_variety: the chance each beat that the director is shown the moves each fighter hasn't used yet this fight (status and set-up moves included; hold-only moves are left out). 0 = off.

_teams_comment: Teams set with /team: fighter -> team name. Fighters who share a team never attack each other and win together, in every fight. Empty = everyone fights alone.
