(Temporary alliances are made during a fight with /ally and are not kept here.) worn_after: an attack a fighter has thrown this many times among the last twenty attacks is named to the director as worn out every beat (0 = off), with a push toward an improvised technique of her own body or a use of the scenery instead.

console._comment: How the text looks on screen. styled_text: the stat blocks mark headings with **two asterisks** and the story marks thoughts with *one*; Spyder's console (and most terminals) don't understand those marks, so with styled_text on the program turns them into real bold and italic. auto = on in Spyder, Jupyter, and terminals; on / off force it. bold_color: an optional colour for the bold parts (yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue, white, or empty for none), for consoles that don't draw bold text heavier. /export always keeps the plain asterisks. Change live with /style.
console._layout_comment: layout: how the stat math is laid out. clear (default) = every hit as three labelled rows (damage, resistance, health: each with before -> after and the math that gives it), grouped under what caused it, blocks spaced out, one chance roll per line, no line wider than about 100 characters, every beat in full. tight = one unlabelled row per hit, everything packed (needs a wide window). classic = the long Before / Calculations / After blocks. Change live with /layout.
console._timing_comment: timing: after each beat, one line says how long it took, how fast the model wrote and read, and what had to be written again. /timing shows the averages by narrator model; /timing off hides the line.
console._speed_check_comment: speed_check (since build 286): after a beat, Ollama is asked how much of the narrator model sits on the graphics card. When warn_from or more of it is running in system memory instead (which alone can make a beat several times slower, without anything being written differently), it says so once, and again only if it gets worse, with what to do: close other programs using the card, OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 so Ollama's working memory for the notes is smaller, or a slightly smaller version of the same model. enabled false = no check.
console._italic_colors_comment: thought_color / sound_color: the story's italics are a fighter's thoughts or a sound she makes written out (*Nngh*). Spyder's console doesn't slant text, so each also gets a colour to stand out (yellow, cyan, green, magenta, red, blue, white, or empty for none). /set console.thought_color green

pinfall._comment: Only used by the quick /pin three-count command. Story pins (story_prompt.txt) are holds plus the director eliminating the loser.

body_zones._comment: Groups of body parts for /focus (also: injured or weakened = what is already hurt). Each zone lists body regions (head, neck, shoulder, chest, belly, back_up, back_low, fore_up, fore_low, hind_up, hind_low, tail) and/or words found in part names. A fighter without a zone (a serpent has no legs) is simply open everywhere.

vulnerable._comment: the soft, weak places: throat and neck, eyes and nose, belly, the joints

down._variety_comment: How a fall ends. slump_sitting: thrown or knocked into something upright (a wall, boulder, stalagmite, pillar), the chance she ends SITTING slumped against it instead of lying at its foot. sit_down: a plain knockdown, the chance she is sat down hard on her haunches instead of laid flat. roll_through: a THROWN or LAUNCHED fighter, the chance at full strength that she rolls through the landing and comes up on her feet (she still takes every impact; the chance shrinks as she weakens; never from your own commands). resist_handling: a fighter lying on the ground, the chance at full strength that she fights off being rolled, hauled up, thrown or dragged when the DIRECTOR chooses it (shrinks as she weakens; your commands always work). Set any of them to 0 to turn that outcome off. keep_feet (since build 243): a blow the DIRECTOR says knocks her down ('knocked down'; not a throw, a launch, a crash into the scenery or a move that knocks down by itself) may leave her staggering but still standing. The chance comes from her strength left: full at full health, half at half, empty at 0% and below (in between, a straight line), x light_mult for a blow that takes almost nothing from her, falling to x big_mult for one that takes big_blow_pct % of her full health or more, never above max. So even badly hurt she goes down to a solid blow only most of the time (with these numbers about 75%, near 90% to a huge one). Your own commands always knock her down. enabled false = the director's knockdowns always happen, as before.
down._spring_up_comment: spring_up: a fighter knocked or thrown down may come straight back up on her feet in the same moment (she still takes every impact). The chance rises from 0 at `from` % strength to `max` at full strength, so a fresh fighter is rarely left lying for an opponent to pin; roll_through (x her strength share) is used when it is higher.
down._tumble_comment: tumble_chance: a fighter who is thrown or launched (not slammed, not dragged) doesn't always stop where she lands: this often she TUMBLES ON across the ground (a light scrape on 2-3 more parts) and, tumble_into of those times, fetches up against something in the arena (a solid knock on 1-2 parts; water, snow or sand is a light one; a hazard does what it does). A fighter who tumbles doesn't roll through to her feet. 0 = never. Rolled for the director's throws and launches; in your own commands add 'tumble' as the last surface (/throw Ripples "the cave wall; tumble"). Change live with /tumble.

grapple._comment: A GRAPPLE (director action "grapple", your /grapple): one fighter seizes another and keeps hold of her, both on their feet. While the grab lasts neither can dodge the other; the one holding can throw the same close move again and again (a pummel: up to pummel_max blows in a beat, each at pummel_power of one full blow, each after the first costing energy_per_extra_hit), hold a stream on her at no distance, or throw or slam her with no chance of the grab being slipped. The held fighter can hit back and rolls to wrench free every beat (the usual hold-break roll times holds.break.grab_mult). The grab itself costs energy.costs.grapple and squeezes only lightly. How often the director is pointed at one: director.clinch_chance.
grapple._pummel_comment: A pummel (the same close move thrown again and again inside a grab) has no fixed length: after the second blow every further one may be the last. The chance that it ends starts at pummel_end_start and grows by pummel_end_step per blow; a tired attacker ends it sooner and a fresh defender spoils it sooner (both fighters' strength count), and it also ends when the attacker runs out of breath. pummel_hard_cap is a distant limit (0 = none). pummel_max: a fixed limit if you want one (0 = none; 4 was the old rule). A pummel is usually one-sided: the held fighter only takes it. pummel_answer_chance: of the pummels she manages to spoil (about half of them), how often she does it by landing a short blow of her own on the one working on her (0.5 = about one pummel in four is answered; 0 = never).
grapple._pummel_in_pin_comment: pummel_in_pin: whether the director may rain a pummel down on a fighter she has PINNED (false by default: a pin is a pin; pummels are for a grab, a fighter who is down, or one pressed against the scenery). Your own commands can always do it.

frenzy._comment: Now and then (chance per pummel; ground_chance on someone lying on the ground) a pummel turns into a frenzy: the chance to end after each blow is x end_mult, each extra blow costs energy x energy_mult, and the blows keep going back to the same spot (stay_chance) or the one right beside it. health.soft_cap still keeps the health loss of one beat in bounds; the parts take it all. ground_end_mult: above 1, a pummel on someone lying on the ground ends sooner (1 = as long as any other).

variety._comment: HOW an outcome plays out once the dice have decided WHAT happens. Each entry is a set of ways with weights (compared with the others in the same set); the engine picks one each time and tells the narrator, so the story varies without ever contradicting the result. Raise a weight to see that way more often; 0 removes it. /variety shows and changes them. charge_stands: a fighter who keeps her feet after being charged into the scenery. charge_falls: one who crumples (lying three ways, or sitting against it). dodge: how an attack is avoided. hold_break: how a hold is broken. hold_strain: how a held fighter fights a grip that stays on. struggle: what a pinned fighter tries. getup_fail / getup_rise: how a try at getting up fails, and how she finally rises. bite_rock: how a bite rocks a fighter who is standing free (dragged toward the biter, shaken on the spot, yanked off her line, or jerked as she pulls free).

scene._comment: The arena. current: which scene from scenes.json a run starts in (the start-of-run question and /scene set it). ask_at_start: ask which scene every time the program starts. events: whether the place does things by itself (a stalactite falls, a wave sweeps the deck). event_chance: the chance per beat that it does (0 = never; /hazards chance <n> changes it). event_gap: beats that must pass between two events. event_from_beat: no events before this beat. Events never happen while a pin or a hold is on. /hazard <name> [fighter] makes one happen.

variants._comment: Which version of a fighter a new fight uses, for fighters that have a "variants" section in fighters.json. "original" = the entry as it is written. Ripples: "sleek" has no flotation sac (a bare throat instead; her tells and body parts are written around that). Change with /variant Ripples original | sleek; it takes effect in the next fight.

learning._comment: Fighters learn during a fight. A fighter who has broken out of a pin of the same shape before (the same body regions pressed) escapes it more easily: x (1 + pin_escape_per_time per escape), at most pin_escape_cap. A move that has landed on her twice or more is one she has learned to read: her dodge chance against THAT attacker's move x (1 + dodge_per_hit per hit after the first), at most dodge_cap. enabled false = off.

wary._comment: A move that left one of her parts at at_damage or worse makes her wary of it: she dodges it more (dodge_mult), but jumps at a feint of it more (feint_mult).

arena._comment: How the arena takes part. water_dodge: dodge chance in the water, for a Water type (native_) and anyone else (other_), in shallow water and deep water (where the director last placed her: 'in the shallow pool', 'in the deep channel'). slip_chance: a fighter who dodges on slick footing (algae, wet stone, ice, mud, the shallows) may go down as she does it (a Water type in the water slips x slip_native_mult as often). shake_chance: a charge that slams her into a wall, a stalagmite, a pillar, a tree... may shake loose whatever the arena drops (its 'falls' event: a stalactite, a branch, debris), onto her, at the end of the beat.

flight._comment: Winged fighters (a body with Wing parts). 'take off' (a reposition on her own action) puts her in the air for airborne_beats; ground fighters' close moves can't reach her there; her close moves become dives (dive_mult). After a dive she climbs back up (climb_chance) or lands; the one she dove at may catch her and drag her down (counter_grab). A wing at ground_at% damage brings her down. Carry moves drop the defender from one of drop_heights.
flight._vigour_comment: vigour: a winged fighter who is still strong flies a lot. By her strength (healthy: at or above healthy_at % of her full strength; fair: at or above fair_at; low: below): takeoff_mult multiplies director.flight_chance (how often the director is told she could take off, and how firmly), extra_beats adds to airborne_beats each time she goes up, climb_mult multiplies climb_chance after a dive. enabled false = as before.
flight._speed_comment: speed: every dive she lands and climbs back up from builds speed (one pass, up to max_passes): each pass makes her next dive land per_pass harder (x(1 + per_pass x passes) on top of dive_mult). Taking off again or coming down starts it over. enabled false = off.
flight._strafe_comment: strafe: after a dive that lands, as she climbs away, chance (x vigour strafe_mult by her strength) that her speed carries her round for a second, quicker pass: one more blow at power x the dive's power on another part, costing energy. enabled false = off.
flight._dive_counter_comment: dive_counter: a dive at a fighter on the ground can be answered as it goes past. on_dodge: after she sidesteps the dive, the chance she strikes the flyer as it streaks by (in place of the usual evasion.counter_chance); on_hit: the chance she takes the dive and still gets a blow in as it passes. momentum: the flyer's own speed adds to that blow.
flight._air_pass_comment: air_pass: two flyers both in the air can reach each other with close moves. mult: the speed of the pass in the blow (with flight.speed's passes on top); rake_back: the chance the one struck rakes back as they cross (x her flight.vigour strafe_mult); momentum: that blow's speed.
flight._leap_comment: leap: a fighter on the ground climbs high ground in the arena (a boulder, a tree, a pillar...) and leaps at a flyer with a close move. reach: the chance she gets to her (x 0.5 + 0.5 x her strength share; the flyer can still dodge); mult: the blow's weight; drag_down: the chance she drags the flyer down with her (who lands drag_landing); hit_landing: how hard her own landing on her feet jars her legs; miss_landing: the fall when it falls short (she goes down); energy: what the climb and leap cost.
flight._air_grab_comment: air_grab (on by default, since build 233): two flyers both in the air can grab each other there, if the one grabbing has something to grab with up there (a part matching grip_parts: talons, feet, claws, or the hands, paws and arms some flyers have, like a Charizard): she locks on in the air and, locked together, the two of them tumble down to the ground (the grab then goes on there like any other: a slam, a hold, a pin). enabled false: no grabbing anyone in the air; she must come down first.
flight._knock_from_air_comment: knock_from_air: a blow that lands on a fighter in the air may knock her out of the sky: base + per_damage x the damage it did + per_wing_damage x her worse wing's damage, at most max. She falls and lands.

knock_from_air._health_mult: the chance above x this by her overall strength: at full strength, at half, and with nothing left (eased between): a strong flyer rides out blows that bring a worn one down
knock_from_air._spread_share: per_damage counts her worst hit in full and every other part the blow struck at this share: a gust or a blast over her whole body does not bring her down like one crushing blow

flight._air_recover_comment: air_recover: a flyer a blow would hurl (a move's launch effect: thrown, launched...) may catch herself on her wings instead of falling: by_strength is the chance at full strength, at half and with nothing left (eased between), halved again when her worse wing is at wing_halves_at % damage. A move that always throws (a launch at 100%) can't be ridden out. The blow can still knock her out of the sky as any blow can (knock_from_air). enabled false = a launch always brings her down.
flight._strain_comment: strain: a hurt wing still lifts her, at a cost. Past `from` % damage on her worse wing, taking off costs energy_per_100 x more energy per 100% of damage past it, and every beat she stays up that wing takes power x (its damage / 100) more damage. Only a wing at max_wing % (shredded) can't lift her at all. ground_at is now only where the air's dodge edge has faded away.
flight._strain_caps_comment: energy_max_mult: the take-off never costs more than this x takeoff_energy, however hurt the wing. power_cap_at: the strain counts the wing's damage only up to this %, so it stops snowballing. max_wing_grounds: true = a wing at max_wing % can't lift her at all (off: a flyer can always try).
flight._weak_takeoff_comment: weak_takeoff: below `below` % of her full strength, taking off is a roll she often loses: at_below is the chance just under that, at_zero with nothing left (eased between). The energy is spent either way.
flight._dodge_comment: In the air her dodge rests on her wings, not her legs: chance x 1/(1 + wing damage/wing_per) (the worse wing counts double) x 1/(1 + flight-muscle damage/body_per) (shoulders, chest, belly, back) x 1/(1 + head and neck damage/head_per). The airborne_dodge_mult edge fades with the worse wing's damage and is gone at ground_at.
flight._carry_comment: carry: any winged fighter in the air with talons, feet or hands can seize one on the ground with a close strike (the director's "carry") and haul her up: chance x (0.5 + 0.5 x her strength) x 1/(1 + worse wing damage/wing_per) x (the lighter the load, the likelier: 0.75 against a fighter at full strength, up to 1 as she weakens), at most 0.95; costs energy. She is dropped from one of drop_heights. fall_strikes: how many strikes in the same chain can catch her on the way down beyond the first, by the drop's severity.
flight._spike_comment: spike: a fighter falling (dropped from a carry, or launched by a chain) struck from ABOVE by one in the air with a dive, a charge or a held stream is driven straight into the ground: the blow takes mult (in place of the dive's edge; caught helpless in the air still applies), and her landing goes severity_bump steps harder than it would have been (at least heavy, at most brutal) with landing_force x its power, and she doesn't tumble on. A charge or a held stream from above always spikes; a close blow from above does on close_chance (the last one: a slash with more still to come in the chain is just a slash on the way down).

stances._comment: Moves with "target": "self" and a "stance": protect (the next attack on her stops against it; used again straight away it holds less often: repeat_mult per repeat), counter (the next close blow that lands is sent back at reflect_mult, spread over two front parts) or mirror (the same for blasts, beams and streams).

weather._comment: Moves with "target": "self" and a "weather": rain, sun or hail. It lasts beats; type_mult changes move power by type; hail chips every fighter who isn't immune each beat.

summary._comment: The end-of-fight summary (printed under the injury report, /summary, and given to the narrator for the aftermath). It only reads what happened; it changes nothing in the fight.

fight_length._comment: Presets for /length: about how many beats a fight runs. Each sets health.loss_per_damage_point to base x health_loss and damage.resistance_scale to base x wear: fighters lose health and wear down faster, so a pin wins sooner (pin success follows her remaining health). Pin openings and escapes are not changed. From build 182 the shorter presets speed up health loss and slow wear (how fast a part softens) to 0.7, so a fight is short without every blow piling onto the same few ruined parts. Older measurements: over 100 simulated fights each (Nocturne vs Ripples, lakeside forest; build 146's balance: fewer wild swings, Nocturne vs Ripples closer to even).

30._measured: 28 beats, 0.4 devastated parts per fighter (build 183: Glacia vs Cinder and Nocturne vs Ripples, 40 fights each, /scale 3)

35._measured: 32 beats, 0.7 devastated parts per fighter (build 183: Glacia vs Cinder and Nocturne vs Ripples, 40 fights each, /scale 3)

40._measured: 38 beats, 0.7 devastated parts per fighter (build 183: Glacia vs Cinder and Nocturne vs Ripples, 40 fights each, /scale 3)

45._measured: 44 beats, 0.8 devastated parts per fighter (build 183: Glacia vs Cinder and Nocturne vs Ripples, 40 fights each, /scale 3)

50._measured: 50 beats, 1.1 devastated parts per fighter (build 183: Glacia vs Cinder and Nocturne vs Ripples, 40 fights each, /scale 3)

submissions._comment: Submission holds: wrestling holds that WRENCH (a camel clutch, a crossface, a Boston crab, an armbar, a leg lock, a tail crank, a limb wrench). They do damage every beat, harder each beat, and are NOT pins (no clock, no pass-out). An opening is rolled each beat on a fighter who is down and not pinned or held (chance, x weak_mult under half strength), max_per_fight a fight at most (0 = no cap; the chance is tuned for about one a fight). power / second_power: the main grips and the bracing ones; ramp / second_ramp: how much harder each beat. max_beats: after that the holder lets it go. Breaking out: the plain-hold chance x break_mult, growing by grow per beat it has been on (up to max_break), unless she is STUCK (under stuck_below % strength, or a gripped part at stuck_damage %+): then it doesn't grow (x stuck_mult), a pin opening on her is always there, and the holder is pointed at letting go into a pin or hurting her another way. The one held can't get up while it's on, and blows on her land x moves.vulnerable.submission.
submissions._from_ground_comment: from_ground (since build 243): a fighter who is down herself may still lock a submission on someone who is down too (she rolls into it, crawls onto her, hooks her from where she lies), and while she works it she stays down rather than rolling to get up. Before, nobody on the ground could start one, and in a submission match where both were often down the fight could run on for hundreds of beats. match_only (on by default): only in a submission match (finish.submission.enabled). enabled false = she has to be on her feet to lock one.
submissions._serpent_holds_comment: serpent_holds (since build 337): twelve holds made for serpents. On a serpent (anyone on one): neck ride (astride or along her neck behind the head, squeezing), serpent tail crank (sitting on her, her tail cranked back against its curve), crest pull (paws knotted in her head fins, hauling her head back), serpent crab (her long body bowed backward over itself), jaw clamp (her jaw held shut and her head twisted), tail wring (her own tail or tails wound round the end of the serpent's, wringing it), belly press (knees or forepaws grinding into her soft upturned belly). Serpent on serpent: coil lock, neck wrap. A serpent on anyone with limbs: leg bind, arm wrap, neck loop. So a Buizel on a downed Milotic has 6-8 holds to choose from (3-4 before), and a Milotic on a Buizel 5 (2 before). false = without them.
submissions._invented_fit_comment: invented_fit (since build 258): a hold of the director's own invention that is named for a part of the body (a knee lock, a heel hook, an armbar, a wrist lock, a kimura, a choke, a tail crank...) has to grip that part: one of its grips on her leg, her arm or shoulder, her neck or head, or her tail. Otherwise it is refused and the director tries again (a standing knee lock on her left shoulder in the build-254 Ripples vs Nocturne log). false = the name is not checked.
submissions._match_comment: match (since build 244; only in a submission match, finish.submission.enabled): submissions start more often there. standing: an opening can come while she is ON HER FEET too, not only when she is down; the holder takes her down into the hold (a tackle, a sweep, a leg hooked out: told in the story) and locks it where she lands. Its chance each beat is standing_base, + per_100_worn for every 100% damage on her worst-hurt part (one that can still make her tap, in a several-tap match; up to 3 of those), never above standing_max: with these numbers about 4% a beat while she is fresh, 8% with a part at 100%, 16% with one at 300%. A fighter who is down herself can't take down one on her feet. The openings while she is down: chance (x weak_mult under half strength), and since build 249 x down_mult in a submission match, never above down_max: down on the ground is where a hold most often starts. late (since build 247): the longer the match runs, the more they go for the hold: past `after` beats, the chance of an opening on her feet rises by per_10 for every 10 beats more, and its ceiling goes up to late.max (with these numbers +3% at beat 40, +9% at beat 60). late.enabled false = no rise. standing false or enabled false = openings only while she is down.
submissions._upright_comment: upright (since build 245): some submissions are put on a fighter still UPRIGHT, on her feet or sitting up (a full nelson, a standing sleeper, a bear hug, a hammerlock, a side headlock, a guillotine, a cobra clutch, an abdominal stretch, a standing armbar or wrist lock, an octopus hold, a rear chinlock; for four-legged holders a scruff hold, a foreleg bite, a shoulder ride, a hind leg hook; an upright coil for serpents, a talon shoulder clamp for birds), and the director may invent its own with "upright": true. Held on her upright, each beat it may BEAR HER DOWN with the grip kept on: chance base, from its second beat on her (never the beat it is locked), + per_beat for every beat after that, + weak x how much of her strength is gone, never above max. She goes down a STAGE at a time (stages, in order; each a name, a posture and what the story is told: posture standing = still on her feet, sagging, off balance a beat; knees = down on her knees, sitting up; flat = lying on the ground. Add, remove or reorder them as you like; she starts at the first stage below where she is, so a fighter sitting up in the hold starts from the knees stage). skip of the time a drop takes two stages at once. Each drop is its own roll, so a hold usually takes her down over a few beats. readjust of the time the holder has to shift her grip as she goes: the grips lose readjust_mult of their pressure and a beat of their build, but stay on. In a submission match, an opening on her feet (match.standing) offers these as they are, and takes her down into any other hold. enabled false = no upright holds: every submission needs her on the ground. Since build 249: plain_holds: any other grip on her while she is up (jaws on her knee, tails round her hip; not a grab chest to chest, not a pin) can bear her down the same way, stage by stage. leg: added to the chance when a grip is on a leg she stands on (hip, thigh, knee, foot; a four-legged fighter's forelegs too); per_100_worn: added for every 100% damage on the worst gripped part (up to 3). supporting: holds that carry her weight (lifting her, riding her on the holder's shoulders): their chance is multiplied by support_mult, since the holder holds her up. held_getup: taken off her get-up roll while a grip is on her leg (rising on a leg held down is much harder). standing_tap_mult: her chance to tap while still on her own feet is multiplied by this (she has her legs to fight it with: most holds bear her down before she gives in; a supporting hold isn't damped). pick_share: on her feet, the share of openings that offer a hold keeping her standing; the rest take her down into a hold on the ground.

stages.name: sagging
stages.says: her legs start to go under it: she sags, knees bending, still on her feet and fighting to stay there

stages.name: on her knees
stages.says: her legs give and she sinks to her knees, sitting back on her heels, still locked in it

stages.name: flat
stages.says: she is forced all the way down, flat on the ground, the hold riding her down

submissions._small_joints_comment: small_joints: a submission whose hardest grip is on a wrist or an ankle (a paw, a hand, a foot, a talon) is harder to lock in and easier to get out of, so these quick, sharp holds don't finish a fit fighter too easily. set_chance = how often it locks when she goes for it, plus set_hurt x the health the defender has lost (a worn-down fighter is easier to catch); when it doesn't, she gets her hands on it and it slips out (no hold, no damage, the opening spent). escape_mult = her break-free chance in one that did lock, multiplied. enabled false: they lock and hold like any other.
submissions._escape_comment: escape: breaking out of a submission goes by her OWN health, as with a pin: points are [health %, chance a beat] in straight lines between them (flat past the ends), so a strong fighter gets out of most holds before they become a pin (about two in three from full health, never certain) and a badly hurt one rarely does. The chance is then a little higher when the holder is hurt (holder_hurt: +50% against a holder at nothing) or the grip is light (grip_weight: how much the grip's power counts; 0 = not at all), changed by statuses (wet fur, paralysis, adrenaline), grows by grow per beat it has been on (this grow, not the submission's own; not when she is stuck), at most max_break, and never below floor however hurt she is. match_holds: in a submission match (finish.submission) every hold that hurts (not a grab) is broken this way too, since any of them can make her tap. enabled false: the old chance (the plain-hold chance x break_mult), which barely changes with her health.
submissions._grind_comment: grind: a submission's wrench works a part down rather than smashing it: on a part still sound it does from_mult of the usual damage, rising to to_mult on a part worn to nothing, and it wears the part's toughness wear_mult times as fast as a blow of the same power. So a hold hurts little at first and more every beat it stays on, and a second hold on a limb already worked bites far harder. enabled false: a submission hurts like any grip.
submissions._damage_cap_comment: damage_cap: a submission's wrench never uses more than these multipliers on a worn part, however ruined it is: mult (damage) and health_mult (health). Looser than pin.pressure_cap (0.45 / 1.0): a wrench hurts more than being held down, but it can't run away with the numbers. Once it becomes a pin, the pin's own cap applies. enabled false = no cap.
submissions._becomes_pin_after_comment: becomes_pin_after: a submission still on after this many beats becomes a PIN (the pin clock and pass-out start) without easing off: its grips go on wrenching at full power and keep building, capped like any pin's presses (pin.pressure_cap). 0 = never.
submissions._variety_comment: Holds: no cap on any of them. The director is shown the holds used so far as a nudge toward new ones, and may INVENT a submission of its own (a name, the parts it grips, what grips each): the engine checks every grip against both bodies (the parts must be hers, the grip must use a part the holder has). The list includes ones a Pokemon's body makes possible (a tail-bound knee crank or a tail strangle for a fighter with tails, a jaw lock), and ones that use the scenery: a knee levered back over a root or a ridge of rough ground, an arm wrenched round whatever she lies against.

tactics._comment: Setups and payoffs. The engine notices when a fighter has set something up (her opponent soaked while she has lightning; the rain called by a fighter with water moves; the sun by one with fire) and watches for the payoff for payoff_beats beats. The director gets a PAYOFF nudge while one is waiting, and now and then (idea_chance) an idea for a setup or a read (a Mirror Coat, a Protect or a Counter to go round). The narrator is told when a beat is a setup (the plan shows in a thought) and when it is the payoff (it was planned, and the other realises). The screen shows both (🧠).

play._comment: Playing as fighters (/play). free_pins: true = a fighter you play may always try to pin (like a typed direction); false = she gets the same dice-rolled openings as everyone (shown to you before you choose). ai_answers: true = after your moves, each fighter the director runs answers with an action of her own every beat; false = only when the moment calls for it.
play._dice_comment: dice (/play dice): fair = the dice decide, /commands can still force outcomes; strict = at the mercy of the dice (no forcing commands, no /undo, typed directions don't open pins); free = the dice are off for the fighters you play (their attacks land, openings always there, first-try get-ups, any pin or hold on them breaks).

_numbness_comment: numbness: a devastated part (at_damage 300%+) that takes a hard blow (hard_at 40%+ of damage before the part curve) goes NUMB chance 30% of the time, for 1-3 beats: the pain cuts out, a dead, strange heaviness and shock instead, and blows there land as a dull jolt and a cold rush of shock. Then it wears off and the pain floods back, horribly. It can't go numb again for `cooldown` beats. With this on, the old permanent 'numb with shock' level at 1000%+ is not used.
